title: Accenture may exit China after unsolicited offer as investors debate its AI future
text:
Accenture is reportedly exploring a potential $1.5 billion sale of its operations in China. According to a report in Financial Times, 'Chinese operations' sale talks come as the world’s largest publicly traded IT consultancy Accenture sharpens its focus on faster-growing markets and seeks to reassure investors over its strategy in the artificial intelligence era. The Dublin-headquartered company has enlisted JPMorgan to conduct a strategic review of the unit following unsolicited approaches over the past year, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The entire Greater China division, which encompasses mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, could command a valuation of up to $1.5 billion. People close to the discussions noted that any formal process is anticipated to attract interest from private equity companies alongside a select group of strategic suitors. Accenture may choose to maintain a meaningful minority holding to preserve continuity for existing multinational and domestic clients, though discussions remain preliminary and may not result in a final transaction.

Accenture stock has seen ups and down this year

The strategic deliberations coincide with broader volatility for Accenture's stock, as markets evaluate whether consultancy giants will benefit from companies adoption artificial intelligence or suffer as clients automate internal workflows previously handled by external contractors. Meanwhile, tightening data security and cross-border regulatory scrutiny in Beijing has prompted several Western advisory firms, including McKinsey, to scale back their Chinese footprints, segregate technology infrastructure, and navigate hurdles to international integration.

How billions from 'China office' sale may help

The potential divestment would provide fresh capital as Accenture positions itself for long-term artificial intelligence deployment. Speaking at a recent investor gathering, chief financial officer Angie Park noted that the firm retains an established history of exiting businesses, offerings, and regional operations that fall short of strategic or return targets. Management reiterated plans to deploy efficiency gains into customer pricing and targeted acquisitions, while upholding shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases. The move follows long-range guidance outlined by the consultancy, in which it projected subdued top-line expansion across the next two years ahead of an expected acceleration toward the end of the decade driven by enterprise AI adoption. Wall Street responded favorably to the outlook and recent earnings outperformance, with analysts pointing to expanding opportunities across its $3tn addressable market as the consultancy recalibrates its global footprint.

End of Article

title: ‘No accountability’: Ex-cricketer seeks clarity over Shami’s continued omission
text:
Mohammed Shami (ANI Photo)

Mohammed Shami’s continued omission from India’s plans has raised fresh questions, with former India cricketer Mohammad Kaif calling for greater transparency from the selectors following the announcement of the squad for the upcoming series in New Zealand. The BCCI announced India’s squads earlier this week for the New Zealand tour, which includes two Tests, five ODIs and five T20Is. However, the absence of the experienced fast bowler from the squad has drawn criticism, particularly in view of his domestic performances and past contributions to the national team. Kaif believes the selectors owe Shami an explanation, given the pacer’s achievements and his crucial role in India’s run to the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Shami finished that tournament as the leading wicket-taker, claiming 24 wickets in just seven matches. “No questions are asked, no BCCI selector explains the decisions, there’s no accountability. You’ve to keep transparency. This is about Mohammed Shami – the player of the 2023 world cup. If he wasn’t there, India would not have reached the final. When Hardik Pandya got injured, Shami came in and didn’t make you feel the absence of a sixth bowler. If Shami wasn’t there, India would’ve been searching for a sixth bowling option. Rohit Sharma took India to the final with five bowlers because Shami was the backup," Kaif said on Cricbuzz. The former India batter also pointed to Shami’s performances in domestic cricket, arguing that the pacer has continued to make a case for himself despite being away from the international setup. “Shami took 22-23 wickets in Indian conditions. So, I feel there has to be some transparency why the decision has been taken. He’s doing everything – playing first-class cricket, Ranji Trophy, taking wickets," he added. Shami last represented India in March 2025 during the Champions Trophy triumph. His most recent Test appearance, meanwhile, came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in June 2023. The fast bowler has since been attempting to regain his place through domestic cricket following an extended absence from the longest format. Concerns over his match fitness have reportedly been a key factor behind the selectors' reluctance to include him in the Test squad, with questions remaining over his ability to withstand the demands of red-ball cricket. Shami has also been bowling short spells in domestic matches, a factor cited in discussions over his omission. Kaif, however, questioned whether that should be a decisive consideration, pointing to the workload management followed for India’s pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah. “I heard that he’s (Shami) bowling short spells and so not being picked. Jasprit Bumrah also bowls four-over spells in Test cricket. In England, his workload was being managed and Shubman Gill followed it. title: Congress’s post-truth politics of distrust, undermining democracy: Rajnath Singh
text:
For nearly seven decades, Congress govts retained executive control over appointment of CEC

It is said that often truth is the first casualty of war. This is increasingly becoming true of political contests as well, where post-truth politics is emerging as an important dimension of public discourse. In the post-truth scenario, false propaganda, distorted narratives, and emotional appeals devoid of logic often take precedence over objective facts and verifiable evidence. And, reasoned debate gives way to demagoguery. Once largely a subject of academic debates, post-truth has now become a feature of everyday politics. Misinformation campaigns designed to gaslight are increasingly used to not only sway public opinion but also discredit democratic institutions. Allegations are repeated and amplified even when the evidence to substantiate them is conspicuously absent. In this, truth seems to be not merely the first casualty, but it risks becoming the final casualty as well. India’s political discourse is not immune to this post-truth phenomenon. Increasingly, sections of the opposition parties appear to be manufacturing outrage, peddling propaganda and weaponising misinformation to spread anarchy, placing avaricious political goals above national interests. The article does not aim a jeremiad against the opposition nor a claim that constitutional institutions are beyond criticism. Dissent is the lifeblood of democracy. What it is not is a licence to peddle falsehoods. Disagreement is necessary for better policymaking. What it is not is a pass for vindictive and sustained assault on public trust through allegations that crumble under factual scrutiny. The purpose, therefore, is to challenge these falsehoods and restore public trust in constitutional institutions, which has been eroded by the cynical politics of manufactured distrust. This becomes particularly significant when we examine how electoral institutions and processes have been attacked by certain sections of opposition to hide the fact that people are rejecting them again and again. Three issues, in particular, stand out: the recurring allegations of manipulation of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), the controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and unscrupulous attempts to discredit the Election Commission of India (ECI). First things first, EVMs have repeatedly been subjected to allegations of manipulation by the opposition. The Supreme Court has examined such challenges on multiple occasions. Finally, in 2024, in its ‘Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India’, the Supreme Court put to rest all doubts and rejected demands for a return to paper ballots. The Supreme Court observed that repeated challenges based on suspicion and doubt, without cogent material or data, were “execrable and undesirable”. title: City halls torched, shops looted: France in shock after violent protest - videos
text:
Chaos, loot and fire as France burns amidst widespread unrest

France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools escalated into violence, leaving businesses damaged and public buildings in flames. President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against rioters while announcing measures to address public grievances. The scale of the unrest was visible in Paris on Sunday, where shattered shopfronts, broken glass and dislodged cobblestones littered the area around Place de la République. Videos across social media sites also showed damage and looting in other shopping and tourist districts. Authorities estimated that around 5,50,000 people took part in Saturday’s demonstrations, while organisers put the turnout at 8,00,000. The protests were backed by labour unions, student organisations and activists seeking to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 over social injustice.

Macron vows action as arrests mount

In a televised address, Macron acknowledged the public’s “anger” and “shame” over the unrest, while drawing a distinction between peaceful demonstrators and those involved in violence. “Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable,” Macron said. He also condemned what he described as “unrestrained violence” by “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.” Social media has been flooded with viral videos of burning buildings, smashed storefronts and clashes, with users declaring “France has fallen” and warning that the country is on the brink. At least 2,400 people were arrested, according news agency AP. Macron said he had instructed prefects to work with mayors to protect public buildings and businesses, including by banning protests where necessary.

City halls set ablaze, businesses looted

In Limoges, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall on Saturday, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate said “radical troublemakers” had broken in while officials, employees, security personnel and members of the public were inside. “They deliberately set the building on fire. It is an extremely serious and unspeakable act,” Barate said. In Marseille, protesters briefly entered the City Hall lobby, while a group damaged a police station. In Lyon, a fire broke out inside a tourist office. Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire described the damage as “considerable and unprecedented”, while stressing that the capital must remain a place where people can demonstrate and businesses can operate safely.

Political blame and economic concerns

The unrest has also fuelled political tensions ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen criticised Macron’s government, while left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon condemned looting and destru

title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
text:
CJI Surya Kant inaugurates the Ladakh HC bench in Leh Sunday

NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level — an altitude no other HC can ever match. Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, “I am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.” J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein. Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many. Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh. “But a name on a court’s letterhead is not the same as a court on one’s doorstep… The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,” he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani. But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services. “Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court’s compound, but at the litigant’s door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,” he said.

title: Paid to clear records, got fake orders; Indiana staffer charged
text:
A former legal secretary in Indiana is facing 42 felony charges and three misdemeanour charges after a three-year police investigation into alleged forged court orders, missing legal fees and fake criminal record expungements. According to a probable cause affidavit reported by Region News Source, 37-year-old Heather Ann Textor of Lowell was arrested after clients who paid to clear their criminal records allegedly received fake court documents and forged letters from state officials instead. The investigation was led by Sergeant Joe White of the Indiana State Police Organized Crime and Corruption Unit. It began in October 2023, when a resident of Gary hand-delivered a suspected fake expungement petition to state police officers. A check of the records showed that the unique identification number on the man's completion letter belonged to someone else. Court clerks in Lake and Porter counties also confirmed that they had no records matching the case numbers or the man's name listed in the documents. Court records cited by Region News Source state that Textor worked as a legal secretary at the Merrillville law firm Weiss, Schmidgall, and Hires. Investigators believe the alleged scheme took place between November 2019 and October 2025.

Unauthorised diversion of client funds

The police affidavit describes a pattern of suspected financial wrongdoing involving cash, credit cards and mobile payment apps. In one case, a client paid Textor a $1,000 cash retainer in November 2019 and later made additional payments. The law firm's accounting records showed small filing fees, but the $1,000 cash payment did not appear in the company's records. The receipt book linked to the payment was also missing. Textor allegedly used her personal electronic payment accounts to divert money that was meant for the law firm. According to police records: One client provided debit card details for a $375 retainer payment. However, only $24.84 was processed through the firm's official system, while $350.16 was sent directly to Textor's personal PayPal account. Another client made a $1,000 debit card payment. Of that amount, $37.58 went to the firm, while $962.42 was transferred to Textor's PayPal account. A third client paid $850 through Cash App after Textor identified the account as the firm's official business account. Lawyers at Weiss, Schmidgall, and Hires told investigators that the firm had never opened or approved business accounts on PayPal or Cash App. They also said the firm did not accept legal fees through either service.

Serious consequences for clients who trusted the documents

The fake legal filings had serious effects on clients who believed their criminal records had been cleared or their driving privileges restored. In one case reported by Region News Source, a client paid $850 to resolve a driving suspension. Textor told her she would email the court to deal with the matter. title: Trump to redevelop 106-year-old DC golf course, plans 15-month closure
text:
Donald Trump plans a 15-month makeover of Washington’s historic East Potomac Golf Links. (Photo: AP/MSGA)

US President Donald Trump has announced plans to close Washington, DC’s historic East Potomac Golf Links from November 15 for a 15-month redevelopment, despite an ongoing legal challenge over his administration’s plans to transform the public course into a world-class golfing destination. In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump said the Department of the Interior, under Secretary Doug Burgum, had developed the redevelopment plan in collaboration with renowned golf course architect Tom Fazio. The President said the redesigned course would remain open to the public while meeting the standards required to host major international tournaments. Trump announces redevelopment plan with architect Tom Fazio

He said the redesigned course would be accessible to the public while being capable of hosting some of the sport’s biggest tournaments, including the US Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup and the Presidents Cup. “When completed, it will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments such as the U.S. Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup, and the Presidents Cup,” he added. Trump also said the United States Golf Association, PGA of America and PGA Tour had been notified about the proposed course and would have it on their list of venues for major events.

title: Meta’s ‘highest-paid employee’ on message from Zuckerberg that changed his career
text:
Meta AI chief Alexander Wang with CEO Mark Zuckerberg

In April 2025, Alexandr Wang was sitting in a staff meeting at Scale AI, the data-labelling company he co-founded, when his phone pinged. It was a WhatsApp message from Mark Zuckerberg: "Have time for a call?" Wang's first thought, as he tells it now, was simply, "huh, interesting." That call ran for 44 minutes. Within two months, Meta had put $14.3 billion into Scale AI for a 49% stake and brought Wang in to run its AI efforts. Wang and Zuckerberg retold the story together on Cheeky Pint, the podcast hosted by Stripe co-founder John Collison, in an episode recorded around the release of Meta's new Muse Wonder AI model. The timing of that message matters. Meta had released its Llama 4 models on April 4, 2025, to a lukewarm response. Around April 20, Zuckerberg said, he started calling people across the industry for advice on what to do next. Wang was one of them.

Alexandr Wang's memo told Zuckerberg to hire fewer, better people

Two days after the call, Wang sent Zuckerberg a long memo. Zuckerberg described it on Cheeky Pint as Wang laying out what he would do "if I were in your position." The first point was about people, and how few of them Meta needed. "The very first thing is that you don't need a lot of people, and talent density is the thing that matters," Zuckerberg recalled. That idea still shapes Meta Superintelligence Labs. Its core research team numbers under 200, "closer to 100," according to Wang, inside a company of roughly 75,000 employees. The hire raised eyebrows. Wang, now 29, is an MIT dropout who built Scale AI into a key data supplier for the big AI labs, but he had never trained a frontier model. Collison pointed this out on the show. Zuckerberg said he spoke to the heads of research at all the major labs before deciding, and came away sure: "Alex is the guy." What followed was a recruiting sprint Zuckerberg called "supernova." He cleared his calendar for a month or two just to meet researchers. "I don't think either of us slept that much for the first couple of months," he said. Wang also recalled one early meeting that left him uneasy. When he said Meta's first priority should be a strong reasoning model, one of the existing leads asked whether consumers needed one at all. Wang said he called Nat Friedman, now head of Meta's AI products, straight after.

Meta's CFO warned Wang the AI bet had to work

By the end of 2025, the numbers had become enormous. Zuckerberg said Meta was preparing to "write this check for like, I don't know, like $100 billion, $200 billion" before anyone had seen the new models. "I'm like, Alex, are you sure this is going to work?" At an executive gathering in Hawaii, Wang said, CFO Susan Li pulled him aside several times to drive the point home. "If it's good, it's all good. We're great. But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad." Wang admitted that all he had to show at the time was a "vibe report" on research progress and a few plots.

title: Indiana daughter loses will challenge, ordered to pay $22,208 in legal fees
text:
Stacia questioned whether her father had signed the will freely and knowingly. (AI image)

An Indiana woman who challenged her father's decision to leave his entire estate to his fiancee has lost her case and now faces a growing legal bill. According to the court document, Stacia Davis was ordered to pay $22,208.18 in attorney fees after failing to prove that her father's will was invalid. On Wednesday, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld that decision and ordered her to pay additional fees for the appeal. The final amount of those extra charges has yet to be determined. At the centre of the dispute was Larry Davis, who died in 2022 at the age of 79. In a will signed nearly two years before his death, Larry had decided that everything he owned would go to his fiancee, Michelle Tressler. The couple had been living together since 2012. The decision meant his three adult children, Sherry, Scott and Stacia, would receive nothing unless Tressler died before him. She was still alive when Larry died, leaving her entitled to inherit his estate under the will. Stacia questioned whether her father had made that decision freely and with a clear understanding of what he was signing. Her challenge began a lengthy court dispute.

What happened after daughter challenged will?

Following Larry's death in 2022, the court accepted the will and appointed Tressler to manage his estate. Stacia challenged it the following month, claiming her father might not have been mentally capable of making a will and raised allegations of pressure and fraud. The case eventually reached a hearing in February 2025, when the court heard from Stacia, Tressler and two women whose signatures appeared on the will. Both witnesses confirmed that the signatures were genuine. Although neither could remember all the details of the signing, their testimony supported the document's validity. Another document presented during the hearing created problems for Stacia's case. It was an affidavit that appeared to come from one of the witnesses and questioned whether she had witnessed the signing. However, the woman told the court that the signature on the affidavit was not hers. Stacia said the document had arrived unexpectedly by post and that she did not know who had sent it. The lower court nevertheless found the affidavit fraudulent and criticised her decision to continue pursuing the case. The court also found that she had not provided acceptable evidence proving her father was mentally incapable of making the will or that Tressler had forced or improperly influenced his decision.

How did the inheritance dispute turn into a $22,208 bill?

The challenge did not only concern who would inherit Larry's property. It also affected the process of managing what he had left behind. In July 2024, the court removed Tressler from responsibility for the estate after finding delays in its administration. Attorney Robert W. York was appointed to take over as special administrator. title: US: Immigration dept returns Indian national to Oregon jail to face manslaughter trial
text:
Indian national returned to US Oregon jail over crash that killed two newlyweds

US authorities have transferred 32-year-old Indian national Rajinder Kumar to state custody in Oregon to face prosecution over a November 2025 tractor-trailer crash that killed two newlywed Americans, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said. Kumar has been indicted in Deschutes County, Oregon, on two counts of first-degree manslaughter and three counts of recklessly endangering another person. The charges remain pending before the state court, and the allegations have not been established at trial. In a post on X on Sunday, October 18, ICE's Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Seattle office confirmed Kumar's transfer to the Deschutes County Jail, saying the move would allow state criminal proceedings to continue. “Two Americans lost their lives, and their families deserve accountability,” ICE ERO Seattle Acting Field Office Director Julio S Hernandez said, according to the agency's official statement. “ICE worked closely with law-enforcement partners to ensure Kumar is returned to state custody to answer for the serious charges against him,” Hernandez added, according to ANI. He further said, “This coordinated action protects the public, supports the victims’ families, and ensures that an individual accused of these crimes does not evade justice.” “ICE will continue using every lawful tool available to protect the American people from criminal activity committed by illegal aliens,” Hernandez said. According to ICE, the agency had lodged an immigration detainer with the Deschutes County Jail following Kumar's earlier arrest. However, the county released him in April 2026 without honouring the detainer, the agency said. “ICE officers subsequently located and arrested Kumar at large earlier this year,” the agency said in its post, without specifying the date or location of his subsequent arrest. ICE said deportation proceedings would remain on hold until the conclusion of the state criminal case. “Following the conclusion of state criminal proceedings, ICE will pursue Kumar’s immigration case consistent with federal law,” it said. The agency's statement also outlined Kumar's immigration history. According to ICE, US Border Patrol apprehended him near Lukeville, Arizona, on November 28, 2022, after he “illegally entered the United States from Mexico”. He was subsequently placed in removal proceedings. ICE said that “a pending application does not confer legal status in the United States”.

End of Article

title: Why Pakistan will wear pink jerseys in ODI tri-series against England

Pakistan cricket team (AP Photo)

Messages promoting breast cancer awareness will also feature on the stadium’s big screens and LED perimeter boards. Commentators will reinforce the campaign’s message during the live broadcast, helping the PCB reach audiences both in Pakistan and abroad. The initiative aims to use the visibility of international cricket to encourage greater awareness of the disease and the need for timely medical attention. title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf raise $300,000 for charity with 20 luxury watches
text:
Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf turned 20 limited-edition watches into $300,000 for charity(Getty Images)

Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf celebrated 10 years with Swiss watchmaker Longines in 2018 with a fundraiser that brought in $300,000 for their charities. The tennis legends marked the anniversary with a limited-edition watch collection, but the real story was where the money went. The auction supported Agassi’s education foundation and Graf’s Children for Tomorrow, which helps children and families affected by war, exile and violence. The project brought together two causes the couple had supported for years. Agassi focused on educational opportunities for disadvantaged young people in the United States, while Graf’s foundation worked with children dealing with trauma. Later that year, Graf explained how the Longines partnership had helped her charity reach more children and expand its work into schools.

How a limited-edition watch auction raised $300,000 for charity

Longines unveiled the special Conquest V.H.P. collection at a charity gala at Paris’s Musée Rodin on June 2, 2018. The event honoured Agassi and Graf and celebrated a decade of partnership with the Swiss watchmaker. The collection featured 10 men’s watches and 10 women’s watches, created in limited numbers for the occasion. Longines then held an online auction throughout June. The company kept the first numbered set, marked 1/10, for its museum in Saint-Imier, Switzerland. Buyers acquired the remaining nine sets, and the auction raised $300,000 for the couple’s foundations. The proceeds went to the Andre Agassi Foundation for Education and Children for Tomorrow. Agassi’s foundation works to improve educational opportunities for disadvantaged young people, while Graf established Children for Tomorrow in 1998 to help children and families affected by war, violence and persecution. The fundraiser also reflected how the couple’s relationship with Longines had grown beyond a commercial partnership. Per Las Vegas Sun, Agassi said, “It was built around an overlap of shared values.” He explained that Longines first supported his former Grand Slam for Children event in Las Vegas before the relationship grew over the years.

Steffi Graf says Longines helped her charity reach more children

Graf offered a closer look at the impact of that support in the same Las Vegas Sun interview. At the time, she said Children for Tomorrow helped a little over 1,000 children each year, mostly through therapy. “We’ve been able to raise more funds and continue to grow, and now we are able to go into schools and work with teachers and train teachers to understand trauma. We just have a bigger reach now,” Graf said. Along with therapy, it had begun reaching children through schools and training teachers to recognise trauma. title: How Tom Brady's childhood love for baseball cards inspired his business
text:
Tom Brady’s childhood love for Don Mattingly cards inspired his growing trading card business beyond the NFL (Image via Getty Images)

Tom Brady has seven Super Bowl rings, but his love for baseball cards started long before his NFL career took off. As a child, he spent his money collecting cards of Don Mattingly, his favourite player. After years, Brady still owns that collection and sometimes brings it to CardVault store openings. What began as a childhood hobby has now become a business venture that keeps him connected to the sports collectibles world. Brady started collecting cards when he was around seven or eight years old. Growing up in San Mateo, California, he often visited a local hobby shop to add to his collection. The interest stayed with him through his football career and into retirement. At Fanatics Fest in New York in July 2026, he even got the chance to meet Mattingly and share the story behind his childhood collection.

Tom Brady still holds on to his Don Mattingly collection

Tom Brady did not hide his excitement when he met Mattingly at Fanatics Fest. The former New York Yankees star had been his favourite player since childhood, and his cards once filled the pages of Brady’s binder. “Since I was seven years old, I only wanted Don Mattingly cards,” Brady told Mattingly at Fanatics Fest in July 2026. He recalled how the cards filled the laminated pages of his childhood collection. Brady still holds on to that binder and sometimes brings it to CardVault store openings. Collecting also helped him develop a practical skill. During an interview with Front Office Sports at Fanatics Fest in July 2026, he joked that collecting baseball cards helped him become better at maths. For Brady, the appeal goes beyond owning valuable cards. He enjoys finding something new, following the players he admires and building a collection over time. Those childhood memories now connect directly to his work in the trading card industry.

How Tom Brady turned his childhood hobby into CardVault

Brady joined CardVault as a co-owner in 2024. However, he wanted more than a single shop carrying his name. title: Putin proposes trilateral summit with Trump, Xi to discuss Ukraine war: Report
text:
Putin Floats a Summit With Trump and Xi to Discuss Ukraine Deal

Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month to discuss the Ukraine conflict, with Moscow seeking a peace deal favourable to its interests, The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported. Putin reportedly raised the proposal during a telephone conversation with Trump on October 9. The Kremlin has confirmed that discussions about a possible meeting are underway, although no final decision has been made. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told WSJ that the three sides had yet to agree on the meeting or its agenda. “There is no clear understanding yet regarding the meeting itself or its potential agenda, although all three parties acknowledge the hypothetical possibility of such a meeting taking place,” Peskov told WSJ. A senior US official told the newspaper that Trump had not formally agreed to the summit but could be open to the proposal as he seeks to end the Russia-Ukraine war. According to the report, the Kremlin suggested holding the trilateral talks alongside the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, scheduled for November 18 and 19 in Shenzhen, China. Russian diplomats have reportedly presented the proposal to Chinese officials, who indicated they would not object if Trump agreed to participate. The proposal has raised concerns in Ukraine and among Washington's European allies, particularly over the absence of Ukrainian representation in discussions about the conflict.

Trump says negotiations making progress

On Sunday, Trump said negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict were making "great progress" while defending his administration's diplomatic approach towards Moscow. He also accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of failing to secure a better deal two years ago. In a post on Truth Social, Trump said he wanted to avoid actions that could push Russia away from the negotiating table. He also referred to ongoing hostage negotiations and said he could sign the relevant document at a later date. "My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table. Great progress is being made, and that includes current hostage negotiations! Signing that document at this time will do that, and I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump wrote.

Moscow and Washington discuss energy cooperation

The proposed summit follows a 90-minute telephone conversation between Putin and Trump earlier this month, which Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov described as "very substantive" and friendly. title: Batteries to autos: Chinese imports remain in top gear
text:
Two-and three-wheeler imports have shot up to $107 million during April-Aug, compared with $2 million a year ago

NEW DELHI: Every cheer for electric vehicle sales in the country also means that import of batteries from China goes up too given the complete dominance India’s neighbour enjoys in the global trade of this product. Not surprisingly, the spurt in the sale of EVs in India has resulted in import of batteries from across the border nearly doubling to $2.9 billion during April-Aug, making it the sixth largest import item from China so far this year, the latest commerce department data showed. The high growth has meant that it has overtaken electronic instruments, electric machinery, plastic raw materials and residual chemicals. With India and other countries failing to make any technological breakthrough, import of batteries is only going to surge. Indian battery makers, the few that have managed to set up shop after the PLI for the sector failed, in any case, are just packing the cells imported from China.

India-China trade

There are other areas of concern too. For instance, two-and three-wheeler imports have shot up to $107 million during April-Aug, compared with $2 million a year ago. Similarly, car imports are up 2.6 times to $226 million in the first five months of FY27 -- probably led by BYD -- from $87 million in the corresponding period last year. Even gold and silver imports have surged as have oil products (3x to $179 million), dye intermediates (2.6x to $338 million) and bulk minerals (3x to $180 million) but they remain small compared with electronics, machinery, chemicals and plastics that make up around three-fourth of imports from China. With its firm grip over the electronics and telecom value chain, higher production of mobiles, computers and other devices in the India has not led to imports of components and inputs from China shrinking in any way. Official data showed that telecom equipment, including mobiles, as well as electronic components have seen over 40% imports growth in the first five months, when trade deficit with China widened to nearly $56 billion as against $44.7 billion during April-Aug 2025. At this pace, it is set to cross the deficit for 2025-26, which was pegged at $112 billion. No wonder, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman and commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal have expressed a worry about it in recent days and last week both underlined the need for a “fair deal”. title: Former Labor attorney general turned judge Robert McClelland named new anti-corruption boss
text:
Former Labor attorney general and federal court judge Robert McClelland has been named as the new boss of the National Anti-Corruption Commission.

McClelland was the country’s top law officer in the Rudd government, serving from 2007 until 2011. He has served as the deputy chief justice of the federal circuit and family court of Australia since 2018, and was appointed to the court by the Coalition in 2015.

Christopher Savundra has been named as the Nacc’s new deputy commissioner. He is currently the executive director of enforcement and compliance at the corporate regulator, Australian Securities and Investments Commission.

Paul Brereton, the first boss of the commission, quit in May, saying criticism of him was “drawing attention away” from the body’s purpose.

The attorney general, Michelle Rowland, said on Monday McClelland had been chosen through an open, competitive and merit-based selection process.

Christopher Savundra has been named as the Nacc’s new deputy commissioner.

“I congratulate deputy chief justice McClelland and Mr Savundra on their proposed appointments,” Rowland said.

“Deputy chief Justice McClelland and Mr Savundra’s expertise will be an asset to the commission, and I have confidence in their ability to contribute to its important work to enhance integrity across the Commonwealth public sector.”

McClelland and Savundra will begin five-year terms on 11 January next year.

The Parliamentary Joint Committee on the National Anti-Corruption Commission signed off on the appointments, as required by legislation governing the commission’s work.

Rowland said both candidates received unanimous support from the committee.

The selection panel included attorney-general’s department secretary, Katherine Jones, former Federal Court judge Raymond Finkelstein, and Australian Competition and Consumer Commission boss, Gina Cass-Gottlieb.

Brereton was criticised for doing consulting work for his previous employer – the inspector general of the Australian defence force (IGADF) – while serving as the Nacc’s commissioner.

The Nacc was also heavily criticised after an initial decision in 2024 to not investigate the six people referred to it by the robodebt royal commission. It subsequently reversed the decision the next year.

title: Jacqui Lambie condemns One Nation cartoon mocking her struggle with vaginal prolapse
text:
Jacqui Lambie has condemned a One Nation cartoon mocking her health struggle with vaginal prolapse, as politicians from across the parliament back the Tasmanian senator against the “nasty” attack.

The latest cartoon, part of Pauline Hanson’s Please Explain series, took aim at the Albanese government’s Digital Duty of Care legislation which targets online safety.

It depicts Lambie, an army veteran, as saying “I can’t laugh because of my prolapsed vagina” before adding a crude sound effect ridiculing the health condition.

In an emotional address in the upper house in August, the independent senator spoke of her own struggles with the women’s health issue and the lack of access to care faced by other female veterans.

Responding to the cartoon on Monday, Lambie said voters doing it tough in a cost-of-living crisis didn’t need any more “nastiness”.

“If you think it’s a laughable matter about women having problems with their reproductive system then you be my guest, and you stand by her. But seriously, enough is enough,” she told ABC’s RN.

Releasing a statement following her media appearance, Lambie said going public with her condition didn’t make her health “fair game”.

“Speaking openly is not an invitation to be mocked or degraded,” she said.

“By making this cartoon, One Nation didn’t just make light of my own medical struggles, but those of so many other women who have experienced reproductive health issues.”

Speaking in Tasmania, the One Nation leader said the cartoon might have brought awareness to the condition.

“Jacqui Lambie, get over it … it is actually satirical, and I think she’s taken a heart in which she shouldn’t be,” Hanson said.

“Have a good look at it, have have a bit of a laugh, Jackie, and lighten up.”

Industry Minister Tim Ayres lashed the “nasty style of politics” he described as imported.

“There’s tens of thousands of Australian women who battle with health conditions like this one or others, and they don’t deserve to be smashed up by some cheap, nasty bit of political propaganda run out of Pauline Hanson’s office,” he told Nine’s Today Show.

Shadow Minister for Small Business Jacinta Nampijinpa Price said the health condition should not be made light of.

“I don’t like women being ridiculed for very personal issues such as that, and being mocked and played down, and certainly not leaders in our country, for that to happen too,” she told News24.

“When it comes to the world of politics, we need to play the ball, not the person.”

Speaking about Hanson, Lambie said “decent leaders don’t stir up hatred, pushing us towards bloody anarchy”.

Independent Victorian MP Monique Ryan condemned the cartoon on Sunday, saying Lambie had shown “courage and honesty in speaking of her experience of vaginal prolapse”.

“Pelvic organ prolapse – bladder or vaginal – affects about 1 in 12 Australian women. It’s often linked to physical strain, heavy lifting or past childbirth. It’s uncomfortable and debilitating.”

title: ‘Limited evidence’ of protester violence at Sydney demonstration against Israeli president Isaac Herzog visit
text:
An inquiry into a Sydney rally against the Israeli president’s visit has so far found protesters were “largely peaceful” and there is “limited evidence of physical violence on the part of the protesters”.

The Law Enforcement Conduct Commission (Lecc) kicked off its inquiry into the February protest at Sydney’s town hall against the visit of Isaac Herzog on Monday, outlining a number of issues it is examining, including police use of OC spray and “police boasting about gratuitous force”.

Lecc launched its investigation after widespread allegations of police brutality at the protest. Viral video footage showed police punching multiple protesters, and grabbing Muslim worshippers while they undertook sunset prayers.

Monday’s opening address was heard in public before closing for five-week long private examinations. The watchdog agreed to hold a portion of the hearing in private after the NSW police commissioner, Mal Lanyon, made a last-minute bid to have the entire hearings held in private, delaying the scheduled hearing by almost a month.

Counsel assisting the Lecc, Kirsten Edwards SC, said in her opening address that the evidence is far from concluded. But so far it shows: “there is limited evidence of physical violence on the part of the protesters. The protest appears to have been largely peaceful in its early stages.”

“Later conduct by protesters, described in the evidence of police as aggressive, was for the most part verbal and connected to a desire to march,” Edwards said.

“Footage also shows protest organisers at various points apparently attempting to defuse conflict with police.”

Police charged 30 people in the months after the protest with various offences, including hinder arrest and assault police. But almost a dozen of those protesters have had the charges against them withdrawn.

Edwards said that the Lecc would examine police conduct according to a law in place at the time, which restricted protesters’ ability to march.

This law, known as the Public Assembly Restriction Declaration, or Pard, was found unconstitutional by the state’s highest court two months after the protest.

On Friday before the Downing centre local court, police withdrew charges against seven people, after four people had theirs withdrawn in recent months.

In June, the local court set a joint hearing date for 25 of the approximately 30 people initially charged, which is expected to last six weeks in the local court in July 2027. After the dropped charges, the number of people part of that joint hearing is now down to 17.

Edwards said Lecc was examining multiple widespread concerns that had emerged in the 400 complaints lodged by the public and the 1,000 hours of footage the Lecc has reviewed. She said this included the use of OC spray against the mobility impaired and in close proximity to people’s faces.

title: Kylie Minogue songs already used to train AI as tech firms ‘strong-arm’ Australian government, music body warns
text:
AI has already been trained on the works of Australian artists including Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave without compensation, the peak global body for music rights has claimed, as the Australian government has been warned against giving in to “strong-arming” from tech companies seeking to weaken copyright law.

The International Confederation of Music Publishers (ICMP) – which represents Sony, Warner and Universal as well as thousands of independent publishers on six continents – has warned that of the dozens of countries approached to water down copyright laws, Australia appears to be the only to consider doing so.

John Phelan, the ICMP’s managing director, told Guardian Australia AI companies were asking policymakers to “legitimise larceny”.

“They’re trying to strong-arm Australian policymakers into ‘if you don’t do this, we won’t invest’.”

In July, Anthony Albanese said it would be “theft” if artists did not retain control over whether their work was used to build and train AI, and what they were paid for its use.

Music, film, media and news organisations had expressed concerns the government was being lobbied by global tech companies behind closed doors to weaken Australia’s copyright laws to help train AI models, without compensating the creative sectors.

But government and opposition members of a parliamentary committee on artificial intelligence appeared to revisit the issue this week, describing the current situation as a stalemate.

They said AI models were already training on copyrighted works in the United States without compensating creators – but that without changes to local copyright laws, those companies were withholding training frontier AI models in Australia.

In a joint letter to the prime minister this week, the inquiry’s Labor chair, Jo Briskey, and its deputy chair, Liberal senator Jonathon Duniam, recommended the government “examine current copyright settings” while ensuring creators retain control and are paid.

The independent senator David Pocock has raised concerns that the committee was coming to a position on copyright predetermined by the prime minister, after staffer edits were seen in the letter. Briskey has rejected the claim.

AI companies’ demands

The ICMP has been tracking how AI companies are attempting to change copyright law in different jurisdictions to allow training. Phelan highlighted methods that the companies had used to train their models on music, such as with spreadsheets containing millions of lines of music available on YouTube.

A key claim of the AI industry is that its models are not trained on Australian content due to copyright rules. title: Labor promises $30 weekly cap for Victorian public transport amid push for free travel
text:
Public transport fares in Victoria will be capped at $30 a week if the Labor government is re-elected next month – but commuters will need to dust off their Myki cards to benefit.

The premier, Ben Carroll, on Monday said the fare cap would begin on 1 January, the day after half-price fares end. The discounted fares were introduced after a period of free public transport in response to the fuel crisis sparked by the US-Iran war.

A $15 cap would also be introduced for concession-card holders, while exisiting benefits – including free public transport for children and free weekend travel for seniors – would continue.

Carroll told reporters the new cap would save regular commuters up to $1,400 a year.

“[This is] real important cost-of-living relief, in a time of rising interest rates and increased petrol prices,” he said.

But the state’s public transport minister, Vicki Ward, said commuters must use Myki cards to access the capped fares.

This is despite the government completing the rollout of tap and go payment across the public transport system last week, when concession card holders were able to pay using a bank card, smartphone or smartwatch.

“We’ve never advised people to throw out their Myki card. So I’d suggest they have a look in the back of the couch and find their Myki card if they need to,” Ward said.

She said the government would to make the $30 cap accessible via tap and go “as quickly as possible”, but would not provide a date.

Carroll said the cap would cost the government $206m and would run for two years until December 2028.

The government said the cap was not sustainable in the long-term and would be funded through “commonsense decisions to reduce spending” in other areas.

The announcement was welcomed by the Swinburne university transport expert Prof Hussein Dia, who said it would provide households with certainty during the cost-of-living crisis. But he said the benefits would not be equitable.

“The greatest benefits will naturally go to people who already have good access to trains, trams, buses, and travel frequently,” Dia said.

“People in outer suburban areas with poorer public transport may receive much less benefit, even though they may face equally strong cost-of-living pressures.”

Juanita Pope from the Victorian Council of Social Service said the organisation had long called for cheaper public transport.

“A fare cap is good policy on many fronts: good for household budgets, road congestion, and the climate,” Pope said.

The Greens leader, Ellen Sandell, urged the government to go further and make public transport free.

“After 12 years in government, Labor is only offering Victorians a temporary discount with an expiry date after the election,” she said.

“People are sick of paying more and getting less. We need more frequent, reliable and accessible trains, trams and buses that people can actually depend on.”

title: Priest accused of sexually harassing minor boys arrested
text:
The Mangaluru police have arrested Siprian Pinto, the priest at St. Vincent Ferrer Church at Valencia in Mangaluru, for alleged aggravated sexual assault on five 14-year-old boys.

Police Commissioner Sudheer Kumar Reddy said Pinto was arrested at the house of his relatives.

The police will produce him before the magistrate after the interrogation and completion of other procedures.

In the complaint before the Mangaluru South police on the night of October 15, one of the victims, a 14-year-old boy, claimed that Pinto gave him a chocolate and said he loved the boy’s smile.

He then took the boy to a room in the church and inappropriately touched him.

Subsequent visits

On his subsequent visits to the church for prayers, the boy alleged that Pinto touched him inappropriately.

On the evening of August 14, Pinto called the victim to the receptionist room, hugged him and put his hands inside the boy’s undergarments.

Also read: Priest found guilty of abusing minor girl under guise of rituals

The victim then told his four friends, all aged 14, about Pinto’s conduct. His friends said that they too had experienced the same.

The victim said he informed his parents about the sexual harassment, and they all went to the Mangaluru Bishop. On his instructions, they lodged a complaint.

The complaint was registered for offences under Sections 8 (sexual assault) and 9 (aggravated sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and Section 75(2) (sexual harassment) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

title: Key conduit in ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani case arrested
text:
A key aide to Gem Granites owner R. Veeramani, who allegedly facilitated money transfers to help the octogenarian businessman evade police action, has been arrested, police sources said on Sunday.

The Special Investigation Team (SIT), constituted to probe cases registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act against Veeramani and his associates, arrested Sakthivel, his manager. Investigators suspect that he played a key role in transferring funds to individuals who allegedly helped the businessman evade legal action, the sources said.

Veeramani is facing multiple allegations of sexual abuse of children and a case relating to abetment of suicide. Besides Veeramani, his associate Shanti, her husband Mahendra Simhan, and five others have been arrested and lodged in Puzhal Central Prison.

On Sunday, the Central Crime Branch of the Greater Chennai Police registered a seventh case under the POCSO Act against Veeramani, based on a minor’s statement alleging that she had been sexually exploited by him. The incident occurred in the residence of Shanti. Statements have so far been recorded from 11 victims, most of whom were minors when the alleged offences took place, the sources said.

The arrest of Sakthivel is expected to shed light on the alleged transfer of large sums of cash and gold through one or more middlemen to help Veeramani avoid police action. “Sakthivel organised the transfer of funds and purchase of gold on the instructions of Veeramani. He was the key conduit between the businessman and the middlemen who tried to help in evading police action,” a police officer, who did not want to be quoted, said.

The police are also searching for N. Prakash, who is on the run and believed to be staying abroad. Investigators found that he had a bank balance exceeding ₹20 crore, most of which was allegedly received through bank transfers from firms owned by Veeramani. He had served as an adviser to the Gem Group of Companies, the sources said. Investigators have established the purchase and delivery of gold worth about ₹24 crore, besides identifying other cash transfers.

Sakthivel’s questioning is expected to help trace the alleged beneficiaries of these transactions, the sources added. The SIT in a statement said incriminating materials were seized from Veeramani’s residence on Lloyd’s Road in Royapettah, his farmhouse in Kanathur, and a business establishment.

title: Uttar Pradesh Khadi festival begins in Meerut
text:
The ten-day Khadi Festival and Exhibition organised by the Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board commenced in Meerut, showcasing a wide variety of traditional Indian products, handicrafts, textiles and indigenous goods from different parts of the country.

The exhibition features a collection of products, including Khadi garments, Banarasi silk sarees, warm clothes, Kashmiri shawls, dry fruits, crockery and several other traditional items.

“Visitors can explore brass products from Moradabad, exquisite Kantha embroidery from West Bengal, silk products from Banaras, bedsheets from Pilkhuwa, and wooden handicrafts from Saharanpur. Khadi institutions from various regions of Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar have also set up stalls displaying their diverse range of handwoven textiles and indigenous products,” said Shishir Singh, Chief Executive Officer of the Uttar Pradesh Khadi and Village Industries Board.

Mr. Singh added, “with the festive season underway, the exhibition offers a wide range of products suited to celebrations such as Durga Puja, Dussehra, Dhanteras and Diwali. From traditional clothing and home décor to handcrafted decorative items, wooden artefacts, brassware and other festive essentials, the exhibition provides visitors with an opportunity to shop for unique, locally produced goods while supporting traditional artisans and small entrepreneurs,”.

In the exhibition, a Gandhi Pavilion has been established at the centre of the exhibition, featuring a spinning wheel that highlights the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi and the importance of Khadi in India’s freedom movement. Rajya Sabha Member Dr. Laxmikant Bajpayee and other public representatives inaugurated the Khadi Festival on Saturday (October 18, 2026). The representatives toured the exhibition and felicitated traders participating from different states.

Such Khadi exhibitions are organised across Uttar Pradesh to promote traditional industries, generate employment opportunities and provide market access to entrepreneurs associated with village industries. The initiative aims to connect Khadi with India’s cultural heritage while encouraging self-reliance and supporting local artisans under the vision of “Vocal for Local.”

The exhibition showcases a wide variety of products, including handwoven Khadi garments, stoles, handicrafts, herbal products, home décor items and region-specific traditional goods, offering visitors an opportunity to celebrate India’s rich craftsmanship while contributing to the growth of the rural economy.

title: Bengaluru: Two minors detained for murdering 13-year-old boy
text:
Two minors, aged 16 and 17, have been detained for allegedly murdering their 13-year-old neighbour over a petty dispute about a month ago, after his body was found on the premises of Vibhutipura lake on October 12.

The victim, Arafath, a class 7 school dropout, was allegedly attacked with stones by the duo following a confrontation near the lake on the evening of October 4, the police said.

According to the police, the murder was allegedly triggered by an argument that broke out about a month ago after a two-wheeler was blocked. The dispute involved Arafath, his brother and one of the accused. The accused allegedly held a grudge against the boy and repeatedly picked fights with him following the incident.

On October 4, when Arafath was near Vibhutipura Lake, the two minors allegedly waited for him and confronted him. During the altercation, the boy reportedly threatened to bring his elder brother to beat them up and attempted to flee.

Fearing repercussions, the duo allegedly chased him and attacked him with stones. Arafath collapsed following the assault. The accused then allegedly dropped a large stone on his face, killing him on the spot, before fleeing, the police said.

His body was subsequently found on the lake premises on October 12, prompting the police to investigate the murder and identify the suspects.

The police said all three boys were school dropouts.

title: Self-taught artist recreates the magnificence of Tamil Nadu’s temples in miniature
text:
On surfaces as tiny as pencil lead, chalk, and sandalwood, intricate temple sculptures come alive through the work of a self-taught micro artist in Chennai.

S. Kaviyarasan, 27, hopes to take his art to international competitions and showcase the State’s sculptural heritage. The artist, a native of Dharmapuri, began practising when he was ten years old, driven by a fascination with the sculptures he saw in temples.

“I started trying to carve when I was in class five. I looked at sculptures in temples and practiced on my own,” he says, sitting cross-legged in a classroom in the Manidheya Neyam IAS Academy, Chennai, where he came in 2022 to prepare for government examinations, run by former Mayor Saidai Duraisamy.

He studies the details of sculptures, their design and the ideas they convey, using them as the starting point for his miniature works. “When I go to temples, I look at the sculptures and try to understand what they are trying to tell us, and how they have been designed,” he says.

Mr. Kaviyarasan’s interest led him to explore the engineering and artistic ingenuity embedded in Tamil Nadu’s temple architecture. The stone chains at Varadaraja Perumal Temple in Kancheepuram, the rotating stone ball inside a yazhi’s mouth at Kailasanathar Temple, and stone carvings of Sri Margabandeeswarar Temple in Virinjipuram, near Vellore, also informed his work.

Elements from these appear in one of his notable creations, a sandalwood sculpture of Nataraja, which also features the sages Patanjali and Vyaghrapada, and Ravana lifting the Himalayas. Carved from a single piece, the overall structure casting a shadow resembling a person in prayer.

His interest in history also influences his work. He speaks of Rajendra Chola I, whom Mr. Kaviyarasan has carved in a piece of chalk, and the temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram, stressing the importance of understanding the historical context behind the structures and figures he recreates. “In common history textbooks Rajaraja Chola is more famous, but Rajendra Chola also has a great history. He built Gangaikonda Cholapuram. He carved his own legacy, but he also paid homage to his father’s legacy,” he said.

Mr. Kaviyarasan’s work has earned him recognitions such as the Guinness World Records for making 617 interlinked chain links from pencil lead, the Asian Book of Records in 2019, and the Indian Book of Records in 2019 and 2021. He is currently pursuing a digital art course.

His journey, however, began with practice at home, without his family’s knowledge. His father, Selvam, is a tailor, while his mother, Manjula, manages the household. It was only later, when teachers and others recognised his work, that he began to see micro art as something he could pursue seriously.

“I was doing this at home without telling my family in the beginning. Later, some teachers in college supported me. They told me that this was a form of art and that I could take part in competitions,” he says.
