title: Nagenthran criticises TVK-led government over lack of monsoon preparedness
text:
BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran on Sunday criticised the TVK-led government over its alleged inefficiency in monsoon preparedness.

Rainwater stagnation in many parts of Chennai was due to the alleged lack of precautionary measures, even though there was a weather advisory in this regard, he said. The impact of heavy rain noticed in the international air terminus, GST Road, Ganesapuram subway, and many arterial roads and areas in Tambaram was only indicative of the alleged inaction of the government machinery, Mr. Nagenthran said.

Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay must realise that administration was about standing with the people to address their grievances, the BJP leader added.

title: Two-year-old boy dies of suspected malnutrition in Alappuzha
text:
A two-year-old boy was found dead at his home here on Sunday in a suspected case of malnutrition, the police said.

An officer of Trikkunnapuzha police station said that according to doctors, the toddler was “acutely anaemic” and appeared malnourished as his weight was 7.6 kg, whereas the normal weight for his age would be closer to 12 kg.

“A histopathology test will confirm whether the toddler’s condition and death were caused due to some illness or malnourishment,” the officer said.

Five other children

He said a case for unnatural death has been registered, and following the results of the histopathology test, the future course of action will be decided. The officer said that the child’s father was an autorickshaw driver living with his wife in Karthikappally and they have five other children, including a newborn. One of their children had died earlier, he added.

The wife was admitted to the government medical college hospital at Vandanam on Saturday to give birth, and the children were at home with the father.

Child welfare committee

On Sunday morning, the father found that the two-year-old boy had died. The child welfare committee took the remaining children into their care, the officer said.

The officer further said that the couple and their children were earlier moved to a shelter home, Gandhibhavan, in view of their poor living conditions. “However, they created problems there and returned to their home here,” he said.

title: Release recommendations of Thiruppugazh Committee,   Anbumani urges T.N. government
text:
PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Sunday urged the State government to make the Thiruppugazh Committee report public and implement its recommendations after Chennai recorded heavy rainfall on Saturday.

In a statement, he said several parts of Chennai received rainfall of an intensity comparable to a cloudburst, and if such incidents were to become frequent, it would necessitate the urgent implementation of flood mitigation measures.

“For more than five years, the Pattali Makkal Katchi has been warning that climate change could lead to cloudburst-like situations in Chennai and that the city’s flood-prevention and stormwater drainage infrastructure must be strengthened to deal with them. Yesterday’s rainfall has only reinforced this warning. There is also a risk of the situation worsening this year due to the impact of El Niño. Taking these factors into consideration, the government must intensify flood-prevention measures,” he said.

There was a possibility that Chennai could receive even heavier rainfall in the coming days than what it experienced on Saturday. Climate change, which is threatening the world, could cause impacts beyond anyone’s imagination. “Keeping this in mind, it is the government’s responsibility to undertake comprehensive flood-prevention measures,” he said.

Even after 43 months, the Thirupugazh committee report has still not been made public. The previous DMK government had stated that the report contained a total of 161 recommendations on flood mitigation and that 101 of them were being implemented.

“However, no one knows what those 161 recommendations were or which 101 recommendations had actually been implemented,” he said. Chennai must not be allowed to be submerged by floods once again, he added.

title: Teja Singh Samundri’s legacy takes centre stage in BJP’s pro-Sikh push in Punjab
text:
With the 2027 Punjab Assembly election nearing, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is trying to build a pro-Sikh image by weaving historical Sikh narratives, and Sardar Teja Singh Samundri, a key architect of the Sikh gurdwara reform movement, and a co-founder of the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC), has become one of the focal points of that outreach.

As the centenary of his martyrdom is being observed this year, the BJP’s top leadership, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, have frequently invoked Samundri’s legacy at public rallies. Samundri, who refused to compromise on his principles and declined conditional release from British custody, died in 1926 at the age of 43 at the Lahore Central Jail.

The Sikh icon actively participated in several agitations, including the ‘Chabian da Morcha’ (in 1921-22 for the control the keys to the treasury of the Golden Temple in Amritsar); the ‘Guru ka Bagh Morcha’ (in 1922 for the control of the Guru ka Bagh gurdwara in Ajnala); and the ‘Jaito da Morcha’ (in 1923, over the removal of Maharaja Ripudaman Singh of Nabha by the British). Samundri was arrested several times.

The naming of the Teja Singh Samundri Hall at the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar serves as a reminder of his pivotal role in shaping modern Sikhism.

The Central government’s ‘Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav’ initiative, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, pays tribute to Samundri’s contributions. By evoking Samundri’s legacy, the BJP wants to place Sikh sacrifice within the larger story of the freedom struggle and the party’s focus on nationalism.

The BJP has tried to draw attention to its ‘pro-Sikh’ image by highlighting the steps taken by the Union government since 2014, including the formation of a Special Investigation Team to probe the 1984 anti-Sikh riots cases; the opening of the Kartarpur Corridor, which connects the Kartarpur Sahib gurdwara in Pakistan with Dera Baba Nanak shrine in India’s Gurdaspur district in Punjab; the waiving of GST for langars; and permitting Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) registration for Harmandir Sahib.

The BJP has also declared December 26 as ‘Veer Bal Diwas’ to mark the martyrdom of Sahibzadas Baba Zorawar Singh and Baba Fateh Singh, sons of Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru. The appointment of Kewal Singh Dhillon, a Jat Sikh, and his appointment as the party’s new State president is seen as another attempt by the party to consolidate its position in the community.

“The BJP is trying to cultivate as many Sikhs as possible,” Amarjit Singh Narang, former Professor of Political Science, Indira Gandhi National Open University, told The Hindu.

“There is speculation about a possible alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). While that may happen or not, these efforts by the BJP to woo Sikhs could favour the BJP either way. If they win over Sikhs without an alliance, it is good enough for them. If an alliance with the SA

title: Neha Bora | The permanence of agitation
text:
“Another world is not only possible, she is on her way. Maybe many of us won’t be here to greet her, but on a quiet day, if I listen very carefully, I can hear her breathing.” In 2024, Neha Bora cited this quote by Arundhati Roy, calling her work a “bridge to the possibility of a different or better world”.

Today, amid widespread protests in Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls and state crackdown, Neha, 29, a PhD student from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) and a non-binary person who uses they/them pronouns, stands at the centre of the movement. Neha, the current president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist–Leninist) Liberation, came into the national spotlight during a 23-day hunger strike at Jantar Mantar that began on June 28. The protest culminated in the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Also read | ‘Coordination with CJP on agenda basis, but alliances are always on radar’: Neha Bora

For Neha and her team, they are doing “nothing different from what they have been doing over the last few years” — protesting for what they believe in. Videos of Neha being detained by the police during protests in the city four years ago are resurfacing, drawing comparisons with footage of the activist’s recent detention.

Recently, however, people Neha supported in the past have come forward to back the youth protest. One example is the survivor of the Unnao rape case, whose cause had prompted Neha to protest earlier. The goodwill Neha has built through years of activism is now translating into support from all quarters, say Neha’s comrades.

Hailing from Uttarakhand, Neha’s political journey began with a theatre group during the undergraduate years in Delhi University. Neha’s family supports the BJP government that the young leader is determined to challenge, but attitudes within the family have begun to shift. Since the Jantar Mantar protest, Neha’s mother has been supporting the daughter’s activism in her own way — by calling to remind them to rest and be ready for the next protest. Police action and detentions sometimes frighten people close to Neha. But Neha seems to be undeterred. “We’ve taken to the streets knowing that we can be detained, roughed up, bruised. But what about the people who are being bruised, broken, raped, and killed for no fault of theirs?” Neha said recently.

On the frontlines

Even away from the public eye, Neha speaks softly, but the voice rises while talking about how women and queer people have borne the brunt of the BJP’s ire. They will therefore be on the “frontlines of the resistance”, says the AISA president. Neha has worked on gender issues for years, from protesting the release on bail of the men convicted of raping Bilkis Bano to serving as the student representative on their college’s Internal Complaints Committee. For this generation, humour is a way of responding to all that is wrong

title: Visakhapatnam’s Bengali community celebrates Durga Puja with rituals, bhog and cultural programmes
text:
Bengali families across Visakhapatnam are celebrating Durga Puja with rituals, bhog and cultural programmes, each association keeping alive its own history.

Durga Puja began as a private affair in the households of zamindar families in early Kolkata before evolving into a community festival, or ‘Sarbojanin puja’, in the early 20th century. Wherever a few Bengali families gather, the festival follows.

Bengali professionals moved to Visakhapatnam in the late 19th and early 20th centuries to work in stevedoring, port construction and the Bengal Nagpur Railway. Today, several pujas are held across the city.

The Bengali Association, established in 1929, is the oldest association of a non-Telugu community in the city, said Arunabh Karmakar, a software engineer and member of the association. Dasara, he said, is “the biggest festival” for the community.

The puja was suspended for three years during the Second World War and resumed after 1945, said Secretary A.N. Bhattacharjee. Earlier venues included the Town Hall, the Simhachalam Devasthanam hall, near KGH and Rani Chandramani Park Marg. It is now held at Vasavi Function Hall, beside One Town Police Station, from October 16 to 21. The association’s president is Swarup Kumar Banerjee.

Mr. Bhattacharjee said dramas that took nearly two months to rehearse had given way to dance performances as people found less time to practise. Most families once lived in One Town, but now live in other parts of the city. Treasurer Rabindranath Karmakar said the idols are smaller this year because of the height of the roof; they once stood about seven and a half feet tall. Bhog, prepared without onion or garlic, will be served for four days as the puja has an extra day.

Waltair Kalibari on Railway Station Road is celebrating the 66th year of its puja, which was started by Bengali railway employees. General Secretary Joydev Chakrovortty described the temple as the city’s first and oldest Kali temple. Celebrations began on October 15 and will end with immersion on October 21. The cultural evenings feature “Bangla Sa Re Ga Ma Pa” artistes from Kolkata.

Utsab Cultural Association, formed in 2011, held its first puja at AMCOSA Hall in Maharanipeta, where it continues, said Vice-President Dr. Alok Mazumdar. “We have a very special bond among all the families,” said Nilima Choudhury, a member. The programme includes dance forms from different States, a comedy drama, “Bhuter Golpo”, Dhunuchi Nach and Sindur Khela, with immersion on October 20.

On the last day, married women apply vermilion to the goddess and to one another in Sindur Khela, wishing each other a long and happy married life. At immersion, the community bids the goddess farewell and invites her to return next year.

EOM

title: 85 books by inmates released at Cuddalore Central Prison
text:
Former Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary V. Irai Anbu on Saturday released 85 books written by inmates of Cuddalore Central Prison under Sirayil Mulaitha Siragugal (wings that grew in prison), an initiative to nurture their creative abilities and support rehabilitation.

The books were developed with support from the Ezhuthaga Iyakkam (Write Movement) and the Tamil Nadu Prisons Department, comprise poetry, stories, essays, songs, and letters. Mr. Irai Anbu said the publication of 85 books within six months reflected the sustained efforts of the participants, the Ezhuthaga Iyakkam team, the district administration, and prison authorities. He urged the inmate-authors to continue writing and said that their works could help society understand their lives and experiences while providing an opportunity for introspection.

“When you leave this campus, society will see you as creators,” he said, encouraging them to return to the community with confidence and a renewed sense of purpose.

Describing the initiative as an achievement for Cuddalore, he said the combination of training, sustained engagement, and publication deserved recognition. He urged the authors to become role models for others and draw inspiration from everyday experiences for their next books.

Cuddalore Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar said the initiative was a model for prison reform that had enabled inmates to establish themselves as writers and creators. Writing could change the way inmates viewed themselves and how their families and society perceived them. Efforts would be made to expand the initiative, he said.

Deputy Inspector-General of Prisons, Vellore Range, G. Shanmugasundaram; Cuddalore Central Prison Superintendent A. Parasuraman; New Century publishing house managing director Santhanam; and Ezhuthaga Iyakkam coordinator V. Killivalavan participated.

title: Man held for smuggling ganja on government bus at Katpadi
text:
A 33-year-old man was arrested after the police seized 10 kg of ganja from his bag onboard a government bus in Christianpet village on Sunday.

The police said the arrested person was identified as S. Ganesh Kumar, a native of Anupparpalayam in Tiruppur district. He was travelling in a government bus that was proceeding to Vellore from Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh.

The bus halted at a check post near Katpadi for a vehicle check.Police personnel checked the luggage of commuters, and they found contraband in Ganesh Kumar’s bag.

Initial inquiry revealed that Ganesh Kumar procured ganja from agents in Chittoor to sell it among industrial workers in cities such as Coimbatore, Tirupatur, Erode, and Salem. A case was registered by Katpadi Police. He was lodged at Central Prison in Vellore.

title: Supreme Court address a parental anxiety: How to keep the Internet safe for children | Explained
text:
The story so far: A Supreme Court judgment on October 15 addressed the everyday anxiety of parents, who are torn between allowing their children access to the Internet and the need to keep them safe from vile, abusive online content.

The judgment by a Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran reasons that the solution is not to ban children from using the Internet, but to take measures to keep them safe from exploitation by predators lurking online. The court declared that a child, like any other individual, has a fundamental right to access and use the Internet.

The court said the Internet is a marketplace of ideas, creative expression and information. Its value is priceless, not only for information. For children in remote areas, the Internet is often the only source of learning and information. Likewise, for children with special needs, the Internet is often the only place where they are able to find company in others like them

The State, lawmakers and parents cannot blame children for the presence of Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) on the Internet. The wrongdoer is the person who creates, circulates, sells or seeks out such material, and the intermediary which fails to detect and remove the content. To keep the child away from the Internet on account of such failures would be to mistake the victim for the problem.

Any measure for the safety of children must be directed at the harmful material and those responsible for the same, and not at the children themselves.

The court held that “our children are entitled to both safety and the freedom to access the Internet”. To deny them the freedom to go online would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age did not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.

What led to the judgment

The court found that its directions for online child safety in a September 23, 2024 judgment in a petition filed by Justice Rights for Children Alliance were largely ignored for the past two years, leading to serious lapses.

The court said there had been an “alarming increase” in child sexual exploitation and CSEAM circulated on social media platforms. It flagged how indirect links to such harmful material were promoted and shared through social media algorithms to bypass the rigours of the special penal provisions designed for the protection of children within cyberspace.

“Links to view child pornography were circulated and sold for anywhere between Rs. 40 to Rs. 5,000”. The court described the state of affairs as a “disquieting failure” on part of online platforms. Due diligence would have meant not only removal of child pornographic content but also making an immediate report of the illegal content to the police under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

title: 15 dead, over 40 injured as truck rams into devotees outside Gwalior temple
text:
At least 15 people, including two women and two teenagers, were killed and more than 40 injured after a truck rammed into a crowd of devotees outside the Sheetla Mata temple in Madhya Pradesh’s Gwalior in the early hours of Sunday (October 18, 2026), officials said.

The incident occurred around 1.30 a.m. near the temple, located in the middle of a hill in the Santau area, about 20 km from Gwalior city. According to the police and eyewitnesses, a truck laden with paddy hurtled down a steep slope and ploughed into devotees waiting outside the temple premises before crashing into a wall near the temple gate and bringing it down. The truck was going to Punjab, and the driver was using GPS navigation, the officials said.

Gwalior Superintendent of Police Dharm Vir Singh told The Hindu that the injured had been admitted to various hospitals across the city. Gwalior Collector Ruchika Chouhan said that two to three critically injured people were being treated at the trauma centre of the State-run Gajra Raja Medical College. About 10 others were admitted to private hospitals, while the remaining injured had been discharged after treatment.

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav ordered the transfer of City (Vishwavidyalaya region) Superintendent of Police Ravi Bhadoriya over alleged negligence and suspended eight police personnel, including three town inspectors, a traffic inspector, a head constable, and three constables. Mr. Yadav also ordered a detailed investigation into the incident.

Mr. Singh said the truck driver, who had fled the scene, and the vehicle’s owner had been arrested from neighbouring Dholpur district in Rajasthan and were being interrogated. Both are from Punjab.

“During questioning, the driver said the vehicle’s brakes began to malfunction while he was climbing uphill and failed completely as he reached a slope, causing him to lose control. He then veered to the left and rammed into the area outside the temple where several devotees were present,” Mr. Singh said, adding that a medical test was being conducted to ascertain if the driver was under the influence of alcohol.

Barricades and crowd management arrangements were in place at the temple, but the truck broke through about five barricades, injuring two State Home Guards personnel, the SP said. The police were trying to ascertain how the truck entered the prohibited zone despite diversions and checkpoints, he said.

Magisterial inquiry ordered

Ms. Chouhan has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident by Additional Collector C.B. Prasad. Asked about possible lapses in crowd management, she said the inquiry would establish responsibility.

“We had held two to three meetings about the management of devotees and arrangements at the temple, and responsibility was fixed for everyone. So, we are now investigating at which level the lapses happened so that action can be taken,” she said.

title: Eight workers mowed down by speeding car in Punjab's Sangrur; 12 injured
text:
Eight workers were killed, and 12 others sustained injuries after a car ran over them on Lehragaga-Jakhar road in Punjab's Sangrur district on Sunday (October 18, 2026), police said.

The incident occurred near Alisher village when a group of more than 20 workers enrolled under Viksit Bharat Guarantee Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission Gramin (VB-G RAM G) — several among them women — were engaged in some work. Some of them were sitting along the road.

A speeding car coming from the direction of Jakhal mowed down the group of workers, police said.

Subsequently, the car driver abandoned his vehicle and fled from the spot, Superintendent of Police Palwinder Singh.

Five workers died on the spot, another police official said. The injured were taken to a hospital, where some were said to be in serious condition.

Sangrur Deputy Commissioner Poonamdeep Kaur said eight workers were killed in the incident, while 12 were injured.

The district administration is taking all necessary steps, including providing medical help to the accident victims, she said.

Punjab Cabinet Minister Barinder Kumar Goyal, the local MLA, expressed grief over the incident. He said the injured are being provided medical treatment, and assured all possible help from the government for the victims. Ambulances have been deployed to shift bodies, he said.

Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema, too, condoled the death of workers. “The tragic incident that occurred with women labourers working under MGNREGA near the village of Alisher in Lehra is extremely sad. In this hour of grief, heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. May the Almighty grant eternal peace to the departed souls and give strength to the families to bear this loss,” Mr. Cheema said.

Congress MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring expressed grief over the deaths. “Deeply saddened by the tragic incident in Lehra where eight MGNREGA workers were mowed down by a speeding car, leaving several injured. This is heartbreaking.

“These are the poorest workers who toil hard to earn a living. I urge the administration to ensure immediate medical aid for the injured, sternest action against those responsible and adequate compensation for the families of the deceased. May the departed souls rest in peace,” the Ludhiana MP said in a post on X.

Leader of Opposition in Punjab Assembly, Partap Singh Bajwa, also expressed grief over the tragic incident. “The tragic loss of eight MGNREGA workers in Lehra after being struck by a speeding vehicle is deeply distressing. Several others have also sustained injuries in this horrific incident. My heartfelt condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones. May the departed souls rest in eternal peace, and may the injured recover soon,” he said

title: 17 dead after stampede breaks out at Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal
text:
At least 17 people, most of them women and children, died and 25 people were injured after a stampede broke out at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata on Saturday night (October 16, 2026). The incident took place around 7:40 p.m. at the exit gate of the Pandal, a statement from the police said.

Also Read: Kolkata pandal stampede on October 17, 2026

According to reports, a large crowd had gathered at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotstab in Kolkata’s Girish Park area and tried to take shelter inside the pandal after a brief spell of rainfall.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the stampede broke out after a misleading announcement was made by the organisers of the Durga Puja pandal. He said that the organisers of the club have been detained at the local police station and an investigation will be held to ascertain the reasons behind the incident.

The injured have been admitted to a State-run health facility. “Our priority is to give medical aid to the injured. 17 persons have died. This is a painful incident. Of the 25 injured, one is critical, and 24 are stable. We stand by the family of the dead,” Mr. Adhikari said. The Chief Minister said that he is at Medical College, Kolkata and also spoke to the family of the deceased.

The Durga Puja pandal has been closed to the public after the stampede. After the incident, local people gave a hand to rescue the injured. Eyewitnesses said that there was not much police presence at the pandal when the stampede broke out. The pandal is located in a narrow area and access to it was blocked by stalls that have come up around the pandal.

Fire fighters, disaster management team, and senior police officials rushed to the spot for rescue operations, according to a police statement.

Reacting to the incident, President Droupadi Murmu expressed deep sorrow over the loss of lives and extended her heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. “The news of the deaths of people in a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata is extremely sad. I express my deepest condolences to all the bereaved families. I pray for the swift recovery of those who have been injured”, Ms. Murmu said in a post on X.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the incident as “extremely distressing” and announced compensation of ₹2 lakh for the dead and ₹50,000 to the injured. He said the local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah arrived in Kolkata on Saturday (October 17) evening. He was scheduled to visit several Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata on Sunday, but said in a social media post that he had cancelled all his scheduled engagements in the wake of the stampede.

“Deeply shocked and saddened to learn about the stampede at the Chore Bagan Puja Pandal. I pray to Maa Durga for the speedy recovery of all those injured and for strength and courage for their families during this difficult time,” former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee shared on her social media.

title: TDP hopeful of a cakewalk in Kamalapuram Municipality as YSRCP stays away from contest
text:
Not a single nomination was filed by the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) for the elections to the Kamalapuram Municipality in Kadapa district even as the last date ended on Sunday.

As a consequence, TDP’s chairperson candidate G. Swapna, as well as the councillor nominees, were hopeful of a cakewalk as only Independents were in the fray.

Unlike the violent incidents in Pulivendula and other places, Kamalapuram did not report any clash or violence, but the YSRCP candidates stayed out of the contest.

“The rivals, perhaps, found it unviable to focus their energy and funds on the municipality, as it will any way come into our fold, thanks to the people’s unwavering support,” Kamalapuram MLA Putha Krishna Chaitanya Reddy told The Hindu.

Meanwhile, the deadline for filing of nomination papers for the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) ended in Kadapa district on a hectic note, with cases booked on several persons for resorting to violence. Several senior leaders were kept under house arrest on the final day of filing nominations.

The district police booked cases against 63 people, mostly belonging to the YSRCP, in Pulivendula for Saturday’s violence, particularly assault of police forces and arson that led to destruction of public property.

Taking cognisance of the crowded processions that took a violent turn, the district police placed former Deputy Chief Minister S.B. Amzath Basha under house arrest in Kadapa and Member of Parliament Y.S. Avinash Reddy in Pulivendula.

TDP Pulivendula in-charge ‘B. Tech’ Ravi and the party’s district president C. Bhupesh Reddy were also placed under house arrest.

Decrying his house arrest, Mr. Amzath Basha accused the ruling party leaders of assaulting his party cadres with sticks and rods, besides flaying the policemen for remaining a mute spectator.

Meanwhile, TDP’s Kadapa Mayor candidate Matli Suvarna filed her nomination in the presence of Kadapa MLA Reddeppagari Madhavi Reddy and party’s zonal coordinator R. Srinivasa Reddy.

title: MBA student smuggled MDMA on train to Vijayawada or ₹50,000 commission, say police
text:
An MBA student, Yerramsetti Naga Sowmya, who was caught with MDMA by the Government Railway Police (GRP) and EAGLE at Vijayawada railway station on October 14, had allegedly procured the contraband from a Nigerian in Bengaluru, police sources said.

The EAGLE and GRP personnel arrested Sowmya, a native of Patamata in Vijayawada, after she arrived in the city on Bengaluru-Howrah Express.

Investigation revealed that Sowmya’s boyfriend, Venkata Sai Vardhan, is in jail after being named an accused in a similar case. She reportedly took ₹50,000 as a commission from a drug handler, Sheik Basheer, for smuggling MDMA from Bengaluru to Vijayawada.

“Sowmya allegedly collected 110 grams of MDMA worth ₹11 lakh from a Nigerian national Andol Noel at Yelahanka in Bengaluru before boarding the train to Vijayawada. She had plans to hand over the drug to Basheer,” an investigating officer told The Hindu.

Police have seized the mobile phones of Sowmya and Basheer.

“We are trying to trace the suppliers and clients through the social media platforms used by the accused,” a GRP official said.

title: Analysing female labour of the North East States and Union territories
text:
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) 2025 report shows a clear increase in Female Labour Force Participation (FLFPR) since 2019–20. The rise was more pronounced in rural areas, where the percentage increased from 33% to 45.9%, than in urban areas, where it rose from 23.3% to 27.7%. This difference calls for a closer look at the northeastern States, where female labour force participation is higher, and Union Territories (UTs) to understand how female labour force participation changed in rural and urban areas.

The chart below presents the Average Annual Percentage Point (AAPP) change in rural Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR) for each State between 2019–20 and 2025.

The AAPP is used to indicate the pace of improvement. It shows that major rural northeastern States and UTs are above this benchmark. Arunachal Pradesh records the highest increase, at 8.28 percentage points per year, more than three times the all-India benchmark of 2.58. At the other end, FLFPR declined in Delhi and Lakshadweep. The difference between the highest and lowest AAPP is more than 10 percentage points, from +8.28 in Arunachal Pradesh to −2.34 in Lakshadweep. This means that the national average of 2.58 points conceals substantial State-level variation.

The chart below shows that Arunachal Pradesh stands out again, with an AAPP of 5.24 points above the all-India urban AAPP of 0.88 pp, followed by Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Chandigarh, A&N Islands, Assam, Tripura and Jammu & Kashmir.

But Puducherry, Ladakh, Delhi and Lakshadweep recorded negative AAPP. The urban range, from +5.24 to −1.30 percentage points, remains considerable, even though the national average is much lower than in rural areas.

The rural all-India AAPP is therefore 1.7 percentage points higher per year than the urban figure. For a statistical analysis, this is important: the national direction and the State-level distribution are two different stories. While the aggregate shows an increase, it does so across the NE States, while the UTs are far more heterogeneous.

However, AAPP alone is insufficient to evaluate the performance of northeastern States and UTs, as it measures only the pace of change and does not consider the level of female labour force participation from which a State started. Therefore, the 2019–20 FLFPR for each State is used as the baseline. Combining the baseline level with the subsequent AAPP provides a more meaningful assessment of whether States are catching up from a lower base, sustaining improvements at higher levels, or making slow progress.

In the chart below, the upper-left portion of the rural scatter contains Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur and Tripura.

These States had an FLFPR below the all-India 2019-20 benchmark but recorded AAPP above the national average, indicating faster improvement, whereas Delhi recorded an AAPP below the all-India average.

title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
text:
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.

In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."

Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".

Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry.

The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

On Sunday, looting and clashes with police continued on a smaller scale in parts of the capital and Lyon.

Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people in Paris, according to the AFP news agency, and bottles and rocks were again hurled at police.

Sunday saw cities across the country confront the impact of what developed into one of the worst bouts of disorder in modern French history.

In Limoges, the ornate 19th Century city hall was gutted by a fire started by rioters on Saturday, its clock tower and roof collapsing and the flames took hold.

Speaking near the ruined building, Annèyse said: "This is very upsetting. Harming heritage buildings just because you are angry at the government is selfish, I think. It's hurting everybody."

"It's awful and unbelievable," said another man who gave his name as Gerrard. "We are very sad and I think it will be a long time to put it back as it was before."

Shopkeepers were seen early on Sunday morning picking up large shards of glass in Paris as rubbish trucks cleared up debris on some of the larger streets.

Student protests which began last month escalated significant on Saturday after they were joined by trade union members and other anti-government groups.

The response from political figures has pointed to France's deep political divisions as the country prepares for an election in April which could see the hard-right pitted against the hard-left.

France's Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that while demonstrating was a fundamental right, there were "outrages" committed by "several thousand far-left individuals" who were determined to target public buildings and confront the police.

Later, they were joined by "delinquents who looted and ransacked numerous businesses in several cities in France", he said.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon - leader of the hard-left La France Insoumise party - heavily criticised Nuñez and police chiefs on social media.

title: 'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
text:
A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests on Saturday.

Dramatic footage shared online shows the 19th-century building engulfed in flames, with the spire of its clock tower later collapsing.

On Sunday, stunned residents watched as firefighters, who had battled the blaze through the night, assessed the building's structural integrity. Officials have not yet confirmed whether the town hall is at risk of collapse.

"Damaging heritage buildings because you're angry with the government is selfish", one resident told the BBC.

BBC correspondent Chris Bockman reports from Limoges.

title: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
text:
Four members of the Canadian military have died and dozens were injured in a major fire at a base in the province of Alberta.

Addressing the nation on Sunday from Ottawa, Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".

The fire broke out at about 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases, and is now contained. Its cause is still unclear, but officials said it did not appear tied to "terrorist activity".

"The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces who we have lost," said Carney.

The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died.

Of the 39 injured people being cared for in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said at a press briefing on Sunday evening.

Fire and rescue teams are remaining at the scene to contain any potential flare-ups, Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh told the BBC.

Members of the infantry had been conducting "high-intensity combat training with live munitions" at a grenade range and attack range, where 10 soldiers practise attacking a simulated enemy, Maj-Gen Wade Rutland told reporters at the briefing.

"There was a multitude of ordnance moving through the Wainwright training area," he said, including a grenade launcher, grenades, small arms and ammunition.

A grass fire ignited about 1km (0.6 miles) away, with the cause currently under investigation, and moved toward the attack range.

"What I would say is there was multiple training activities happening throughout the training area at the time," he said. "Uncommonly strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly and shift direction towards the range administrative area."

Cannon fire had been heard coming from the base on Saturday before it suddenly stopped, Mayor Pugh told the BBC, noting it's not uncommon to hear cannons being fired there.

News then came through that local emergency services had been deployed to an "all hands on deck" situation.

Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".

The people who were hurt were on the attack range and included reservists and soldiers from the Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, officials said.

In a statement early on Sunday, the Canadian Armed Forces said that "while the incident remains under investigation, at this time, there are no indications that it was the result of any terrorist activity".

Rutland told the briefing: "We do not believe this [incident] to be a result of any oil and gas infrastructure nor any outside interference".

title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
text:
US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table.

"I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table".

Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia on Friday night, two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened.

Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake".

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump's order by calling it "an important and truly historic moment". He said the sanctions, which were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September, would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has described the suspension of the sanctions as a 60-day pause during which their potential impact on the US and global economies would be analysed.

In his Truth Social post, Trump also said Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did", adding "he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now".

Zelensky has pushed for an end to fighting, and has repeatedly said that Putin doesn't want peace, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week.

Despite the international sanctions, Russia has still been able to export oil, much of it to China and India - often at attractive discounts. According to the think-tank Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), China has taken about half of Russia's crude exports, with India accounting for about 37%.

In remarks to a European Union summit, after Trump announced the deal to buy diesel from Russia and said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Putin, Zelensky said it was nice to be among "real leaders".

title: Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
text:
Two Russian men secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services have given rare accounts of operations they claim to have been involved with, that have targeted military assets and personnel inside Russia.

One of the men, whom we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role from Russia in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil.

He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs.

The documentary, by independent Polish journalist Marcin Mamon, also features a man we are calling Foma, a Russian living in exile in Poland.

Foma runs a network of undercover volunteers in Russia, that surveils high-level officers that the GUR - Ukraine's military intelligence service - is considering targeting, he says. He stresses they are never involved in the attacks themselves.

He was also tight-lipped about who they were surveilling, but after Lt Gen Fanil Sarvarov was assassinated in December last year in Moscow, Foma admitted he had provided the Ukrainians with intelligence on him.

There have been previous media reports of Russian sabotage groups, but it is rare to get access to someone operating on the ground, like Ivan, explaining alleged activities.

The GUR has confirmed that Ivan and Foma are both working for the agency. But it also has acknowledged that it cannot know the full picture. When Ivan's handler was pressed on whether he could be trusted, the handler replied: "I'm not sure of anyone, except myself."

And both the GUR and the men are cautious about how much detail they share, making it impossible to verify the activities the men claim to have carried out.

The broad tactics Ivan and Foma describe, however, have been acknowledged by the Ukrainian authorities. Kyiv has spoken of its strategy of co-ordinated drone attacks on what it claims are legitimate targets inside Russia, and has acknowledged it uses secret agents for this.

There have also been several political assassinations in Russia since the start of the war. As a matter of policy, Ukraine never officially admits or claims responsibility for targeted attacks, though a Ukrainian intelligence officer has previously admitted to the BBC it was behind the killing of senior military figure Lt Gen Igor Kirillov in December 2024.

It is difficult to confirm how many Russians are doing this kind of work for Ukraine. According to Foma, they number about 300-500, though this is impossible to verify.

If you are outside the UK, watch on YouTube, external and listen to the BBC World Service Documentary Podcast - Shadowmen: Russians working with Ukraine

Ivan and Foma say they are both opposed not just to Russia's war in Ukraine, but to President Vladimir Putin's regime - and believe his political future depends on the war's outcome.

"At the moment... I think the [Putin] regime might fall if they lose the war… Through our actions... we are trying to speed this up," Ivan says.

title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting in Mumbai
text:
Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff has survived a shooting in Mumbai and has not sustained any gunshot wounds, according to Indian police who are investigating the incident.

The 36-year-old was shot at on Sunday evening, while he was in a car that was leaving a football club in the suburb of Juhu.

Several news outlets have published a video showing at least two gunmen firing multiple shots at close range at the front passenger seat of a car while it is slowly moving past a crowd.

The incident has heightened concern about the safety of public figures in India, with some killed or injured in targeted attacks in recent years.

"These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," said Eknath Shinde, deputy chief minister of Maharashtra state, where Mumbai is located.

He paid a visit to Shroff after the shooting on Sunday evening, and said the actor and his mother had been left "shaken" by the attack.

Police said two people were injured in the shooting, including Shroff's driver, local media reported.

This is the latest in a string of attacks on some of the country's biggest public figures in recent years.

In 2024, police in India arrested two members of a criminal gang for a gun attack targeting the home of Bollywood actor Salman Khan.

That same year, influential Indian politician Baba Siddique was shot dead in Mumbai.

The son of two actors, Tiger Shroff made his acting debut in 2014 with the romance film Heropanti and went on to star in several films.

He is also a football enthusiast who plays for the professional football club Mumbay FC.

title: EU tariffs aimed at China hitting Ukraine, steel boss says
text:
The boss of one of Ukraine's biggest steel companies has called on the European Union to drop import restrictions on products made from the country, arguing it has been "bundled together" in measures aimed a curbing cheap imports from the likes of China.

Yuriy Ryzhenkov, chief executive of Metinvest, told the BBC the recently-imposed tariffs on imported steel to the EU were "unfair" and had been put in place "without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in".

He said he wished to see "at least a carve out" for Ukraine to access the EU market.

A spokesperson for the European Commission said the EU "took into account the difficult situation" of Ukraine when deciding its steel policy.

The trading bloc has recently imposed restrictions on steel imports in an effort to protect steel manufacturers of member nations.

It has capped the amount of steel which can enter the EU tax free at 18.3 million tonnes per year - a 47% reduction from 2024 levels.

There are some country-specific quotas in the policy, but the overall aim is to cut the amount of steel that can be imported due to member nations struggling to compete with cheap imports from the likes of China and Turkey.

Despite a free-trade agreement (FTA) being in place between the EU and Ukraine, the FTA does not stop the EU from introducing separate trade protection measures.

"Ukraine has been bundled together into those measures without any consideration for the situation Ukraine is in," Ryzhenkov said, pointing to the war with Russia.

"Access to the European market is crucial for survival," he added. "The restrictive measures that have been put in place by the authorities in the European Union, they don't help.

"I think it's unfair that Ukraine has been treated in the same way as all of the other importers into the European Union."

The Ukraine steel industry estimates steel exports to the EU could ultimately fall by about 50–60%.

The EU said Ukraine's specific steel quota guaranteed exports of the metal, but acknowledged this was at a "level lower than in the past years".

"Despite the war effort, Ukraine remains an important exporter of steel to the EU," a spokesperson said, adding it had "offered compensations" to its largest suppliers, which included Ukraine.

title: Threat forces Israel to Austria flight into emergency landing
text:
An Austrian Airlines flight from Israel to Austria has been forced to divert to Bulgaria after a reported bomb threat.

The Airbus A320 plane was travelling from Tel Aviv to Vienna on Sunday night but made an emergency landing in Sofia, where passengers were evacuated, the Bulgarian transport ministry said in a statement.

The Bulgarian air force scrambled a MiG-29 fighter jet to escort the airliner, the transport ministry said. No injuries have been reported and an investigation has begun.

It comes after a pilot attempted to hijack a Flydubai flight en route to Tel Aviv last month by attacking the captain, before the flight's crew and passengers overpowered him and landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

Bulgarian and Israeli media reported that a bomb threat had been made.

Austrian Airlines has confirmed a threat was made, without giving further details. A spokesperson told the AFP news agency there were 51 passengers and six crew members on board the jet.

Authorities conducted a security search of the plane after it landed in Sofia, about 30 minutes from when the alert was first raised. It was over Romania when it diverted to Sofia.

Flight tracking data showed Austrian Airlines 82 left Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv on Sunday evening before landing at Vasil Levski airport in Sofia three hours later.

Last week, Croatia and Germany both scrambled fighter jets after a commercial flight from the Greek holiday island of Corfu to the German city of Nuremberg accidentally sent out a hijacking alert.

The BBC has sought further comment from Lufthansa, the owner of Austrian Airlines.

title: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to 'public benefit fund'
text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic says it will commit 5% of its shares to a fund that will make donations for the "public good".

The announcement comes as Anthropic lays the ground for a potential blockbuster stock market listing that could value the firm at more than $1tn (£750bn).

The AI industry has come under intense scrutiny recently over safety concerns and fears about its impact on society and the economy. Anthropic reportedly said in its initial public offering (IPO) filing that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".

Anthropic said its proposed fund could support nonprofit organisations, and efforts to address AI's impact on the jobs market.

None of the shares held by the the fund would be used for lobbying or political donations in the US or overseas, it added.

Anthropic's Public Benefit Fund could also receive another 2% of the firm's shares at its board's discretion, the Claude developer said in a statement released on Sunday.

Technology billionaire Elon Musk responded to the announcement on social media with: "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." "This is what I will be doing," he added.

Last week, Anthropic told prospective investors that its revenue surged by 45% to $16.8bn (£12.6bn) in the three months to the end of September.

In common with other AI firms, it is seeking to position itself as being able to generate huge profits despite spending billions on developing the technology and building infrastructure to power its models.

Companies around the world, primarily technology firms, have cut thousands of jobs after investing in AI, with many pointing to higher efficiencies from its adoption.

title: Australian Greens senator denies claims of misconduct towards women
text:
An Australian Greens senator has denied allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards women and accused his party of "nasty political games", days after the claims emerged.

Last Thursday, Greens leader David Shoebridge said Senator Jordon Steele-John, 32, had taken leave from the party room after a letter from seven current and former members said he had been accused of "multiple allegations" of misconduct between 2017 and 2025.

In an online post on Sunday, the senator denied the claims and said he was not on leave. On a sexual assault claim, he said police investigating the matter had closed the case and no charges were laid.

An internal party probe has been launched into the allegations.

Steele-John, who has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair, was first elected to the senate in Western Australia in November 2017.

In his letter responding to the claims, Steele-John said his nickname - "Feels on wheels" - initially referred to him being emotional when advocating for disability rights but had since taken on a "more sinister meaning" about his alleged mistreatment of women.

He accused Shoebridge of mishandling the matter and questioned the timing of the letter, saying "it is no coincidence" that the allegations were sent to the leader "the day after we agreed on the timeline for the next preselection" ahead of the next federal election.

Days after the letter with the claims was sent to Shoebridge, local media reported that the party had created a 47-page dossier years earlier that listed a number of allegations against Steele-John and how to manage media coverage if they emerged.

Steele-John said the dossier was made so that the media would not "bombard" the two women at the centre of those claims and that neither woman had made a complaint.

He acknowledged the allegations against him would have "damaged" the public's trust in him and said he was "committed to rebuilding that by acting with as much transparency and accountability as I can".

Shoebridge's office confirmed that the allegations had been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission.

title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
text:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July.

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism, including from some US Republicans.

However, on Sunday, Zelensky said on Telegram he had had conversations with Trump's top negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
text:
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.

A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.

Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday.

"We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku.

The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.

But the weather - powered by strong El Niño conditions in the Pacific - has so far prevented them from beginning a second of three phases, in which underwater objects will be probed to determine their depth and sediment will be dredged.

"We're working to get everything done today if we can," Bandla said. "The crew's really excited."

Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her twin-engine Lockheed Electra when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937.

From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California.

But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel.

One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.

Images of the so-called Taraia Object - which Purdue University says is visible in photography dating back to 1938 - show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters, though other explorers remain sceptical.

Interest in the expedition prompted New Zealand's Air Force Museum to publish, external previously unseen reconnaissance images of Nikumaroro on Friday.

While the Taraia Object is not obviously visible in any of the black-and-white slides, taken in 1938 from a seaplane, they do show the beached wreck of the SS Norwich City, a British merchant vessel that ran aground on the island during a storm in 1929, killing 11.

Purdue, which with the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) is spearheading the expedition, said the incident demonstrated the risks surrounding the island.

To get into the atoll's lagoon, a boat has to navigate through a narrow gap created in the reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.

title: Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
text:
Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.

"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him. "We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."

The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California. Police said officials are investigating his death as a suspected overdose.

Gerber had been a model like his mother and younger sister Kaia, making his catwalk debut for Italian label Moschino aged just 16.

Crawford wrote in the post on Sunday: "We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years."

"We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain," she also posted.

"Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia," she wrote in closing, with an emoji of angel wings.

The tribute also listed the dates of his birth and death.

The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner lists Gerber's case as pending additional investigation. The Santa Monica Police Department has said there is no indication foul play was involved in his death.

Gerber's sister Kaia also dedicated a post to him on Sunday which included a video of the two siblings as children dancing together, a photo of them standing near the ocean, and a four-page letter to "prez" typed out on a blue background.

In the letter, she said she had been scared of getting her ears pierced, so "you went first".

"But when I held the earring they took from your body, all I could think was: That belongs to you," she wrote.

"I am learning how to love you when I cannot see you," she also wrote. "How to tell you something without picking up my phone to call you. How to be your sister in a world that I can't reach for you in," she wrote.

In recent years, Gerber had spoken openly about his mental health challenges and drug use and frequently posted videos on Instagram himself for what he called "Mental Health Mondays".

His father Rande Gerber, a well-known businessman, co-founded the Casamigos tequila brand with George Clooney.

title: Anthropic says it will commit 5% of shares to ‘public benefit’ fund
text:
Anthropic has pledged to commit 5 percent of its shares to a new fund dedicated to the public good, with plans to increase the contribution as the artificial intelligence giant’s market value grows.

The creator of the AI assistant Claude announced the new “Anthropic Public Benefit Fund” on Sunday as tech firms face intense scrutiny over the potential dangers posed by the frontier technology.

list 3 of 4Protesters disrupt Ben-Gvir event forcing him off stage

list 4 of 4Flight from Israel makes emergency landing in Bulgaria after bomb threat

end of list

In a blog post, Anthropic said it was committing 5 percent of company shares with immediate effect, subject to stockholder approval, with an additional 2 percent to be added “at the board’s discretion” for every 50 percent increase in the company’s value.

“Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good,” the San Francisco-based firm said.

“It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.”

Anthropic said the fund could be used to make donations to traditional nonprofits, as well as “direct distributions to specific populations”.

It said labour market disruption due to AI could be among the causes addressed by the fund.

“Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” the company said.

“The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”

Anthropic, officially registered as a “public benefit corporation” in the US state of Delaware, said the fund would not be used for lobbying or political donations, either in the United States or overseas.

Founded in 2021 by former employees of ChatGPT creator OpenAI, Anthropic is preparing for what could be the largest public initial offering in history. It is expected to list on the US stock market before the end of 2026, with analysts forecasting a valuation exceeding $2 trillion.

The company’s charter requires its leadership to balance shareholder returns with responsible AI development.

The breakneck speed of AI development has prompted widespread anxiety about possible negative downstream effects on society, including the job market.

In a report published last month, consulting firm McKinsey estimated that up to 11 million American workers may need to switch careers over the next decade due to AI-driven automation.

title: Trump defends Russian sanctions relief, lashes out at Zelenskyy
text:
United States President Donald Trump has defended sanction waivers for Russia, saying he wants to keep Moscow at the bargaining table and accusing his counterpart in Kyiv of not wanting to end the war in Ukraine.

Trump made the comments on Truth Social on Sunday in response to criticism of his decision to block numerous sanctions on Russia just days before they were due to take effect.

Recommended Stories

“My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” he said.

The move has triggered a significant diplomatic fallout between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy over the past week.

Zelenskyy said that waiving sanctions on Russia, which launched a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022, “will hurt Ukraine”, telling NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday that it would strengthen Russian President Vladimir Putin’s war effort.

“We can’t compare me and Putin. He’s [an] aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He’s a terrorist, and that’s why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position.”

Trump reiterated his claim that Zelenskyy does not want the war on his country to end, saying on Truth Social that Kyiv was launching attacks on diesel refineries in Russia despite knowing it was “seriously hurting the world diesel markets”.

“Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him… he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did,” Trump wrote.

Trump announced plans on October 9 for Russia to supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets to tackle fuel prices that have soared since the US and Israel launched war on Iran in late February. The move led Tehran to effectively close the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of global energy exports transited before the war.

Trump’s embrace of Russian energy has angered not only Kyiv, but also European partners and many US officials, who say the move rewards Moscow while it continues its four-and-a-half-year war against Ukraine.

US-Ukraine talks continue

The Ukrainian president said on X on Sunday that he has spoken with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as part of “virtually non-stop communication” between the two countries’ teams aimed at the “next steps in diplomacy”.

title: Fast-moving grass fire caused Canada’s military base tragedy
text: A grass fire, fanned by strong winds, is being blamed for the Canadian military base tragedy in Alberta. Four armed service members were killed during what was a training exercise with 19 reported in critical condition in hospital.

title: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia, setting oil facilities ablaze
text:
At least one person has been killed, and five others injured after Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, one of Kyiv’s largest aerial strikes in the war.

St Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov said firefighters were battling fires sparked by Sunday’s attacks on the St Petersburg oil terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and industrial warehouses in the Kolpinsky district south of the city.

list 2 of 3Why Iran-US negotiations keep failing

list 3 of 3Photos: Protests across France spiral into looting, blazes and clashes

The governor said the “massive” strike killed at least one person and injured five, and that several residential buildings and two houses were also hit.

The attack disrupted flights at St Petersburg’s main airport, one of the country’s busiest, which was restricting operations “for safety reasons”, Beglov said.

Russian e-commerce company Ozon said there was a fire at its logistics hub in St Petersburg. The internet company VK said drones attacked its data centre in the broader Leningrad region, adding that normal services were available to users.

Leningrad Governor Alexander Drozdenko said 145 drones had been shot down and about 20,000 people were without electricity following the drone raid.

The Ministry of Defence said 1,015 Ukrainian drones were neutralised overnight over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.

US-Ukraine tensions deepen

The strikes came as tensions between Kyiv and Washington deepened, with US President Donald Trump criticising Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, and the prospect of further US sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.

On Sunday, Trump defended his Friday decision to put a hold on implementing new sanctions on Russia, saying he did not want to do anything that would “foolishly” drive Moscow “away from the bargaining table”.

In a social media post, the US president said he believed new sanctions would undermine negotiations to bring about a diplomatic end to Moscow’s war on Ukraine, refuting bipartisan criticism that he was favouring Russian President Vladimir Putin’s interests over Kyiv’s.

Trump also lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been critical of Trump’s recent outreach to Putin, for launching strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, claiming Zelenskyy “doesn’t want to end this war”.

Trump had announced on October 11 that Russia and Ukraine agreed to an “energy ceasefire”, but offered no details. Zelenskyy told The Financial Times that he was “done” with the ceasefire a few days later, after holding off on striking Russia’s energy facilities while Moscow had continued attacking Ukraine’s.

Zelenskyy wrote on X on Sunday that Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump’s announcement.

title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case amid widening regional outbreak
text:
Kenyan health authorities say an eighth Ebola case has been detected in the East African nation.

Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth told Kenya’s Citizen TV that of the 38 people tested on Sunday, one had returned a positive result.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Kenya records third Ebola case, linked to first patient who died

list 2 of 3Kenya’s Health Ministry confirms second Ebola case

list 3 of 3Kenya’s Ebola cases test preparedness beyond Nairobi

end of list

“He is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker. He developed fever, headache and muscle pain,” he said.

Amoth said the man, who worked as a patient attendant cleaning utensils and linens, was likely exposed to Kenya’s first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month.

He developed symptoms on Saturday, was quarantined and tested for the virus, a Ministry of Health source said.

The ministry reported four new cases on Saturday, three of whom were health workers who treated the country’s first Ebola patient, a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5.

In a post on X, the ministry said the fourth person was related to the deceased patient.

Kenya has been on heightened alert, as the Ebola outbreak has spilled across the border from the DRC. The current outbreak is of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment.

The DRC has recorded at least 9,400 cases, including more than 4,500 deaths, in the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history, which started in May.

Ituri province in eastern DRC remains the disease’s epicentre, accounting for almost three quarters of confirmed cases, according to the government’s most recent data. It announced on Sunday that the virus has reached an eighth province, North Ubangi.

State-run news agency ACP reported on Sunday that authorities in North Kivu province, where the World Health Organization said substantial transmission continues, are introducing a one-week ban from Monday on people entering the province from Ituri in an effort to slow the spread.

Other measures set to be introduced include restrictions on passenger numbers in cars and on motorbikes and suspension of large public gatherings.

Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 confirmed cases, including 15 imported from the DRC, and two deaths, before it was declared Ebola-free in August.

title: Kinship and surveillance: The return of Somali piracy
text:
Mogadishu, Somalia – The fishing town of Bander Beyla, on Somalia’s Puntland coast, has become a focal point of the renewed piracy crisis. But beyond the hijackings and international security operations, residents are struggling to protect their livelihoods as fishing restrictions, arrests and surveillance reshape daily life.

Abdifatah Mohamed has spent 20 years fishing off Somalia’s coast. He began at 15, but says declining catches and foreign trawlers have made it increasingly difficult to support his family.

“I don’t catch as much fish anymore, and the prospects for catching lobsters have become rare,” the 35-year-old said.

“Foreign trawlers are emptying out the seas,” he added.

Somalia’s central government collapsed in 1991, weakening maritime oversight and leaving its waters vulnerable to illegal fishing. Some fishermen, angered by foreign vessels exploiting the country’s resources, have turned to piracy.

“We’re [fishermen] no match for the foreign trawlers, who possess capabilities far greater than us, which impacts the livelihoods of our families on land,” Mohamed said.

He added, “Some from our community have taken up arms at sea, but deep down I know it’s hurting our community.”

A community caught in the crackdown

Piracy has surged off Somalia since late April 2026. The reported number of hijackings varies according to whether counts include commercial ships, fishing vessels and dhows. Several seized vessels have been held near Bander Beyla, bringing the crisis close to the town’s fishing community.

In late August, local authorities restricted fishermen from going to sea amid concerns that pirates were disguising themselves as fishermen.

“The local authorities gave an order the last week of August preventing us from going out at sea, which would remain in effect for two months,” Mohamed said.

“Our families depend on what we catch at sea. Even though our catches [of fish] have gone down in recent years, it helped provide for our families at home. But it’s like we were being punished for crimes we have nothing to do with, and our families have suffered for it.”

For fishermen, Mohamed said, going to sea has become a risk whether they obey the restrictions or defy them.

“It’s a two-way risk, because if the authorities know you went out to sea, they could accuse you of piracy or even transporting supplies to the ships that were hijacked,” he noted.

“While out at sea, you could face arrest or violence from international navies, and get mistaken for pirates, and taken away to a jail in a foreign land. It’s happened to a lot of men from this town.”

Abdirizak Said, who has fished in Bander Beyla for 15 years, said the crackdown has deepened the hardship faced by residents.

“Dozens have been arrested, most of them after they brought food or khat to the pirates, when the ships were anchored near Bander Bayla,” he said.

title: Flight from Israel makes emergency landing in Bulgaria after bomb threat
text:
An Airbus A320 flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna has made an emergency landing in Bulgaria following a reported bomb threat, according to the Bulgarian Ministry of Transport.

Austrian Airlines flight OS82 was near the border with Romania when the crew received a bomb threat and decided to land in the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, the Transport Ministry said in a statement on Sunday.

Recommended Stories
