title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
text:
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.

The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

The health minister, Muhammad Pate, said authorities had begun tracing 44 people identified as contacts of the patient. “We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” he said.

Uganda’s ministry of health said the patient had only transited through Uganda and that she is a Nigerian woman who had been on a business trip to Congo’s eastern region. The Nigerian authorities have not disclosed her nationality.

“Travel through Uganda does not establish that infection occurred here. The location of exposure remains under investigation,” the ministry said in a statement. The ministry insisted Uganda has “no confirmed active Ebola cases”.

Nigeria is the latest country to report an Ebola case as the outbreak spreads across the region. Kenya confirmed its first case earlier this month and has since recorded nine infections. Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases, but it later declared itself free of the virus.

Dr Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centers for Disease Control, said on X that “we are facing an extremely serious threat,” with a fatality rate of nearly 50% of cases.

“This Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has already become the most geographically extensive in history, affecting several countries spread across three regions of Africa,” he said.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control said two weeks ago it was stepping up surveillance following the detection of Ebola in Kenya and strengthening the country’s preparedness for a potential outbreak.

“These efforts have focused on early detection, isolation and referral, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, contact tracing, risk communication and protection of health care workers,” the agency said.

Nigeria established an Ebola taskforce in June after the outbreak in Congo in mid-May.

The spread of Ebola beyond Congo has heightened fears among health authorities about the rapid transmission of the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has infected more than 9,500 people and killed more than 4,600 people.

The latest Ebola outbreak is the fastest-spreading on record and is on track to exceed the deadliest on record, the 11,000 people killed in West Africa’s regional outbreak between 2014 and 2016, WHO has said.

title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau
text:
Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials said on Facebook.

The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.

The police search took place on Monday, involving “investigative procedures aimed at clarifying the circumstances related to the said batch of vaccines”, according to the social media post, which was translated from Portuguese. The announcement noted that seizing the immunizations did not point to “irregularities in the quality, safety, or effectiveness of the vaccines”.

The Bandim Health Project recently posted a letter of approval for the trial from Guinea-Bissau’s national ethics committee at the ministry of public health, dated 14 July and signed by the committee’s president, Mouhammed Djicó Ould Ahmed. A Danish research ethics committee, which had to change its rules to consider a clinical trial, also approved the study earlier this month.

Quinhin Nantote, the health minister of Guinea-Bissau’s transitional government, disputed reports that the trial would move forward.

“This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese on Thursday.

The study was redesigned over the summer, but it would still deny hepatitis B vaccines to 7,000 newborns in the first six weeks of life, in a country where about one in five adults have the virus. Hepatitis B kills 15% to 25% of people with chronic infections, causing cancer and liver failure, and newborns are particularly vulnerable – but vaccination within 24 hours of birth is safe and highly effective at preventing illness.

Any study that would deny the vaccine to participants was “unethical and exposes newborns to serious and potentially irreversible harm”, said Tarik Jašarević, a spokesperson for the World Health Organization (WHO), calling hepatitis B vaccination at birth an “essential public health intervention”.

Through its country office in Guinea-Bissau, the WHO and its partners have been advising the ministry of health on the planned introduction of the hepatitis B vaccine and the potential impact of this study, Jašarević added.

The Bandim Health Project was founded by anthropologist Peter Aaby in 1978, and it is now co-led by his wife, Christine Stabell Benn, an epidemiologist.

Kennedy has repeatedly praised their work, calling them “the deities of vaccine research” at a recent anti-vaccine conference. title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan
text:
More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.

Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.

The DHS did not respond to a question about whether they can keep their work permits, but TPS generally allows people to work while their protections remain in effect.

The decision marks another incident where the Trump administration, which has previously sought to end these temporary protections from deportation and send people back to their home countries, has allowed people covered by the temporary status to stay in the country but without giving any guidance as to how long.

Yuriy Boyechko, CEO of Hope For Ukraine, a non-profit that provides humanitarian aid in Ukraine and helps resettle newcomers in the US, described the government’s announcement as “last-minute patches”.

It is a “bandage that has been placed on a wound that does not solve the real issue,” he said. “It’s time for US to come up with some normal path to permanent residency for all these people,” Boyechko noted. He emphasized that they cannot safely return to Ukraine.

Andrew Arthur, a national-security and immigration expert at the Center for Immigration Studies, a Washington thinktank that favors lower immigration, said the government will eventually decide but faces no deadline. Until then, nothing changes, he said.

“It’s simply going to be an extension until it is a termination,” he said. “It’s beyond cavil that both Sudan and Ukraine are experiencing ongoing armed conflict, and therefore the secretary is well within his authority to continue TPS for each of them.”

The Trump administration has already terminated TPS for more than 1 million people from 13 countries, including Venezuela, Haiti, Honduras, Nicaragua, Afghanistan and Syria.

But in a change in practice roughly a month ago, the administration kept protections in place for nearly 200,000 Salvadorians whose TPS was set to expire on 9 September. In that case they also said that they were going to make a decision at the appropriate time and that in the meantime, people from El Salvador could continue to work and live in the US.

Activists and a bipartisan group of lawmakers have been raising the alarm over the upcoming deadline for TPS to expire for Ukrainians, arguing that conditions remain unsafe for them to return home amid the war with Russia.

title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
text:
Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.

With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.

The Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, Alberta’s capital, celebrated the result.

“Albertans made a clear choice. They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other. Above all, Albertans chose Canada.”

He said the result would allow Canadians to move forward together and accelerate efforts to diversify trade, develop major infrastructure projects and make Canada a global energy powerhouse, with Alberta at its centre.

The results showed an overwhelming majority of Albertans had voted to remain and one radio show host posted: “Someone owes Albertans $130m for this theatrical waste of taxpayers’ money.”

Pollster David Coletto told the Guardian that residents felt the referendum was “a distraction away” from what they wanted their government to focus on.

“There was almost a general sadness about the wasted energy spent on this rather than the more real threats they see, including the Trump administration,” he said. “Most Albertans feel deep grievances with the federal government while also being proudly Canadian. The marriage may be rocky at times, and most Albertans want to see some thing changed, but very few are willing to see the marriage end.”

The province’s separatists, however, saw a silver lining. “We don’t have the final results. I think the numbers are going to fluctuate, but it is fair to say that at least a quarter of Albertans feel that Alberta needs to be treated better,” said Keith Wilson, a leader of the separatist movement.

Others took a different view of the results. “The result is bleak. Independence feels far away and we should not pretend this was not a defeat, however, it changes nothing about the reality of the circumstances Albertans find themselves in,” David Parker, a longtime far-right organiser linked to a massive breach of voter information, wrote on social media.

The Alberta premier, Danielle Smith, welcomed the early results, saying they showed widespread support for remaining in Canada. “Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada,” Smith posted on social media.

Even though the vote was not explicitly about independence – a point that frustrated separatists – the ballot question nonetheless exposed divisions in Alberta’s politics and raised questions about the durability of national unity.

Delays at roughly 100 of the 1,400 at polling stations across the province pushed results back by more than two hours, but shortly after polls closed on Monday evening the results suggested a decisive win for those looking to remain in Canada.

title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel
text:
A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic Las Vegas hotel.

Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.

Prosecutors said tourist Mitchell Fairbarn hurt and frightened the 27-year-old Chilean flamingo when he took it from its habitat at the Flamingo Las Vegas Hotel and Casino and carried the squawking bird to his room on 3 March. Defense attorney Josh Tomsheck told jurors at trial in a Nevada court that the man deeply regretted the “bad decisions” he made while intoxicated.

After about five hours of deliberations, jurors returned convictions on felony and misdemeanor animal cruelty counts against the Ontario, Canada, man.

Fairbarn remains under house arrest pending a sentencing hearing set for 1 December. He faces up to four years in prison for the felony and possibly six more months for the misdemeanor conviction. Following the verdict, he declined to comment as he left the courtroom with his wife. He showed no visible emotion.

His lawyer also had no comment.

After the incident, the flamingo was mostly unharmed but is more anxious and nervous when being evaluated, said Peachy’s veterinarian, Tiffany Moore, medical director of Lone Mountain Animal Hospital.

Prosecutors told jurors earlier that Fairbarn willfully caused the bird physical pain, noting feathers were found on the hotel floor. Video showed the bird squawking while Fairbarn handled it and prosecutors said Peachy felt pain when it was pulled by its feet.

Video played at the trial showed Fairbarn holding the flamingo in an elevator and carrying it down a hotel hallway at the famous hotel. The Flamingo is one of the oldest hotels on the Las Vegas Strip, and its well-known flamingo habitat also features hummingbirds, turtles, koi and other species.

Peachy was missing some feathers after being taken.

Las Vegas police responded to the scene after security staff reported that someone had taken the flamingo. When Peachy was located, it was missing seven to eight feathers, had blood on its feathers and injuries to its wings, authorities said.

Taking the bird was “dumb” and “fueled by drunkenness”, the defense attorney Tomsheck said. But he added that his client never intended any harm to the bird, a key element in the felony charge.

“He should not have done that, should not have gone into the habitat, shouldn’t have touched a bird, shouldn’t have taken Peachy inside,” Tomsheck said. “The truth is, Mitch was drunk. Mitch was stupid. He made bad decisions.”

Fairbarn could be seen in court at one point with head lowered, hands covering his eyes.

title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff
text:
To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.

But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.

Rather than drawing attention to the incumbent’s alleged misdeeds, many of the programme’s millions of viewers sarcastically took Bolsonaro’s hand-written message as an admission of his own guilt.

Following Sunday night’s debate, Lula supporters from all walks of life have flooded social media with photographs of their own self-descriptions inked on their palms.

John Ulhoa, the guitarist from a pop rock band called Pato Fu, jokingly described himself as a “musician (and a hunk)”.

The Emmy-winning comedian Antonio Tabet introduced himself to his 2.8 million followers on X as an artist.

Carlos Marcio used both palms to portray himself as a cellist and author.

Carla Emanuela Sacramento, an obstetric nurse, posted a photograph of herself clad in personal protective equipment and with the words “primary health care nurse” proudly written on her right palm.

Prominent politicians also jumped on the trend, including Lula’s health minister, the infectious disease specialist Alexandre Padilha, whose palm noted he was a doctor, and Tabata Amaral, who identified as a political scientist and astrophysicist.

All across the country, librarians, oil workers, engineers, journalists, architects, pilots, psychologists, seamstresses, street cleaners, teachers, influencers, and police officers used ballpoint pens to inscribe their professions on to their skin.

Writing on Substack, the Latin America expert James Bosworth called Bolsonaro’s stunt a “critical error” in his bid for power.

“It may have seemed like an inspired pre-debate gimmick. Instead, he gave the world a meme image that will stick with him for the rest of his political career,” Bosworth said, offering politicians a word of advice.

“Don’t write the word ‘corrupto’ on your hand and show it to the audience,” Bosworth suggested.

Bolsonaro, who is the son of the jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, is a professional politician who has long faced corruption accusations, although he denies them and has never been convicted. The 45-year-old senator also has well-documented ties to members of Rio’s mafia underworld and once employed the relatives of the city’s most notorious contract killer, Adriano da Nóbrega. Last week two allies were arrested for alleged involvement with the Red Command drug faction, which Donald Trump recently designated a foreign terrorist organisation. Bolsonaro voiced surprise at those arrests and said the men had the right to prove their innocence.

On Monday, Brazilian media reported that Bolsonaro was being investigated by the federal police as part of a money-laundering inquiry.

title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds
text:
A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study.

The analysis from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems.

A two-year pilot managed by the UK-based charity Cool Earth gave 211 people in three communities in Peru’s Asháninka region six cash transfers of 1,032 Peruvian soles each – roughly equivalent to £2 a day – to spend as they wished.

Over the course of the trial, researchers found almost 90% of participants adopted environmentally beneficial practices, such as collective reforestation, restoration of critical water sources and reductions of forest burning.

They also noted a reduction in food insecurity, which can sometimes prompt forest people to start logging or become involved in environmental crimes. Households unable to afford nutritious food fell from 73% to 26%.

Another reported benefit was reduced migration, with the share of participants forced to leave their homes to find work falling from 43% to 18%. Researchers said this allowed more people to remain and protect the forest.

Dr Nick Langridge, a co-author of the report, said: “The findings suggest that when communities have greater security and autonomy, they are better able to protect the ecosystems they depend on.”

There is increasing recognition of the importance of Indigenous stewardship of the Amazon and other biomes that sequester carbon, shelter biodiversity and provide vital ecological services to the planet. But this role is increasingly difficult as Indigenous lands are threatened by miners, loggers, farmers and land grabbers, and as many of the young people of these often economically poor communities are exposed to the internet or lured away to wealthier cities.

How to sustain, encourage and reward Indigenous stewardship is a hot debate in the international aid and environmental community. Many previous payment schemes came with strings attached, such as the Brazilian government’s bolsa família, which has child education obligations, or bolsa verde, which has conservation activity requirements.

The authors of the new study say the project – which was drawn up with local women’s groups – is the first to offer an unconditional basic income to an Indigenous community in the Amazon.

The lead author, Dr Neil Howard, said: “All of this helps ethical conservation. The incentive to exploit or abandon land is diminished, and people are put front and centre with respect and dignity, which contrasts sharply with the colonial history of conservation and Indigenous policy.”

To boost the impact, the project delivered a voluntary “cash plus” complementary programme of community-led education on finance, conservation and climate change.

title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
text:
In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.

Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.

In Greece, heavy rain and thunderstorms caused severe flooding and one fatality across Rhodes, Evia and the Sporades islands last week. According to the National Observatory of Athens, a station in Rhodes recorded 202mm between 3.30am and 9.50am (UTC) on 14 October. Regional authorities reported more than 30 rescue and extrication operations in response to flooding, while the Greek coastguard said four passenger vehicles were swept into the sea during the storm. On Skiathos, flood waters swept away two cars.

Five deaths were reported due to severe flooding in Istanbul, Turkey, last week. Heavy rain on 14 and 15 October prompted school closures, flight delays, disruptive flooding and landslides across several provinces. According to the Istanbul metropolitan municipality, 242mm of rain was recorded in Beykoz, a district of Istanbul province. Nearly 600 people were rescued after becoming stranded and at least 2,700 people were forced to evacuate their homes.

The Turkish state meteorological service issued further alerts for heavy rain and thunderstorms over the weekend across dozens of provinces, with at least an additional 40-60mm forecast for parts of the Marmara and western Black Sea regions.

title: Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
text:
Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping.

Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has vowed to take by force if necessary.

In one performance, Huang Yi-hao insulted the Chinese leader’s appearance, compared him to Winnie-the-Pooh and tore into his political record.

Prosecutors in New Taipei said on Wednesday that an individual from mainland China who was identified as “K” had paid the five defendants to injure Huang badly enough to require hospitalisation.

The prosecutors said: “This case involves a serious incident in which the Chinese Communist party is suspected of using cross-border suppression tactics to direct lawless elements in our country to suppress dissenting political voices through extreme violence.”

China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to requests for comment.

A GPS tracker was allegedly put on Huang’s scooter months before the attack to identify his daily routines, Taiwan’s Central News Agency said. On 11 September, two defendants drove into Huang’s bike as he rode home, but stopped after hearing Huang scream, prosecutors said.

The comedian was left with a bruised pelvis and the suspects then allegedly pretended to help with an insurance claim in order to send a photo of Huang’s medical certificate to K.

K refused to pay the full sum of NT$450,000 (US$13,900; £10,370) promised to the suspects because Huang’s injuries were only minor, the statement said.

On Wednesday, Huang reposted a video from December 2025 in which he asked the audience to help him by shouting out the name of the person he was about to describe.

In a fast-paced diatribe, the comedian, dressed in a traditional gown, evoked “swept-back hair” and a “plump figure”, and criticised policies on Hong Kong, Covid and the property market. After finishing with an expletive, the crowd chanted back Xi’s name before breaking into applause.

In May, two people were prosecuted after spreading faeces and paint at a Taipei club hours before a Huang show.

Lev Nachman, a professor of political science at National Taiwan University, said: “It is important to remember that what we are reading about is obviously a more extreme case, but there have been threats and acts of violence against critics of the Communist party here in Taiwan for many years.”

Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council said in October that at least 126 individuals had been affected by Chinese transnational repression.

The Guardian has contacted the Chinese foreign ministry for comment.

In a post on Wednesday, Huang said: “If people can be subjected to this kind of treatment simply for criticising the Chinese Communist party when it does not even govern Taiwan, how can we expect to retain our current freedom of speech if the CCP were ever to rule Taiwan?”

title: Shark trapped for a month in South Korean canal is finally freed
text:
In South Korea, they call them jagyeongdan, a word whose meaning sits somewhere between vigilante group and neighbourhood watch. Each night they put on hi-vis vests, picked up their selfie sticks and gathered around the harbour in Busan to keep watch over an unlikely charge: a stranded shark affectionately known as Bukang-i.

On Wednesday, after more than a month in the canal and at the third attempt, the shark was successfully guided out, South Korea’s oceans ministry said. Officials expect her to move into open water in time.

For the month that she was stranded, the group of self-appointed guardians took turns to protect her, patrolling the waterfront at night for visitors who might disturb the animal.

Most are YouTubers who livestreamed the waterway, where the shark became a national celebrity. They stayed up through the night, calling out anyone shining torches or lasers into the water. Some of their videos have been watched hundreds of thousands of times.

“They bring fishing lamps, or the kind of lights people use at a campsite,” said Choi Won-jin, one of the shark’s protectors. He would arrive as the lights went out along the canal and wait for the offenders Koreans online call “lantern villains”.

The shark had been marooned in the canal since 18 September. Named after Bukhang, the Korean name for the city’s North Port, and about 3 metres long, the female dusky shark was one of a species classed as endangered worldwide. More than 1.6 million visitors came to see her, the city said, at a park that used to draw about 2,000 people on a busy Saturday.

Authorities had twice tried to guide her back out to sea and failed. Until she left, the shark remained in the canal, drawing crowds by day and leaving a handful of men to keep watch after dark. They patrolled the canal’s park to check everything was in order, ate snacks as the night went by, and shared their grievances on air about the behaviour they witnessed.

“We’re ordinary members of the public,” said Choi, who has had a YouTube channel for 10 years and covers trending issues in South Korea. “So we have no choice but to put it nicely, and get them to understand as best we can.”

“Don’t, please don’t switch the torch on,” said one of them, a YouTuber who lived nearby and went by the name Na Tae-soo. Most people complied, he said. “The animal thrashes about at night because of the torches, and it’s dangerous.”

His footage captured the shark twisting sharply away from a beam of light at 2am and striking the side of the canal. The national institute of fisheries science later confirmed an abrasion on her snout and said a visitor’s torch was likely to have startled the shark into injury.

Korean media reported that 105 officials from seven agencies watched over her, with a team on standby to reach the water within three minutes. Choi disputed this, saying that after dark it was almost up to him and the others.

title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
text:
Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.

China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.

China’s economy has now grown by 4.6% in the first nine months of the year, putting it on track to hit the government’s 2026 target of 4.5%-5% growth without extra stimulus measures.

Industrial production rose 5.5% in September, up from 5.2% in August, while retail sales only increased 1.1%, up from 0.4%.

Duncan Wrigley, the chief China economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said Beijing’s policymakers were likely to conclude that their efforts to stabilise headline growth in the third quarter were successful.

“Headline industrial production rose in September partly as coalmines resumed operations after safety inspections prompted by a major accident. Manufacturing output growth remained robust at 6.0% year on year in September, buoyed up by stronger export demand for electronics, AI-related equipment and autos,” Wrigley said.

“Hi-tech manufacturing output continues to outperform traditional sectors, as China climbs the value-added ladder,” Wrigley added.

However, fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% over the first nine months, property investment tumbled by 20.6%, and infrastructure spending remained weak.

Data last week showed that China’s exports surged by more than a third in September, lifted by a rise in shipments of electronics related to AI.

“This pickup in GDP growth mainly reflects ongoing export strength on the global AI/tech boom, more than offsetting drags from the Iran conflict and ongoing weakness in domestic demand,” said analysts at ABN Amro.

title: Three deaths from float crushes raise safety concerns over Japanese festivals
text:
There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.

Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.

He died less than two weeks after a 51-year-old man was crushed beneath a wooden float he was riding at one of the annual Danjiri festivals held in southern Osaka prefecture. The same day, a 48-year-old man was killed in a similar accident at a Danjiri event in a nearby town. Police said 16 people were injured in the incidents.

The accidents occurred when the floats, which can weigh up to 4 tonnes, toppled as they were being pulled at speed around tight corners by hundreds of men, police said. The turns, known as yarimawashi, are a highlight of the festivals, originally held to pray for good autumn harvests.

It is not clear if Nabae lost his balance or if the contraption toppled on to him, according to police in Saijo, where the festival has been held annually since the Edo period (1603-1868).

Media reports said 11 floats, each weighing as much as 3 tonnes, were lined up side by side at the time of the accident.

The annual Saijo festivals, featuring more than 100 floats, are held to thank Shinto deities for plentiful grain crops, the Jiji news agency said.

Saijo’s mayor, Mitsuyoshi Ochi, voiced shock and sadness at Nabae’s death. “Just when we were about to work together to build a new administration for Saijo, this tragedy occurred. I still can’t believe it. I offer my heartfelt condolences,” he said in a statement.

In February, two people died in a crush at the “naked man festival” in Okayama, where as many as 10,000 men dressed in fundoshi loincloths squeeze into the grounds of a temple and compete to seize a pair of sacred wooden sticks thrown into the crowd by the head priest. The two men who succeed are declared “lucky men” for the year.

title: Amelia Earhart researchers leave remote atoll empty-handed after ‘plane debris’ found to be a clump of trees
text:
A US expedition that voyaged to a remote Pacific island in the hope of solving the mystery of what happened to pioneering pilot Amelia Earhart has said an object they suspected to be her plane was a clump of washed-up trees.

“Unfortunately, we weren’t able to find that smoking gun,” said Steve Schultz of Purdue University, standing on the sand in front of a blue lagoon on the atoll of Nikumaroro, about halfway between Australia and Hawaii.

Earhart and her navigator Fred Noonan vanished in 1937 during their attempt to circumnavigate the globe at the equator, leading to one of the largest air and sea searches in history. Nearly 90 years later, people are still looking, with Nikumaroro in the archipelago country of Kiribati emerging as a leading candidate for where they might have crash-landed.

Previous visits to the uninhabited atoll have found signs of a castaway camp, a 1930s-era woman’s shoe and other tantalising evidence attributed to the celebrity aviator, including glass from a cosmetics freckle cream jar.

The latest mission stemmed from 2020 satellite images showing an elongated, white object lying in the shallows of the island, near a sandy outcrop called the Taraia Peninsula.

Other longtime Earhart explorers quickly identified it as a fallen tree, but Richard Pettigrew, who heads the nonprofit Archaeological Legacy Institute, found other images, including aerial video showing what he suspected to be a metallic glint in the water.

After a multi-day voyage by ship and subsequent delays due to bad weather, the 17-person expedition managed to pass through the coral-encircled atoll and set up tents to conduct four days of research, including metal detecting. The crew was forced to sleep offshore, partly due to massive land-dwelling coconut crabs, known as “robber crabs” for their inquisitiveness when searching for food.

By Monday, Purdue University confirmed in a statement that the “visual anomaly” was “likely a collection of large trees deposited along the peninsula’s sandspit”.

It said the glint was part of a natural process. “The fragment’s reflective surface, long associated with the idea that the object was a metallic substance, was due to its carbonate veneer. Other items found by the team were similarly coated with a shiny concretized amalgam of coral sand.”

The trip was partially sponsored by the university in Indiana, where Earhart once taught and mentored young female pilots, and which helped fund her modified Lockheed Electra 10-E, known as her “flying laboratory”.

“While we know this is disappointing to many, including us, this mission adds a new chapter in the quest to find the ultimate answer to the mystery of what happened to Earhart during her attempt to circumnavigate the globe nearly nine decades ago,” the university statement said.

title: Australian politicians say they are paying thousands for their own security upgrades amid rising threats
text:
Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines.

The Labor government and politicians across the parliament are still considering how they will respond when they return to Canberra next week, with ideas being floated including a new committee on MPs’ safety, greater resources for police, and motions of condolence for Haines, who lost both her legs after Monday’s incident. Renewed calls from the crossbench for reforms to question time and the tone of debate in parliament are unlikely to be taken up by the major parties.

In safety briefings with the Australian federal police and Asio granted to Labor, Coalition and crossbench MPs on Wednesday, security of homes and electorate offices was a common concern, according to Guardian Australia interviews with 10 MPs. While a broad review of safety and security is unlikely at this stage, multiple MPs across the political spectrum told Guardian Australia they had spent thousands of dollars of their own money to install safety features based on the advice of the federal police.

Federal ministers receive stronger security assistance, but numerous backbenchers said they felt under-resourced, saying many angry constituents may see all politicians as a homogenous group, and may not differentiate between cabinet members and ordinary local MPs.

“People are getting activated now because they see us as part of the government. We represent the system to them, as much as anyone else,” independent Monique Ryan said.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

Two years ago, the AFP recorded 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against office holders. Last year, that increased to 1,067. On Wednesday, police arrested a man after he allegedly caused a disturbance at a Perth electorate office and was reported to have made verbal threats “while in possession of what has been described as nunchucks”. No one was injured as a result, Western Australia police said.

‘Not well protected’

A number of politicians asked to speak anonymously to discuss reflections from the briefings. While many praised the AFP’s response when their staff contacted them – for instance, to seek advice on holding public events – some said they had received less timely assistance from local police when they requested help, such as to respond to aggressive visitors.

Numerous MPs said they did not want security guards or armed escorts for themselves in public, but that they felt alarmed for the safety of their homes and families.

Some said they would feel more comfortable with cameras and floodlights at home, and had decided to pay for their own upgrades after not being offered such features in risk assessments conducted by security agencies. title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic
text:
The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance.

Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people.

But the latest evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting a penicillin allergy do not have one.

The changes to the Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy guidelines, which have been published in the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology, give the first peer-reviewed and updated advice to GPs and other health professionals about how to diagnose and manage the allergy, and when to refer to a specialist.

Prof Michaela Lucas, a clinical immunologist, said misdiagnosis occurs for a number of reasons, with people sometimes experiencing a rash or nausea after taking penicillin and assuming it’s an allergy, or doctors wanting to be cautious and recording side-effects as allergies.

Other people were told by a parent that they suffered a reaction when they were a child and carry that diagnosis through to adulthood without questioning it, she said, while some side-effects may also be due to the illness itself and not the medicine.

Penicillin is an important antibiotic option, as it treats common infections, said Lucas, a professor at the University of Western Australia’s medical school.

“It is also what is known as a narrow spectrum antibiotic, which means it is targeted at the bug specifically causing the infection,” she said.

“Once you have to avoid narrow classes of drugs, you have to use broader spectrum antibiotics which have a bigger impact of your gut microbiome as they are associated with also killing good bacteria and allowing superbugs to come in and take residency.”

Superbugs are strains of bacteria that are highly resistant to multiple standard treatments.

“Antimicrobial resistance matters beyond the individual patient, because resistant bacteria can spread between people and through communities,” Lucas said.

“If someone develops a serious infection that is resistant to several antibiotics, doctors can be left with very limited treatment options.”

Dr Nick Cooling, the chair of the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners’ allergy special interest group, said the guidelines were based on the latest evidence, and a consensus report from a range of medical specialities.

He hopes the guidance will cut health costs in the community and ease the burden on immunologists.

“We know that people who have a penicillin allergy label go to hospital more,” he said.

“They spend longer in hospital, and they also cost the system more.”

This is because of more treatments needing to be trialled, side-effects from those treatments, and delays in finding alternative treatments.

title: Soft-spoken David Pocock has big ambitions – but first he wants politicians to ‘double down’ on kindness
text:
He’s six foot tall and full of muscle, but David Pocock’s real strength is often sounding like the most sensible, commonsense voice in the room.

At his first speech to the National Press Club on Wednesday, he said he wasn’t launching a bid for prime minister – no matter how much some people might like the softly spoken senator to have more say in federal politics.

Indeed, Pocock said he was already thinking about life after politics, admitting “you can’t do this for ever”. But before the full-time whistle on his parliamentary career, the former rugby star has a match against his toughest opponent yet: the two-party system.

“I want to be part of building a political system that actually delivers for Australians, no matter who is prime minister,” the ACT senator said.

“I see an opportunity at the next election for a new kind of community political collective … I want to use what I’ve learned over the past four-and-a-half years to help.”

He called for a higher calibre of politics after the alleged attack on the independent Indi MP, Helen Haines. He branded parliament’s question time a “disgrace”, urging a “better standard” among colleagues “to take some of the edge off it”.

Speaking directly about Haines, he said parliament must “meet this [alleged] attack on you by doubling down on the values you represent” – listing transparency, accountability and kindness.

In front of staff and allies – including the ACT politician Thomas Emerson, Pocock’s former staffer and lookalike, as well as the Cheek Media founder and Grayndler independent candidate, Hannah Ferguson – he called for three key policy reforms:

A 25% tax on gas exports, which he said could fund anything from boosting welfare to health reforms and aged care.

A 5% levy on datacentres to capture more benefits from the AI boom.

Transparency reforms to shine a light on lobbyists, secret meetings with politicians and vested interests.

Just two months of gas tax revenue would pay for 100,000 home support packages, while prosthetic eyes and noses for cancer victims would be paid for in three hours, he said. Pocock recounted the moment a woman sat sobbing in his office, so destitute on the miserable jobseeker allowance that she ate dog food because she hadn’t eaten meat in so long.

“A 25% gas export tax could help change that, allowing us to have a social security system that keeps people above the poverty line,” he said.

All politicians have these stories, even if not all of them talk about them with such emotion. Politics is a series of choices and priorities and, presented by Pocock in this way, the choice not to fund welfare boosts or aged care or cancer care is hard to justify.

Asked later about calls for budget discipline and cutting spending, Pocock replied instantly: “You can make cuts, or you can grow revenue.”

“I don’t understand why we’re slugging everyday Aussies and yet we’re happy to export gas for free.”

title: No bail for alleged Helen Haines attacker as police chief warns of Australia’s ‘febrile’ political environment
text:
The head of the Australian federal police has condemned a “febrile” political environment that has seen one person charged every week over the alleged threatening of MPs, as Victoria announces new steps to protect politicians.

But the AFP and Victoria police insist they had no intelligence to suggest 43-year-old Brendan Nugent would go on to allegedly drive a Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP Helen Haines in a targeted attack.

Haines had one leg amputated after the alleged attack. Doctors had worked to save her second leg, but it was also amputated, her husband, Phil Haines, said at a press conference on Wednesday. Haines was in a stable condition, he said.

Nugent appeared at the Wangaratta magistrates court on Wednesday morning on charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and a federal offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official, along with cannabis possession.

In court, Nugent looked downcast in a grey jumper and stared straight ahead. The Tarrawingee man did not request bail, and will remain in custody until a committal mention on 4 February.

Magistrate Allison Vaughan noted Nugent had mental health and neurological concerns, and that this was his first time in custody. She asked for a mental health professional to see Nugent immediately after his court appearance.

His lawyer, Chirag Patel, said his client was not on any prescribed medication and was not withdrawing from any substances. Patel said Nugent was also suffering from concussion and idiopathic transverse myelitis – a rare inflammatory disorder of the spinal cord.

Further charges considered

At an earlier press conference in Melbourne, Victoria police’s chief commissioner, Mike Bush, said investigators were considering whether to lodge further charges against Nugent.

“That’s always a consideration,” Bush said. “Of course, we have to locate and follow the evidence, but this is a very serious and tragic incident, and we will be looking at all serious charges.”

Bush also said: “There was nothing known to us that would have arisen, or piqued our interest, or given any indication that [Nugent] was an immediate threat.”

At the same press conference, the AFP commissioner, Krissy Barrett, was asked whether her team was aware of Nugent’s social media posts, which included references to conspiracy theories and conflict in the Middle East.

“We didn’t have any specific intelligence that would have indicated something as atrocious as happened on Monday afternoon,” Barrett said.

“I can confirm we had no holdings or no intelligence to suggest that there was any threat to MP Haines.”

Bush said Victoria police had deployed more staff to Wangaratta to assure the local community, but said he was confident this was an isolated incident.

title: CMFRI launches open-sea mussel longline farming unit at Vizhinjam
text:
The ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) unit at Vizhinjam here has launched its first full-fledged open-sea mussel longline farming unit.

The initiative - supported by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India, under the ‘Development of pilot-scale open-sea eco-mussel farms in India: a Blue Growth Project’ - is aimed at developing sustainable mussel farming technologies and creating additional livelihood opportunities for coastal fishing communities.

Shashi Tharoor, MP, launched the project at Vizhinjam on Wednesday. The project is being implemented in collaboration with the local ‘Vizhinjam Mungal Thozhilali Kshema Sangom.’

ICAR-CMFRI’s Vizhinjam Regional Centre said it has developed advanced mussel hatchery and micro-nursery technologies, enabling large-scale production of mussel seed and reducing dependence on natural seed resources.

The project is being launched at Vizhinjam following successful preliminary farming trials along the Kanyakumari coast. Building on these results, the Vizhinjam unit incorporates 20 specially designed 300-litre HDPE floats, parallel mainlines, suspended mussel culture ropes and an anchoring system.

The demonstration will assess mussel growth, production potential and economic viability under local open-sea conditions, with the active participation of the traditional diving community, ICAR-CMFRI officials said.

title: Local body polls in Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP welcomes Supreme Court directions, urges SEC to ensure free and fair elections
text:
Welcoming the Supreme Court’s directions on the local body elections in Andhra Pradesh, YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy on Wednesday urged the State Election Commission (SEC) to exercise its powers to ensure free and fair polls.

The apex court on Wednesday held that the YSRCP had made out a prima facie case in its plea seeking an extension of time to file nominations for the urban local body elections in Andhra Pradesh. It directed the State Election Commission to postpone the publication of the final list of candidates till October 25.

Addressing the media at the YSRCP’s central office at Tadepalli, Mr. Ramakrishna Reddy alleged that attacks on the opposition candidates, obstruction of nominations and tearing of nomination papers continued, despite the court’s intervention.

He claimed that 76 incidents, including attacks, police-assisted detentions, house arrests, threats and seizure or destruction of nomination papers, were reported from 11 districts on Wednesday. He said the YSRCP would bring the latest incidents to the Supreme Court’s notice.

Welcoming the court’s directions on complaints concerning municipal elections, he said the SEC should act against officials allegedly favouring the Telugu Desam Party (TDP). He urged the SEC to obtain reports from the District Collectors and Superintendents of Police and ensure CCTV surveillance at the nomination centres.

Mr. Ramakrishna Reddy alleged that opposition candidates were facing pressure to withdraw nominations, threats of false criminal cases and obstruction during scrutiny. According to him, complaints to the SEC and police authorities had failed to resolve the problems, forcing the party to approach the Supreme Court.

The YSRCP leader accused the A.P. government of attempting to blame the opposition for the violence.

He maintained that the YSRCP workers were exercising restraint and relying on legal remedies. The SEC and the Director-General of Police were expected to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions and submit the required compliance report, he said.

“The YSRCP has faith in the judiciary. We expect that the electoral process be conducted in accordance with the law,” he said.

Meanwhile, YSRCP leaders demanded that the opposition party candidates be provided with protection and that action be taken against the officials resorting to partisan conduct and acting under political influence.

YSRCP MLC Lella Appi Reddy, after submitting a representation to the SEC, said irregularities related to nomination for ZPTC and MPTC elections were recurring.

title: Meira Kumar entitled to compensation for land acquired by government, says Patna High Court
text:
The Patna High Court has delivered a verdict in favour of former Lok Sabha Speaker and former Deputy Prime Minister Jagjivan Ram’s daughter, Meira Kumar ordering that she was entitled to compensation for the land acquired by the Bihar government.

The single Bench order stated she is entitled to receive compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. Justice Khatim Reza, in an order on October 6, quashed the District Collector’s order that had attempted to seize Patna land by unilaterally cancelling the family’s 60-year-old land records.

The dispute pertained to land measuring approximately 18 Kathas and 10 Dhurs (approx. 0.56 acres) situated at Mainpura locality in Patna, which had been acquired by the State in Land Acquisition Case No. 50 of 1975-76 for construction of a drainage channel under the Bengal Embankment Act.

Although possession of the land was taken by the authorities and the public project was executed decades ago, compensation was never paid either to the original landholder, Indrani Devi, or subsequently, to her successor and daughter, Ms. Kumar.

Collector’s order

During the pendency of the proceedings, the Collector, Patna, passed an order dated 12.04.2023 cancelling the Jamabandi standing in favour of the petitioner’s family and declaring the land as Ghairmazarua Aam land (public wasteland). The legality of that order was also placed under challenge before the High Court.

“This court is of the view that order dated 12.04.2023 passed in Jamabandi Cancellation Appeal Case No. 1 of 2012-13 by the District Collector, Patna is not fit to stand in the eye of law. Therefore, the same is held to be illegal without jurisdiction and accordingly quashed. The Jamabandi created in favour of the mother of the petitioner is restored and it is held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the Act of 2013,” the court ordered.

The court ruled that Section 4(h) of the Bihar Land Reforms (B.L.R.) Act, 1950, applies strictly to land transactions made after January 1, 1946. Because the initial settlement was validly granted by the ex-landlord in 1941, the Collector had zero authority to annul the title.

​The court also slammed the Collector for ignoring his own State-appointed three-man committee report (submitted in 2016), which had explicitly confirmed the 1941 settlement date and warned that Section 4(h) was legally inapplicable.

‘Can’t override sale deeds’

​The Bench noted that Survey Khatiyan entries over a century old are merely historical snapshots and do not override 60-plus years of registered sale deeds, regular mutation, and tax receipts accepted by the State.

​”Long-standing Jamabandi created in favour of a person cannot be cancelled in a summary proceeding. If the State wishes to challenge a pre-1946 title, the proper remedy is to approach a competent Civil Court rather than executing a summary cancellation via revenue proceedings,

title: ULB polls in Andhra Pradesh: SEC orders strict implementation of Supreme Court’s directions
text:
Andhra Pradesh State Election Commissioner (SEC) Anil Chandra Punetha has directed the Collectors and Superintendents of Police of seven districts of Kadapa, Annamayya, Tirupati, Anantapur, Prakasam, Palnadu, and Markapuram, where filing of nominations for elections to the Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) was marred by violent clashes, to strictly implement the orders issued by the ​Supreme Court on October 21.

The SEC stated that the election process in all Municipal Corporations and Municipalities would continue as per schedule, except 19 Corporations and Municipalities in the above districts due to large-scale complaints of intimidation and physical attacks.

Conducting elections in these ULBs would be subject to a decision to be taken by the SEC.

In a video conference with the Collectors and SPs along with SEC Secretary A. Mallikarjuna, Additional DGP (L&O) N. Madhusudhan Reddy and Inspector General of Police B. Raja Kumari on Wednesday, Mr. Punetha said steps must be taken to implement the Supreme Court’s directions immediately.

He said the SEC would take appropriate decisions after receiving the Supreme Court order, on the basis of the reports submitted by the District Collectors and SPs. He directed the officers to take steps to prevent the repeat of the incidents that occurred so far during the filing of nominations for elections to the Mandal and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs and ZPTCs).

Th enomination process began on October 21 and is scheduled to end on October 23.

With regard to the rule that candidates should submit ‘No Objection Certificates’ and ‘No Dues Certificates’ at the time of filing nominations for MPTC and ZPTC elections, the SEC clarified that instructions were issued to the officials to issue the certificates within 24 hours only for the purpose of elections.

It would therefore not be a constraint. He advised the officials concerned not to impose additional conditions contrary to the election code that put the eligible candidates to trouble in filing nominations.

title: No passes, no problem: Dasara fans find their vantage points
text:
Such is the public fascination with the Jamboo Savari that people without passes or tickets to watch the procession from within the Mysuru Palace premises began reserving seats along the stepped viewing galleries at Bannimantap, along the procession route, as early as four days before the Dasara finale.

The stepped galleries, stretching from Bamboo Bazaar to the Highway Circle, were created years ago to facilitate public viewing of the procession. With thousands expected to throng the route to catch a glimpse of the grand spectacle, people went all out to secure their preferred spots well in advance.

Mats and carpets were spread across the steps to mark their chosen places and prevent others from occupying them. People took turns guarding their spots, keeping watch from dawn to dusk and through the night to ensure that their vantage points remained undisturbed.

This year, however, trees and heritage buildings along the route were out of bounds for spectators, with the police taking strict measures to prevent people from climbing them on safety grounds.

The enthusiasm was evident even during rehearsals in the run-up to the finale, when large crowds gathered along the route to watch the elephants.

The eagerness to witness the iconic procession translated into a massive turnout on Vijayadashami, with people jostling for space along the route to catch a glimpse of the caparisoned elephants and the golden howdah.

title: 14 candidates in fray for Guntur Mayor post; election symbols allotted
text:
As many as 14 candidates, including nominees of major political parties and independents, are in the fray for the Guntur Municipal Corporation (GMC) Mayor post in the urban local body elections scheduled for October 28.

Guntur Municipal Corporation Commissioner and Additional Election Authority K. Mayur Ashok announced the final list of candidates on Wednesday, October 21, after the deadline for withdrawal of nominations ended, in accordance with the election schedule.

The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has fielded Kovelamudi Lakshmi Aparna, who has been allotted the bicycle symbol. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) candidate, Tadikonda Alivelu Venkata Nagapadmasridevi, has been allotted the ceiling fan symbol.

Gudavalli Manikumari is contesting on behalf of the Bahujan Samajwadi Party (BSP) with the elephant symbol, while Chopparapu Padmavathi is the Congress candidate with the hand symbol.

The other candidates representing political parties are Degala Mounika of the Amaravati Party, allotted the wardrobe symbol; Pathan Muneer Sultana of the Navarang Congress Party, allotted the gas cylinder symbol; Pendyala Madhavi of the Navodayam Party, allotted the bat symbol; Shaik Khader Bee of the Navataram Party, allotted the coconut symbol; and Shaik Mohammed Zahurunnisa Begum of the Republican Party of India, allotted the electric pole symbol.

Five candidates are contesting as independents. They are Kandepalli Aparna, allotted the refrigerator symbol; Ganji Suvarna Latha, allotted the coat symbol; Jarugumalli Jyothi, allotted the cutting pliers symbol; Manne Sudha, allotted the chessboard symbol; and Sivalasetti Pavani, allotted the camera symbol.

title: Thiruvananthapuram Corporation’s dog shelters face opposition from nearby panchayats
text:
The Thiruvananthapuram Corporation’s plan to shift stray dogs caught from the city to shelters outside the city limits has not been progressing well, with yet another panchayat adjacent to the capital city opposing the setting up of dog shelters in its locality.

Early in February, the Karumkulam grama panchayat had opposed a dog shelter in its area, which it termed illegal as it is being run without permission from the panchayat. Now, the Kuttichal panchayat has come out against another private dog shelter in which around 200 dogs from the Corporation are being housed. The local body has issued a stop memo. The Thiruvananthapuram chapter of People For Animals has alleged ill-treatment of stray dogs at the facility.

Left Democratic Front (LDF) Parliamentary Party leader in the Corporation council S.P. Deepak. who visited the shelter in Kuttichal, said: “it was neither designed as a standard dog shelter nor does it function as one, rather it used to be a poultry farm. The individual running the facility has only a breeder’s licence and has not obtained a licence from the panchayat. The living conditions there are cruel. Approximately 200 dogs are being kept on the premises. I saw the dead body of a dog too, which was not removed from the shelter,” he said.

The LDF has alleged that the highly secretive manner in which the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme is being managed, without adhering to any of the guidelines, is suspicious. Although Opposition councillors have raised this issue multiple times during council meetings, the Mayor has consistently evaded providing a clear response, said Mr. Deepak.

According to an RTI response, over 1,300 dogs have been captured by the Corporation in three months from May. Yet, there are only 301 dogs currently accounted for across the Corporation’s two ABC centres and the shelter at Kuttichal. The status of the remaining 1,000 or so dogs remains unclear, says Mr. Deepak.

Karumkulam grama panchayat president Pushpam Vincent said that those running the dog shelter had promised in February to shift the facility within six months, but no step has been taken yet.

Meanwhile, Corporation Veterinarian Sreerag Jayan said that though the panchayats had opposed the dog shelters, no decision on their future has been taken yet. “We cannot release the dogs that are caught back into public spaces, near hospitals or schools or bus stations as it can become contempt of Supreme Court orders. The Corporation is conducting inspections every week and providing food. Some of the dogs in the shelters are obviously weak because these are diseased dogs caught from the streets,” he said.

title: Ladakh administration dissolves hill council in Kargil, announces panchayat elections on November 21
text:
The Ladakh administration on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) dissolved the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC)-Kargil and announced panchayat elections on November 21 in the cold desert region.

An official said the Ladakh State Election Commission (SEC) proposed to hold the Panchayat General Elections across all panchayat halqas on November 21, 2026. The nominations will close on November 2, the official said. A Model Code of Conduct (MCC) has come into force with immediate effect.

The Ladakh administration has notified 100 elected constituencies for the eight districts of the region, with Leh comprising 22 seats, Kargil 21, Sankoo 13, Changthang 10, Nubra nine, Sham nine, Zanskar nine and Drass seven.

Officials said the number of elected constituencies will also “be the basis for the constitution of” the LAHDCs in eight districts of the region. Earlier, Ladakh had only two hill councils for Kargil and Leh districts. However, the L-G administration has created six additional districts in the region.

The last elections for panchayats and municipalities were held in Ladakh in 2018, when the region was part of Jammu and Kashmir. Ladakh was carved out as a Union Territory in 2019 from the Kashmir division of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir.

LAHDC Kargil dissolved

Meanwhile, the administration of Ladakh also dissolved the erstwhile LAHDC Kargil “with immediate effect following the reorganisation of districts”. The elections to the council in Kargil were held in 2023 and the body would have completed five years in 2028. The elections were won by the National Conference-Congress alliance that won 24 seats, with the NC winning 12 seats and the Congress 10 seats. Two seats were won by the BJP and two by Independent candidates.

The latest developments came at a time when the Centre was holding talks with the representatives of Ladakh over the demands of Statehood and Sixth Schedule. The recent round of talks held in Leh on October 15 saw growing differences between the stakeholders. The Leh Apex Body (LAB) and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), after examining the fresh 32-page draft proposal presented by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), “categorically rejected the draft proposal in principle and said it represents a significant departure from the assurances and commitments made during previous meetings of the sub-committee”.

Official sources said the next round of talks between the Centre and Ladakh’s key civil society bodies, the LAB and the KDA, was scheduled for October 22 in New Delhi.

Saxena reacts

Ladakh governor Vinai Kumar Saxena termed the election announcement as “a historic milestone for grassroots democracy in Ladakh”. “Under LAHDC (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, I have officially notified 100 constituencies for the eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils. This almost doubles the number of councillors from the existing 52 to 100, across our newly structured councils,” said Mr. Saxena.

title: Kannada film stars add glamour to Dasara procession
text:
Personalities from the Kannada film industry, including actors, producers and directors, added a touch of glamour to the grand Dasara procession in Mysuru on Wednesday, drawing cheers from thousands of spectators lining the route.

In what was a rare sight in recent years, a galaxy of Kannada film stars participated in the procession following a suggestion by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who authorised the Karnataka Film Chamber of Commerce to bring the stars on board to enhance the grandeur of the event.

The film personalities travelled in two open-top buses, waving to the cheering crowds as popular songs from yesteryear Kannada films and contemporary cinema played along the procession route. The contingent brought together veteran actors, established stars and emerging talent from the industry.

Led by veteran actor Jayamala, chairperson of the Karnataka Film Chamber of Commerce, the buses, decorated with images of prominent personalities from the Kannada film world, moved along the procession route, adding a cinematic touch to the cultural spectacle.

V. Ravichandran, Ramesh Aravind, Golden Star Ganesh, Murali, Prajwal Devaraj, Sharan, Neenasam Satheesh, Ragini, Pooja Gandhi, Prem, Srinagar Kitty, Mukhyamantri Chandru, Doddanna and several others greeted the crowds from the buses.

Popular actor Kiccha Sudeep watched the procession from the gallery in front of the Mysuru palace, where the Chief Minister and other dignitaries, including Ministers, witnessed the grand finale.

title: Jamboo Savari: Journalists protest police restrictions
text:
Journalists staged a protest inside the Mysuru palace ahead of the Jamboo Savari on Vijayadashami, alleging that police restrictions prevented them from reaching their designated locations in time to cover the event.

The journalists, who arrived in a vehicle belonging to the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR), were initially stopped near the Brahmapuri entrance to the palace.

After an altercation, they managed to enter the palace premises but were stopped again before they could reach the North Gate.

As the journalists protested against the restrictions, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Law and Order) Harsha Priyamvad rushed to the spot and facilitated their passage. T.S. Srivatsa, Krishnaraja MLA, was also present, and criticised the hurdles placed in the way of journalists covering the event.

Agitated over the conduct of the police personnel, the journalists staged a sit-in on the path leading to the North Gate, prompting Director General of Police M.A. Saleem to intervene.

Senior police officials said the confusion over the entry of journalists had arisen because police personnel from outside Mysuru had been deployed for duty at the palace.

Meanwhile, K. Shivakumar, MLC, condemned the alleged misbehaviour of police personnel towards journalists covering the Jamboo Savari and demanded disciplinary action against officials who had allegedly obstructed them from discharging their duties.

He questioned the need for the police to stop the vehicle, which carried an official vehicle pass and the journalists, who possessed valid duty passes issued by the Mysuru City Police Commissioner’s office.

In a letter to the Chief Secretary and the Director General of Police and Inspector General of Police, Mr. Shivakumar, who had also worked as a journalist, said media personnel had faced considerable difficulties owing to inadequate arrangements for covering this year’s Mysuru Dasara celebrations.

Traditionally, journalists were allowed to enter the palace premises through the Karikallu Thotti gate to cover the Jamboo Savari. This year, however, the Police Department designated the Brahmapuri gate as the entry point. Police personnel deployed there allegedly denied entry to journalists despite possessing official duty passes issued by the Mysuru City Police Commissioner’s office, he said.

Meanwhile, the Mysuru District Journalists’ Association (MDJA) too has condemned the alleged arrogance of the police personnel, who prevented the journalists from discharging their duties. MDJA president K. Deepak and General Secretary Dharmapura Narayan, in a statement here, have sought police action and has sought disciplinary action against the police personnel involved.

title: Vajra Mushti Kalaga cancelled at Mysuru Dasara; wrestlers blame police restrictions
text:
The traditional Vajra Mushti Kalaga, an ancient form of martial combat in which two wrestlers strike each other on the shaved head with knuckledusters, was cancelled on Vijayadashami after the police allegedly prevented some wrestlers from entering the Mysuru Palace premises in time.

The Vajra Mushti Kalaga is a centuries-old sporting tradition patronised by the Wadiyars of Mysuru. Wrestlers from the Jetti community enter the arena and strike their opponents with knuckledusters. The wrestler who draws blood from the opponent’s head first is declared the winner.

The event is traditionally held ahead of the Vijaya Yatra and Banni Pooja as part of the private ceremonial procession conducted by the titular head of the erstwhile Mysuru royal family.

On Wednesday (October 21), however, the traditional wrestling bout was called off after some wrestlers reportedly failed to reach the arena in time. A member of the Jetti community blamed the delay on the police allegedly preventing them from entering the palace premises.

“We had reached the palace on time, but the police refused to let us in. They said our passes had to be scanned and kept us waiting,” the community member alleged.

While wrestlers selected for the bouts from Bengaluru and Chamarajanagar managed to enter the palace, those from Mysuru and Ramanagara could not reach the arena in time, another member of the Jetti community said.

According to sources, the palace authorities did not want to let the auspicious time for the Vijaya Yatra pass and decided to cancel the Vajra Mushti Kalaga and proceed with the private procession.

title: Jamboo Savari brings curtains on Mysuru Dasara
text:
Curtains came down on the 11-day Mysuru Dasara celebrations with the grand Jamboo Savari on Wednesday, as a sea of humanity thronged the city centre to catch a glimpse of the iconic Vijayadashami procession, marking the culmination of the cultural extravaganza.

All roads led to the City of Palaces for the Dasara finale, with the famed golden howdah and caparisoned elephants emerging as the cynosure of all eyes. The colourful and awe-inspiring celebrations drew lakhs of visitors.

Nandi Dhwaja puja

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, accompanied by his Cabinet colleagues and local elected representatives, set the stage for the Dasara procession by performing the customary ‘Nandi Dwaja’ puja at the Balarama Gate of the palace around 1.40 p.m.

The puja was followed by the ceremonial procession of elephants, with veteran tusker Abhimanyu featuring as the ‘Nishane Ane’, followed by eight other caparisoned elephants guided by their mahouts. The procession began around 2.20 p.m.

This was Abhimanyu’s final Dasara appearance following his retirement from active Dasara duties on attaining the age of 60. His participation marked a ceremonial farewell to the legendary tusker, whose admirers and animal lovers had sought a fitting send-off in recognition of his contribution to the festivities. Abhimanyu had carried the golden howdah for six consecutive years.

Cultural grandeur

Other elephants in the contingent included Gopi, Mahendra, Lakshmi, Sugreeva, Chaitra and Srirama. As the elephants moved along the procession route amid loud cheers from the crowds, cultural troupes and tableaux arrived one after another, showcasing Karnataka’s cultural diversity and heritage. Artists representing different art forms from across the State and tableaux representing various districts captivated the spectators.

Tableaux from other States, including one from Tamil Nadu showcasing the Shore Temple of Mahabalipuram and Jallikattu, were among the special attractions this year. Cultural troupes from the Northeast and a Tibetan settlement in Karnataka also participated.

Sandalwood plays a part in festivities

Another highlight was the participation of a team from the Kannada film industry, including V. Ravichandran, Ramesh Aravind, Ganesh, Pooja Gandhi, Shruthi, Sharan, Murali, among others. Veteran actor Jaimala led the team of artists in two open-top buses, drawing loud cheers from their fans. Actor ‘’Kiccha’’ Sudeep was also present. Medal-winning sportspersons from the State joined the procession in another open-top bus.

Tableaux representing the Indian Army and Navy attracted considerable attention, while bands from the defence forces played stirring tunes as the procession moved along the route.

After nearly two hours of cultural pageantry, the most eagerly awaited moment came with the arrival of 54-year-old tusker Prashanth carrying the iconic golden howdah bearing the idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari. The flower-bedecked, 750-kg howdah was the centre of attraction as

title: Mysuru: Tableaux captivate spectators at Jamboo Savari
text:
Featuring the attractive tableaux portraying the regional specialities, cultural heritage and social messages, the grand Jamboo Savari held on the premises of Mysuru Palace on Wednesday kept spectators spellbound throughout the procession.

The procession featured 53 tableaux and 46 traditional folk art forms and lasted around two to three hours. It began with a Nadaswaram performance, followed by the tableaux presented by several zilla panchayats of the State, boards, authorities, Mysuru zoo, Indian Army, Indian Navy, Air Force and Central Government Institutions. Tableaux representing the art and culture of Tamil Nadu and Kerala were also part of the procession.

The Mandya Zilla Panchayat tableau, titled ‘Asmithe-Unveiling of Women’s Power’ conveyed the message of discrimination free society and equal opportunity to women. Depiction of a mother feeding her baby, menstrual cups, Akka Café and Shishu Sanjeevini highlighted women’s empowerment and welfare initiatives. Belagavi Zilla Panchayat showcased Belavadi Mallamma, the heroic queen from the region, while a tableau depicting the first Dasara celebrations during the Vijayanagara Empire offered a glimpse into the festival’s historical origins.

Vidhurashwatha, known as the Jallianwala Bagh of South India, featured in the Chickballapur district tableau. The Mysuru tableau highlighted the city’s journey towards the future, built on a strong foundation, with a hilltop temple forming part of its presentation.

Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) showcased India’s indigenous aerospace and defense capabilities. The Indian Institute of Science (IISc) celebrated 117 years of scientific excellence and nation-building through its tableau. New Mangalore Port Trust (NMPT), Karnataka’s maritime gateway, displayed a replica of a cruise ship.

The Karnataka Tourism Department highlighted the natural beauty and rich cultural heritage of the Malnad and coastal regions. Indian Railways showcased the evolution of locomotives and its eco-friendly initiatives. The Indian Navy’s tableau, themed around Atmanirbhar Bharat, highlighted indigenous warship designs and technological innovations, while the Indian Army’s presentation blended soldiers’ courage with technological transformation and preparedness for future battles.

Other notable tableaux included the Department of Youth Empowerment and Sports showcasing the concept of Bharat Jodo, Tibetan Settlement at Bylakuppe, The Mysuru Hotel Owners’ Association, showcasing Mysuru Pak and Masala Dosa; the Karnataka Milk Federation, Karnataka Soaps and Detergents, The Social Welfare Department and Karnataka Tanda Development Corporation. The Chamarajanagar tableau highlighted sacred sites and folk heritage amid forest wealth, while the Tulunadu tableau celebrated the region’s rich culture and traditions.

The Institute of Nephrology in its tableau highlighted the importance of kidney and its donation.
