title: What are Italy’s new measures against violent protests?
text:
The right-wing government of Italy’s Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has approved a raft of security measures, including the deployment of 500 troops in the financial capital Milan, to curb youth-led protests that turned chaotic over the weekend.

“There is nothing revolutionary about vandalising and stealing. Vandalism and theft are not protest, they are criminality,” Meloni wrote on social media on Tuesday, unveiling the decree.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Cost of living protests hit Belgium, Italy, Portugal and France

list 2 of 3Israel’s ties with Europe are fraying. Can its election change that?

list 3 of 3How has the cost of living changed in France, Italy, Spain and Portugal?

end of list

Unrest broke out on Saturday in Milan during a peaceful rally over rising living costs and poor school conditions inspired by similar mobilisations in neighbouring Spain and France.

Groups of mainly young people looted shops, smashed windows and clashed with the police again on Sunday, with riots also reported in Bologna and Turin.

Here’s what we know about the new measures.

What measures have been announced?

The Italian cabinet approved sending 500 troops to Milan until the end of the year to maintain security at key sites, step up surveillance of ‌sensitive locations, ⁠and enhance monitoring across the area, the Defence Ministry said in a statement.

It is unclear what the army will be able to do, given that the cabinet stopped short of granting soldiers additional policing powers following opposition from President Sergio Mattarella. In Italy, the army is responsible for national defence while police carry out investigations and arrest duties.

As part of the new legal measures, which take effect immediately, the government has also introduced a new offence of “violent participation in public demonstrations” targeting people gathering in groups of more than five who use potentially harmful objects including stones, sticks and fireworks.

The offence is punishable with up to five years in prison and a fine up to 20,000 euros ($22,440).

The text of the decree also cites the saying “You break it, you buy it” as grounds for making the parents of minors financially liable for the damage caused by their children. The state can claim damages for any resulting loss against parents’ properties or by deducting public subsidies received by the family.

Children and young people aged 14 to 18 will also be subject to administrative detention, even if they have not committed a crime, provided there is evidence they pose a danger, extending powers that previously applied only to adults.

Additional measures include longer prison sentences of up to 12 years for individuals who use social media or online tools to organise groups for violent public demonstrations.

title: Trump says AI data centres should pay ‘dividends’ in pre-midterm shift
text:
United States President Donald Trump has said AI data centres should pay “dividends” to communities, in a shift before the midterm elections.

“If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend'” Trump said in a post on Truth Social on Wednesday.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Trump launches midterms campaign blitz amid record low approval ratings

list 2 of 3Trump defiant about midterm chances as he rallies for Republicans in Ohio

list 3 of 3California Gov Newsom boosts AI regulation as he eyes 2028 presidential run

The president’s comments come after he doubled down on his support for data centres, a stance seen as one of several political liabilities for Republicans in the run-up to the midterm election, as Trump’s approval rating has hit record lows.

Polls show dismal support for such centres amid concerns about the sprawling complexes’ water and energy use.

In the post, Trump advised companies that they could make the centres popular if they “pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend’.”

“I have watched the process closely, and Data Centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck,” he said. “MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!!”

Several top Republican candidates have opposed data centres before the midterm polls, with the issue emerging as an area of rare bipartisan consensus in advance of the November 3 vote.

Republican Senate candidates, including Ken Paxton in Texas, Mike Rogers in Michigan and John Husted in Ohio, have all called for more restrictions and oversight on the centres, in a reversal of earlier positions.

The issue featured prominently in a recent debate in Iowa, where Republican Senate Candidate Ashley Hinson said the local level should decide whether to build AI data centres.

Despite the shifting sentiment, Trump in late August issued an impassioned defence of data centres, decrying what he called “the anti-Data Center movement” as a gift to China.

“The only reason that communities throughout the USA should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote at the time.

“If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

Trump has taken several measures to accelerate data centre development, including issuing an executive order last year that called for measures to fast-track permitting and environmental review. The order promised to use federal land for the “expeditious and orderly development of data centers”.

Trump has also backed a voluntary pledge by AI companies to cover the full cost of the electricity data centres use, but has avoided supporting legally binding federal restrictions.

A Gallup poll conducted in March suggested that 71 percent of Americans opposed establishing AI data centres in their areas.

title: Russia to send first diesel tanker to the US amid Trump deal
text:
Russia will send its first tanker of diesel fuel to the United States on Thursday, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters amid a deal with US President Donald Trump.

The vessel will have 40,000 tonnes of fuel, but Novak, who made his remarks on Wednesday, did not name which US port the fuel would be delivered to.

Recommended Stories

list of 4 items

list 1 of 4Why Rubio is visiting Reliance’s oil refinery in India, the world’s largest

list 2 of 4Macron lines up more Gulf diesel as France battles soaring fuel prices

list 3 of 4‘I don’t care how it’s done’: Trump pressures Ukraine to cut peace deal

list 4 of 4UK approves development of Jackdaw gasfield in North Sea

end of list

Russia lifted its ban on diesel exports on October 9, which Moscow originally put in place to tackle the country’s shortages as Ukrainian-led drone strikes hindered production capacity.

The shipment comes despite setbacks for Russia’s diesel output. Earlier this month, Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence said that drone strikes knocked out at least half of Russia’s oil refining capacity, forcing cuts at Russia’s top diesel-producing refineries.

“Additional shipments will follow, of course. There were agreements reached between the two leaders. We will meet the United States’ needs, to the extent of our capabilities,” the RIA Novosti news agency quoted Novak as saying.

That was echoed by US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who has been meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin for talks in St Petersburg.

“We are preparing deliveries of several vessels, the tankers, right now. They will go one after another. The financial component should be provided,” he said, adding that Russia would also be able to supply fertilisers in “large quantities” to the US market.

US President Donald Trump had previously said that Moscow would export 300,000 tonnes, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.

US consumers have continued to face high prices at the petrol station, particularly for diesel fuel, a pressing point as the country heads into midterm elections in less than two weeks. The average price for a gallon of diesel is $6.31 ($1.70 per litre), according to the American Automobile Association (AAA). While prices remain well over the $6 mark, they are on the downturn. The average price a month ago was $6.51.

title: Musk pledges $10bn in SpaceX shares for US children: Who really gains?
text:
Elon Musk has pledged to give one SpaceX share to every child in the United States next year – a gift that could be worth more than $10bn.

“This will be the first of many,” the world’s richest man wrote on X on Monday.

About 73 million children under 18 live in the US, according to US Census Bureau data.

At Friday’s closing price of $146.03, the pledge would be worth about $10.7bn.

President Donald Trump thanked Musk on his Truth Social platform, and claimed the shares would be given to children “through TRUMP ACCOUNTS”, the tax-friendly investment accounts for children created under his signature tax and spending law last year.

The pledge comes two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.

Musk is the biggest known donor in the run-up to those elections, having given more than $276m to Republican groups since July.

Musk has not said which children will qualify, when the shares will be handed over, or how.

So how might the giveaway work, and who stands to gain?

Here’s what you need to know:

How much is a SpaceX share worth, and how much is Musk giving away?

SpaceX, the world’s seventh-largest company, began trading on the Nasdaq in June at an initial public offering price of $135 per share.

That price has been volatile. SpaceX shares have fallen 35.3 percent since peaking days after the listing.

The shares are currently trading at around $146 a share. Every $1 move in the share price will change the gift’s value by about $73m.

Musk owns 4.8 billion shares in SpaceX outright, according to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) in August.

Including unvested awards and stock options, his stake rises to about 6.4 billion shares, or 48.4 percent of the company.

Giving away 73 million shares would reduce his outright holding by about 1.5 percent, barely affecting his control of the company. That’s because his voting power, which is currently about 82 percent because SpaceX has two classes of shares, would fall by only 0.1 percentage points, according to a Bloomberg Opinion calculation.

It would be the largest single gift linked to Trump accounts so far.

How would the shares reach children?

Musk has not said.

Trump said the shares would be held in Trump accounts, and Musk thanked Brad Gerstner, the tech investor behind the accounts, for “helping enable this”.

Nearly 70 million Trump accounts have been opened, one for every child under 18 with a Social Security number, according to the White House. Investments held in Trump accounts can roll up with tax deferred until they are withdrawn when a child turns 18. Alternatively, they can be rolled into a tax-friendly IRA – a retirement account for adults – and continue with the tax-friendly status.

Under Treasury rules published on September 30, donors can now gift individual company stock to children via the accounts. Families and friends making regular contributions to a child’s Trump account are limited to investing low-risk index funds.

text: US envoy Steve Witkoff praised Russian President Vladimir Putin as a ‘humanitarian’ while thanking him for the release of American Stephen Hubbard, who spent more than four years in Russian detention after being convicted of mercenary activity in Ukraine.

title: Russia releases American Stephen Hubbard after four years in prison
text:
American Stephen Hubbard has been freed from a Russian prison and is on his way home after United States President Donald Trump said his administration had secured his release.

“Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family,” Trump wrote in a social media post on Wednesday, adding that the US was not required to give anything in return for the release of the 74-year-old former teacher from Michigan.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Russia frees US basketball star Brittney Griner in prisoner swap

list 2 of 3Griner’s release raises fresh concerns about fate of Paul Whelan

list 3 of 3Russia frees ex-US Marine Robert Gilman from detention

end of list

The deal came during a visit to Russia by a top US envoy, and just days after Trump took a series of actions seen as beneficial to Moscow.

Hubbard, whose family says had been living in Ukraine since before Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, was tried and convicted in a closed-door trial, with Russian prosecutors saying he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian military and had fought alongside its forces before being captured. He was sentenced to seven years in prison in 2024.

The US had declared Hubbard a wrongfully detained American.

Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff, who is in Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin on the Ukraine war, told him that “our whole nation sends their thanks” and that Putin was a “humanitarian” for allowing Hubbard to walk free. Witkoff briefly met with Hubbard in St. Petersburg after his release, telling him, “from today is a new life for you”.

The release came at a dynamic moment in relations between the US, Ukraine and Russia, with the Washington-Kyiv relationship under strain at the same time that the Trump administration has pursued policies which Ukraine says have rewarded Putin.

Those include Trump’s decision last week to waive sanctions on Russia imposed by a bill that the US Congress overwhelmingly passed to support Ukraine.

Named after the late South Carolina Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, the legislation targeted the flow of financial resources fuelling Moscow’s war on Ukraine.

That reversal followed Trump’s announcement of a deal to import Russian diesel fuel in an effort to curb high gas prices before next month’s US midterm elections.

title: US congressional candidate Brad Lander freed after West Bank detention
text:
United States Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander says he has been released from Israeli military custody with a warning after being detained alongside dozens of volunteers helping Palestinian farmers harvest olives in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday.

But several dozen others, including rabbis and international volunteers, remain in detention, according to Lander, who called for them to be released immediately.

Lander, a Jewish American and former New York City comptroller, was among approximately 80 volunteers detained by Israeli soldiers and police near the village of Nahalin, outside Bethlehem, according to the Israeli organisation Rabbis for Human Rights.

The group included American, Israeli, Palestinian, British and Canadian volunteers.

Becca Strober, a representative of the Protect the Harvest Coalition, which helped organise the olive harvest, told Al Jazeera that the group had been picking olives at the invitation of a Palestinian family for several hours when the Israeli army arrived.

“It was a nice, peaceful day,” he said. “There was no conflict. There was no settler violence. There was no violence of any kind.”

According to Strober, after a while, soldiers began checking the volunteers’ IDs, and soon after, issued an order declaring the area a closed military zone. They then detained the group, first in the field and later at a police station.

“To this moment, everyone’s still detained except for Brad Lander,” said Strober. “They very clearly told him that they allowed him to be released because he’s likely to be in Congress very soon.”

Israel’s Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, accused Lander of staging a “calculated political provocation,” alleging that he’d deliberately entered a restricted security area without approval.

“This was not about harvesting olives. It was about harvesting headlines,” the ministry said in a statement on X, alleging that Lander’s team and reached out to Israeli representatives in the US in advance of the visit and had been told it would require coordination with relevant authorities, but that Lander ignored those instructions.

“Brad Lander came looking for a confrontation,” said the statement. “Now he is pretending to be its victim.”

title: How Qatar, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia are deepening defence ties
text:
Qatar, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia signed a deal on Wednesday to deepen their defence industry cooperation, reflecting a broader effort by countries in the region to widen their network of security partners amid the prolonged US-Israel war with Iran.

The four countries signed the memorandum of understanding in Doha, building on existing military projects through joint production, technology transfers and more closely integrated supply chains.

The initiative comes as the failure of the United States and Iran to reach a concrete peace agreement pushes countries in the region to diversify their defence partnerships and look beyond what experts described as an overreliance on Washington for their security. But they stress that closer cooperation does not mean abandoning long-standing alliances. Instead, the ambition is to gain greater control over their own security while strengthening pre-existing partnerships.

Arda Mevlutoglu, a defence industry analyst and managing director of Mergen Analytical Strategies, told Al Jazeera that the implications could extend well beyond the four participants.

“We may be witnessing the emergence of an interconnected network of defence and security arrangements extending from the Gulf to South and Southeast Asia, rather than a single formal alliance,” he said.

What would the agreement do?

Together, the four nations could “establish integrated supply chains, allowing these countries to jointly develop, manufacture and sustain defence systems”, he told Al Jazeera.

title: How war in Lebanon has cost young people with autism and ADHD
text:
Beirut, Lebanon – After her husband died from COVID-19 in 2020, Lena Kouyoumjian moved back to her parents’ house in Mazraat Yachouh, a village 20 minutes’ drive from Beirut. For Lena, energetic and outgoing, the move was difficult, but she accepted that she needed help to care for her 20-year-old daughter, Vana, who is autistic and non-verbal.

Lena first noticed her daughter’s symptoms when she was two years old. Vana is still unable to communicate verbally how she feels, but her mother does her best to understand her.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Lebanon’s children face physical, psychological trauma amid Israel’s war

list 2 of 3Psychological toll mounts as Lebanese villages erased by Israel’s war

list 3 of 3‘An act of resistance’: Raja Shehadeh’s diaries find a new home in Scotland

end of list

Like many autistic individuals – and neurodivergent people in general – Vana needs a supportive and stable environment, alongside a structured routine, to feel well.

Lebanon has been engulfed in war since October 2023, with bombings across the country and an economic crisis continuing to impact all Lebanese, particularly neurodivergent people.

When Israel escalated its attacks on southern Lebanon in March, as a trainer for children with disabilities, Lena understood that this could impact her autistic daughter.

“Any sudden change in routine, loud noises, fear, or uncertainty can increase their anxiety and make them feel unsafe,” Lena told Al Jazeera.

“I can see this in my daughter. Since the situation became more difficult, she has become more anxious and sensitive to the changes happening around her.”

Challenging a social stigma

The symptoms of autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) vary depending on the person and condition, but they frequently include sensory issues and emotional dysregulation. ADHD and autism often occur together, combining to make AuDHD, where traits from both conditions can be seen.

People with these neurodevelopmental conditions are often stigmatised by societies that do not fully understand them, including in Lebanon.

While the pressures caused by Israel’s war on Lebanon and mass displacement have led to psychological issues for many, neurodivergent people are more vulnerable due to their need for consistent support and routine.

“Being a parent of an autistic child isn’t something every parent can handle. A challenge I often face is deciding the amount of time and energy I should allocate to my child,” said Lena.

Lebanon’s Autism Awareness Association (AAA) has provided support for both mother and child. Vana has attended classes at AAA, a nonprofit based in Antelias, outside Beirut, for the past six years, which serves as an alternative school for young autistic people.

title: Are the UK, France being pulled into the Saudi-Houthi conflict?
text:
France and the United Kingdom have both moved to deploy military assets to Saudi Arabia, deepening their defence ties with the kingdom as its conflict with the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), in Yemen escalates.

Paris last week said it had begun sending assets to Saudi Arabia as part of a previously announced agreement, after President Emmanuel Macron committed to deploying troops and air defence systems to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu, which has come under attack from the Iran-backed Houthis.

Recommended Stories

The UK, for its part, on Tuesday announced plans to deploy fighter jets to help shield Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks.

Both countries stressed that their support would be defensive.

Analysts say the European moves serve several geopolitical purposes: protecting Saudi oil exports that are important to European energy markets, shoring up their strategic alliance in the Gulf amid US reluctance to offer direct military assistance to Saudi Arabia, and strengthening deterrence against future Houthi attacks.

But the deployments also carry significant risks, many analysts say, potentially drawing the two European states more directly into the protracted Saudi-Houthi conflict.

“If insufficiently deterred, the Houthis may decide that the moment is ripe to test the resolve and resilience of Saudi Arabia’s defensive posture, and attempt to draw Saudi Arabia’s allies even further into the Yemen-Saudi confrontation,” Burcu Ozcelik, a senior research fellow for Middle East Security at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), told Al Jazeera.

‘Support during crisis’

The British and French military support measures come as Saudi Arabia faces a sustained Houthi missile and drone campaign against it, including targeting energy and transport infrastructure.

Houthi attacks targeting Saudi airports in Riyadh and Abha this month have killed 19 people and injured more than 300 others, according to the Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki.

Addressing the UK’s stepped-up military support for Saudi Arabia, UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called recent Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia “absolutely despicable”, specifically condemning the group’s targeting of Riyadh airport.

The UK Ministry of Defence said it would deploy Typhoon fighter jets to fly “defensive counter air missions” in Saudi Arabia, send UK military advisers to work with Saudi staff officers and provide an A400M transport aircraft to help move defence material within the kingdom.

title: From one house to villages: Israeli settlers have Palestinians surrounded
text:
Yousef Shanaran, 52, built a well beside his house, which he can no longer reach. Since October 5, Israeli settlers have besieged his family home in Wadi Rakhim around the clock, a once-quiet corner of the South Hebron Hills among limestone rocks and thorny brush. They are unable to go outside on their own, even to fetch a little water from the well.

It took five days for the army to coordinate the family’s access to the well. After running out of water three days earlier, the Israeli army on Tuesday allowed them to retrieve some from the well.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3The night watch: Palestinians protecting their homes from settler pogroms

list 2 of 3How Israel’s 2026 election works

list 3 of 3Palestine weekly: Israeli settlers attack journalist and diplomats

“Food, there’s none,” Shanaran, who built the sturdy two-storey house in 2016 on land between the Palestinian town of as-Samu and the village of Susiya, planting about 70 grapevines and 30 to 40 olive trees, told Al Jazeera by phone.

“My well, full of water; I built it and lost money on it,” he said. “They keep me from it because they want to get me out of my house.”

More than half a year ago, settlers pitched a tent 300 metres (about 1,000 feet) from the Shanaran residence, restricting the family’s movement and exposing them to attacks and intimidation. On October 5, the tent was moved just 30 metres from their home. That day, about 50 settlers attacked the family with sticks and pepper spray. This marked the beginning of the full siege on Shanaran’s home.

A siege the army ‘doesn’t recognise’

Nasser Nawajeh, a longtime B’Tselem field researcher who now heads the Susiya village council in Masafer Yatta, has tried to deliver supplies to the Shanaran family during the siege, but most attempts have failed. “Once I tried to bring aid to the people, and right away there was an attack from the settlers,” he told Al Jazeera. “I mean they’re there 24 hours to attack.”

Nothing can move in or out of Shanaran’s home without the army’s permission. “This is a displacement policy,” he said. “If they want to take the kids out to school, we have to wait for the army to take them. If you want to bring in food or water, we have to do coordination.”

Since October 15, he has kept asking the army for coordination to deliver supplies to the family — and given excuses each day: “‘The army’s busy, can’t come, there aren’t any forces’ — they tell us ‘tomorrow and tomorrow’,” he said.

There are now two armies to contend with, Nawajeh said: the settlers’ regional units, the Kitat Konenut, meaning rapid response squads in Hebrew; and the regular army, which “comes, demolishes [the settlers’ tent] and leaves”. When the soldiers leave, the settlers simply pitch up their tent again.

Shanaran said the soldiers stationed outside his house do nothing. “They stand and sit, eating and drinking, relaxed, at the door of the house,” he said.

title: Pakistani authorities arrest man accused in $126m US postage fraud
text:
Pakistani authorities have arrested a man accused of masterminding an online counterfeit operation that United States prosecutors say resulted in more than $125m of losses to the US Postal Service.

Faheem Akram, 33, was arrested on Tuesday after an expansive search operation and raids across Pakistan, a senior official at the Pakistani National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency told reporters.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Dozens of South Koreans freed from Cambodia scam centres now home, arrested

list 2 of 3US drops fraud charges after billionaire Adani pledges $10bn investment

list 3 of 3The $3.7bn man: Inside one of US’s biggest Medicare frauds

end of list

Akram was indicted last month by a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida, and is accused of operating a fraudulent website where he sold more than 5.1 million counterfeit stamps in the US.

The stamps, which cost about $2 each, allowed customers to ship their packages at a lower price than official postal rates, causing significant losses to the Postal Service, according to the US Attorney’s office.

The estimate of more than $124m however, represents the losses to the Postal Service and not the proceeds from the website, officials said.

Pakistani investigators discovered that Akram has been operating the website since August 2023 and used 16 bank accounts, including his own and several family members’, for the operation.

Akram has been charged with several offences, including conspiracy to defraud the US and the making and selling of fake postage stamps, as well as four counts of wire fraud, according to the US Postal Service.

He could face 20 years in prison on each count of wire fraud, as well as five years in prison for conspiracy.

Akram is currently in custody in Pakistan, but it is unclear whether he will face trial in the country or be extradited to the US.

title: France’s Macron says protesters won’t be allowed to ‘cause chaos’
text:
French President Emmanuel Macron has said people who plan to “cause chaos” during protests against the high cost of living will not be allowed to do so.

Speaking to the press in Doha, where he met Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Macron said he would meet with French intelligence services before protests planned for Saturday.

He maintained that there has not been any “visible ‌foreign interference in the events ‌that took place”, but warned that “there had been foreign manipulation of information in the aftermath.”

More than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday to demand better conditions in schools and denounce high living costs. At least 2,500 people were arrested after riots broke out in certain areas, with shops looted.

Macron insisted he would “adopt all the measures necessary” to restore what he described as “calm, security and order”.

The French president also criticised “unacceptable and even stupid comments by many, including foreign leaders”.

Macron said the leaders were weighing in on protests in France to rally their political supporters. His comments appeared to be related to United States President Donald Trump, who claimed the protests were about immigration.

Macron’s criticism also appeared to relate to claims made by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who said France had been engulfed by an “invasion of extremist Islam”. Neither Trump nor Netanyahu provided any evidence to support their claims.

On Wednesday, France’s Yellow Vest movement filed plans for a large protest in Paris this weekend, following a second consecutive night of curfews that passed without major incidents.

Macron said it was not currently necessary to enforce a state of emergency, but Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has pledged to increase security at future protests. Lecornu said there would be a “massive deployment” of police, backed by the military.

title: Andhra Pradesh SEC halts election process for 100 ULBs after Supreme Court order
text:
Andhra Pradesh State Election Commissioner (SEC) Anil Chandra Punetha has ordered that the election process for all 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for which the notification was issued on October 14 be stopped forthwith in view of the Supreme Court’s directions.

Mr. Punetha, in a late-evening order, said that the SEC would issue an order on the ULB elections after obtaining reports from the Collectors, District Election Authorities and Police Commissioners or Superintendents of Police October 22.

He said the notification for the elections to 13 Municipal Corporations, 87 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats in the State was issued on October 14 and the nomination process was completed between October 16 to 18, followed by the scrutiny of nominations on October 19.

However, the Supreme Court has directed the SEC to postpone the publication of the final list of candidates for the ULB elections till October 25.

Meanwhile, the SEC was mandated to consider the representations made by the petitioner party (YSRCP) and other candidates, including evidentiary material as well as electronic evidence placed before it and take a decision on the last date for filing nominations wherever it is of the view that candidates were unable to file their nominations due to law and order situation, he said.

title: India-Australia joint military exercise begins in capital
text:
The 5th edition of the India-Australia joint military exercise AUSTRAHIND 2026 is under way in Thiruvananthapuram, a defence spokesperson said.

Approximately 120 personnel each from the Indian and Australian armies are taking part in the exercise, which commenced on October 19 and will last till November 1. The fourth edition was held at Irwin Barracks, Perth, Australia, from October 13 to 26, 2025.

The Indian Army contingent comprises troops from the Garhwal Rifles, along with personnel from other arms and services, while the Australian contingent comprises troops from the 13 Brigade.

The exercise is themed on ‘Joint Sub-Conventional Operations in Island and Coastal Environment under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate.’ “It is aimed at enhancing interoperability, jointmanship and operational coordination between the two armies while developing a common understanding of tactics, techniques and procedures for operations in island and coastal terrain,” the spokesperson said.

During the exercise, troops of both armies will undertake joint planning, tactical drills and combat-oriented training in realistic operational conditions, including aerial and maritime dimension. The training will focus on coordinated operations in coastal and island environments, surveillance and reconnaissance, protection of vital installations and response to humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) contingencies, besides exchange of professional experience and best practices.

In a first, an observer delegation from New Zealand is also participating in the exercise.

‘AUSTRAHIND 2026’ will further strengthen military-to-military cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust between India and Australia. It will reinforce their shared commitment towards peace, stability and security in the Indo-Pacific region, the spokesperson said.

title: What’s behind protests in Portugal?
text: Thousands of protesters have returned to Portugal’s streets after police cleared their camps and arrested dozens of people. Al Jazeera’s Ava Warriner explains what’s behind the protests and why demonstrators are refusing to back down.

title: 'Asked to remove Tiranga pics': What happened at Priyanka Gandhi son's exhibition
text:
Artist and Photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, with one of his photographs at Bikaner House, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: A controversy erupted at Delhi’s Bikaner House after artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and businessman Robert Vadra, alleged that the venue’s management asked him to remove around 74 photographs documenting recent youth protests ahead of his solo exhibition, “No Idea Is Final”. Raihan also alleged that he was asked to remove two photographs of the Indian flag, saying he had refused to take them down. The exhibition opened as scheduled on Wednesday, with around 40 photographs remaining on display while more than 70 were removed, according to a PTI report. The show, featuring wildlife photography, abstract works and images of recent youth movements, is scheduled to continue until Sunday. In a post on Instagram, Raihan wrote, "Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show "No Idea Is Final", which opens this evening at 7 pm. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently, the content is "objectionable". They also directed me to remove two photos of the Tiranga. I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag."

Why were the photographs removed?

Raihan told PTI that the management had raised objections to the “political nature” of the protest photographs. He said he was informed at 3.30 pm on Wednesday that the images had to be removed by 5 pm or the exhibition would be cancelled. According to Raihan, the management said that, given the prevailing political climate in India, it was not the right time to display the images. He maintained that the photographs did not convey a political message and merely documented protests over the preceding six months. "I felt it is my duty as an Indian artist, not just because I am doing a show right now, but it is my duty as an Indian artist to document what is going on... They are censoring the work of artists, I don't know what they are scared of. They even went to the extent of removing the picture of the Indian flag," he told PTI. Raihan also said he had shared the exhibition proposal and layout with the management well in advance and objected to the removal of nearly half the artworks less than 24 hours before the opening. A Bikaner House official told PTI that the administration was not authorised to comment on the matter.

Priyanka Gandhi, Congress leaders react

Priyanka Gandhi Vadra criticised the alleged removal of the photographs, describing it as an attempt to silence young voices. "I think it's ridiculous. What do you think? He is a young boy but I suppose you know, they are muzzling the voice of the youth across the nation. So it's only expected that they'll do it to anyone," she told PTI. title: Man dies after attackers trap hands in car windows, drag him for 1.5km - video
text:
A 37-year-old man, Biru Singh Bhadauriya, died after being assaulted in Kanpur's Hanumant Vihar area.

KANPUR: A 37-year-old man died on Wednesday after he was allegedly assaulted, pinned to the roof of a car with his hands trapped between its window panes and dragged for around 1.5km by a group of attackers in Kanpur’s Hanumant Vihar area. Police are examining CCTV footage as part of the investigation. The incident took place on Tuesday night when Biru Singh Bhadauriya was returning home after visiting a Dussehra fair. The attackers allegedly rammed their car into him over an old rivalry before assaulting him and forcing him onto the vehicle’s roof. They allegedly trapped both his hands between the window panes, shut the windows and drove at high speed for around 1.5km with Bhadauriya on the roof. The attackers then allegedly threw him onto the road and fled. Bhadauriya was rushed to Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital, where he died during treatment on Wednesday. According to a post on the official Kanpur Commissionerate police handle, a man was seriously injured after being hit by an unidentified vehicle on Arra Road on Tuesday night. He succumbed to his injuries during treatment at Lala Lajpat Rai Hospital the following day. Police said a case had been registered under relevant sections and the postmortem examination had been conducted. Further legal action is underway, with investigators examining CCTV footage to establish the sequence of events and identify those involved.

End of Article

title: US, Israel prepare for fresh Iran strikes as Tehran threatens with ‘Father of All Bombs’
text:
Iran threatens to unveil ‘Father of All Bombs’ amid reports of fresh US-Israeli strike plans

The United States and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed military strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections, according to a report by The New York Times. Meanwhile, Tehran has threatened to unveil a weapon it calls the “Father of All Bombs” amid escalating tensions in West Asia. The proposed US-Israeli operation could involve a short but intensive campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities and missile and drone arsenal. Citing US officials and others briefed on the deliberations, The New York Times reported that the two militaries had stepped up exercises, including flights over Iraq to practise strike manoeuvres. US war secretary Pete Hegseth also met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel this week to discuss the possibility of renewed strikes, according to the report. Some US officials believe another round of attacks could push Iran's economy to the brink and pressure Tehran into making diplomatic concessions after nearly eight months of conflict. However, it remains uncertain whether US President Donald Trump will approve a fresh operation. A White House official said the administration did not comment on military plans “that may or may not exist”, adding that Trump was keeping all options on the table to ensure Iran could not acquire nuclear weapons.

Iran threatens to unveil ‘Father of All Bombs’

Amid reports of possible renewed strikes, Iran has warned that it would respond to any fresh military action. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iran was preparing to unveil a weapon described as the “Father of All Bombs”, according to statements carried by Iranian media outlets. “The United States has the ‘Mother of All Bombs.’ We will show them the ‘Father of All Bombs,’ and it will definitely be something new for them,” Mohebbi said, according to Iran's Student News Network (SNN). In separate remarks carried by Iran's Young Journalists Club news agency, Mohebbi said, “We are in the stage of preparing to unveil the ‘father of all bombs.’ This is something new for the enemy.” He did not provide details about the weapon or explain its capabilities. Mohebbi also said Iran's missile stockpile had increased 1.5 times following the 12-day war between Iran and Israel in June 2025, without providing specific figures. He claimed that missile quality, range, destructive power and accuracy had improved significantly. The IRGC spokesperson said Iran was moving towards a defence doctrine based on permanent deterrence and asymmetric warfare. “Now, we say that if a country attacks us, we will not only respond but also launch an offensive,” he said. “Our doctrine will no longer be merely offensive; it will be asymmetric. We will attack the enemy in a way that makes them feel the intensity of our response,” Mohebbi added.

title: ‘Evil man will be punished’: Rijiju warns Delhi man over racial abuse of Tripura youth
text:
From Rijiju to Tripura opposition, outrage over alleged racial abuse of tribal youth

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday strongly condemned "racial" harassment of a tribal youth from Tripura's Gomati district by a Delhi-based social media influencer Amir Shokeen. Rijiju took to X late Wednesday and shared a video of the incident, acknowledging the delay in filing an official complaint but warning that the accused would face action. "This evil man will be punished. There was delay in lodging the official complaint but Delhi Police and Tripura Police will teach him a hard lesson. People who tolerate such wicked behavior in the society are also responsible for the spread of hatred," the Union parliamentary affairs minister said. In the video circulating online, Shokeen can allegedly be heard making racial remarks against the youth. The clip, which surfaced on Tuesday evening, purportedly shows him asking the young man whether he was the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly mocked Tripura when the youth responded that he was Indian. Political parties in Tripura closed ranks on Wednesday over the incident and demanded legal action against Shokeen. Tripura chief minister Manik Saha directed the state director general of police to coordinate with Delhi Police and ensure a proper investigation into the incident. CPM state secretary and leader of the opposition Jitendra Chaudhury demanded an apology from Shokeen. "Establish a precedent that is both resounding and unmistakable, ensuring no one ever dares insult Tripura and the Tiprasa community again," he said.

title: Google co-founder Larry Page leaves California ahead of billionaire tax vote
text:
With Californians set to vote in just a few weeks on Proposition 40 – a measure proposing a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires – Google co-founder Larry Page has emerged as the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections as he will be the richest techie to leave the state. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026. While a few prominent executives, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, have stated they are "perfectly fine" with the proposal, multiple ultra-wealthy residents chose to exit before the January deadline. Chief among them is the 53-year-old Page. Holding an estimated net worth of $292 billion, Page had deep roots in California spanning decades, Fortune reported, adding that had he remained a California resident past the cutoff date, he would have owed an estimated $15 billion under the one-time tax levy.

Moving entities to Delaware and buying big in Miami

State filings have revealed that Page began unwinding his operational and personal presence in California late last year. According to an analysis of corporate records reported by Fortune, Page’s family office, Koop, was transferred out of California and officially incorporated in Delaware in late December. Multiple associated entities, including Flu Lab LLC, One Aero and Oceankind, followed the same route, moving their registrations from California to Delaware during the same month. Simultaneously, Page redirected significant capital toward luxury real estate on the East Coast. The Wall Street Journal reported that Page acquired two premier estates in Miami for a combined $173.4 million, which includes Coconut Grove Estate ($101.5 million, 11,855-square-foot property) and a neighboring parcel purchased for $71.9 million.

The $29 billion dent in Prop 40’s target

The departures of top-tier billionaires have already weakened the potential financial yield of the ballot measure. Prop 40 was projected to generate roughly $100 billion for the state. However, according to an estimate by Fortune, just four departed tech leaders – Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Peter Thiel and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick – would have collectively owed approximately $29 billion. Their relocations before the residency cutoff mean the state has effectively lost out on more than a quarter of the measure's total projected revenue pool before ballots are even counted. Elon Musk, the richest person in the world, moved to Texas in 2020. Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos who recently but briefly secured the second richest person spot, departed Seattle for Miami in late 2023, eventually selling his Hunts Point home for a record $63 million to live in a $237 million Miami compound with his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos.

End of Article

title: Drones fall, strikes stall: How Musk's Starshield curbs hit Zelenskyy’s war effort
text:
Trump growing closer to Putin? How Musk's Starshield curbs cost Ukraine $1 million in drones

A disruption in the US military satellite internet service Starshield caused Ukrainian drones worth more than $1 million to fall from the sky and forced troops to halt almost all operations for three days, The New York Times reported, citing Ukrainian military commanders. A senior Ukrainian commander, identified only by his first name, Oleh, said dozens of armed drones were heading towards Russian military targets last week when their video feeds suddenly went fuzzy. The drones had lost their connection to ground-based pilots through Starshield, a Pentagon-funded satellite internet service, he said. Many of the drones crashed, costing his units more than $1 million worth of weaponry, according to the report. The development comes days after Donald Trump’s reported engagement with Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin over efforts to end the war in Ukraine. The MAGA supremo also recently eased sanctions on Russian oil. Oleh said the disruption forced his units to suspend almost all operations for the next three days, including strikes on Russian command posts and fuel hubs. Such attacks help protect Ukrainian troops on the front lines and slow Russian advances, he said. The reported disruptions have added to the growing tensions between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump. Ukrainian troops said connectivity had improved after a week, but problems persisted. The Trump administration has issued mixed statements on the issue, denying that any changes were made to satellite internet services in Ukraine while also saying that service had been restored. Ukrainian officials fear the disruptions were ordered to punish Kyiv for attacks on Russian oil refineries and pressure it into making concessions in the war. Ukraine has also reported gaps in US military intelligence sharing and delays in deliveries of American interceptor missiles. US officials have denied deliberately disrupting these services.

What is Starshield and how does it affect Ukraine?

Starshield is a military-grade satellite communications system developed by SpaceX, the company owned by Elon Musk. It is a more advanced sister system to Starlink, which is widely used by Ukrainian forces for communications and drone operations. European countries pay for Ukraine's access to Starshield. However, the advanced system is not available to all Ukrainian troops. Many units rely on it to operate drones while using standard Starlink connections for basic communications. Ukrainian officials have reported slowdowns affecting both Starshield and Starlink. Musk has said that Starshield is controlled by the Pentagon. However, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio added to the confusion when he said on Wednesday that SpaceX determined access to both Starlink and Starshield. title: Confidence in poll key for democracy, halt candidates' list: SC to Andhra poll body
text:
SC said the right to participate in elections by filing nominations is a facet of the free poll process.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday said instilling confidence in the election process was vital for democracy and the rule of law as it directed Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (SEC) not to declare the final candidate list for 19 of the 100 local bodies where opposition YSRCP has alleged that its candidates were prevented from filing nominations. However, the court refused to tinker with the Oct 28 polling date. An autumn-break bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and VMohana asked SEC to decide by Thursday if it should, after considering representations from candidates alleging use of force to prevent them from filing nominations, give additional time for filing of nominations or postpone polls. Accepting the suggestion of senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, SC asked DGP to give adequate security at nomination filing centres and to candidates.

YSRCP importing criminals from Punjab: AP govt in SC

Senior advocate Maninder Singh, who appeared for YSRCP, said in 19 of the 100 urban local bodies — 13 municipal corporations and 87 municipalities/nagar panchayats — more than 63% of YSRCP candidates were prevented from filing nominations or their nomination papers were torn. Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for AP govt, said YSRCP was importing criminal elements from as far as Punjab and fomenting violence only to cry wolf later. SEC, through senior advocate K Parameswar, denied YSRCP’s claims. The SC bench said, “Free and fair elections are a basic structure of the Constitution. Right to participate in such elections by filing nomination papers is a facet of the free and fair election process. It is the constitutional mandate to vest the SEC with the duty of conducting and supervising such elections which would necessarily include all steps to ensure free and transparent filing of nomination papers by contesting candidates. The power of constitutional courts in exercise of judicial review, though deferential to the conduct of elections by the EC, cannot be said to be only nugatory.” SC said it was the duty of SEC to direct the state law-enforcing machinery to provide adequate security and maintain law and order to provide candidates a secure environment to file their nomination papers in a peaceful manner. Referring to Singh’s allegations that the state police were, at times, indifferent or selective in registering complaints of YSRCP candidates, Parameswar said SEC had issued directions to police and Luthra said police had taken adequate measures to control law and order issues. Referring to the allegations of the principal opposition party, backed by prima facie material of violence unleashed to prevent filing of nominations, SC said, “We are conscious of judicial deference to the powers of control and superintendence of elections by EC. title: 'Successes in eliminating Maoism': PM Modi, Jaishankar wish Amit Shah on birthday
text:
PM Modi extends birthday wishes to Amit Shah as latter turns 62

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday extended birthday wishes to Union home minister Amit Shah as he turned 62, praising his commitment to national security and public welfare. In a post on X, PM Modi said Shah's administrative understanding had made India's internal security systems more effective. He highlighted the successes in eliminating Maoism and efforts towards building a drug-free society. PM Modi also wished Shah a long and healthy life in service of the people. "Warm birthday greetings to Home Minister Shri Amit Shah Ji. His administrative understanding has ensured India’s internal security systems become more effective. Particularly noteworthy are the successes in eliminating the menace of Maoism and in furthering our dream of a society free from drugs. I pray that he is blessed with a long and healthy life in service of the people," he said.

title: Tamera Mowry lists home for $2.69m after buying 15-acre Napa estate for $3.8m
text:
Actress Tamera Mowry-Housley and her husband, former journalist Adam Housley, are preparing for a new chapter in Napa Valley as they put their longtime Fairfield, California, home on the market for $2.69 million. The June 2026 listing follows their $3.8 million purchase of a neglected wine-country property in October 2024, a move detailed by Realtor dot com and People as the couple documents their renovation journey online. The transition marks a shift from a spacious suburban residence to a rural property where the family hopes to grow its own produce, establish an orchard and vineyard, and embrace a more sustainable lifestyle.

A longtime family home goes on the market

The Fairfield residence, which the couple purchased for approximately $1.4 million in 2011, has five bedrooms and five bathrooms across about 4,863 square feet, according to the listing coverage. Built in 2005, the home sits on a roughly half-acre lot north of San Francisco. Its features include an open-plan living area, high ceilings, a fireplace, an upgraded kitchen with professional-grade appliances and custom cabinetry, and a primary bedroom with French doors opening onto a balcony. Outside, landscaped grounds, a saltwater swimming pool and views of the surrounding hills give the property a resort-like feel. The asking price of $2.69 million represents a substantial increase over the couple’s original purchase price, although the eventual sale price will depend on market conditions and negotiations. Real estate agents Ryan Nemeyer and Alfonso Garcia of the Nemeyer Garcia Team at Engel & Völkers are handling the listing. The agents have highlighted the home’s privacy, outdoor space and access to nearby employment centres as selling points for prospective buyers.

Why the couple chose Napa Valley

The move follows years of searching for a countryside property that could accommodate the family’s ambitions beyond city living. In October 2024, Mowry-Housley and her husband bought a Napa Valley estate for $3.8 million. Unlike their Fairfield home, the new property was in need of extensive renovation. The single-storey residence measures approximately 2,718 square feet and has three bedrooms and three bathrooms. It had reportedly been vacant since 2018. The couple’s decision was driven largely by the land rather than the existing house. The estate spans roughly 15 acres and includes a natural pond, wooded areas and more than four acres of Cabernet Sauvignon vines, according to the property’s previous listing. Adam Housley has described the setting as central to their plans, with the family hoping to create a home that reflects their own design preferences while allowing them to spend more time outdoors.

title: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez gave $3 million to rebuild Maui homes after wildfires
text:
When wildfires tore through Maui in August 2023, the damage extended well beyond the buildings reduced to ash. Families lost their homes, neighbourhoods were disrupted and the shortage of affordable housing became harder to manage. For residents already struggling with the cost of living on the Hawaiian island, finding somewhere to live became an additional concern. As reported by Maui Now, in October 2024, Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donated $3 million to Habitat for Humanity Maui, providing support for affordable housing programmes and work to repair and rebuild homes affected by the fires.

Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez's $3 million donation to Habitat for Humanity Maui

Habitat for Humanity Maui announced the contribution on 29 October 2024. The gift was among the largest the organisation had received in its history, according to the announcement, and came as the island continued to deal with the consequences of the wildfires and an existing shortage of affordable homes. The funding was intended to help the organisation expand its housing work, including construction and repair projects for local families. Some of the money would go towards rebuilding homes damaged by the fires, while other support would help more residents access homeownership. The donation also gave the organisation additional resources to increase its building capacity. For a community facing substantial housing needs, the ability to undertake more projects can affect how many families receive assistance and how quickly homes can be repaired or built.

Maui wildfires increased the need for affordable housing and home repairs

The wildfires that struck Maui in August 2023 caused widespread destruction, particularly in the historic town of Lahaina. Homes and businesses were lost, and many residents had to leave areas where they had lived for years. The disaster placed further pressure on an island where housing costs were already a persistent concern. Recovery involved more than clearing damaged sites and replacing buildings. Residents also needed access to housing they could afford while rebuilding plans moved forward. For households on lower incomes, returning to the island or remaining close to their communities could be difficult when available accommodation was limited and expensive. Habitat for Humanity Maui's work covered both the construction of homes and the repair of existing properties. The Bezos and Sanchez contribution was intended to strengthen those efforts, helping the organisation respond to the needs of families whose housing circumstances had been affected by the fires.

How Habitat for Humanity Maui supports local families

As reported, Habitat for Humanity Maui has worked on affordable housing on the island for more than 25 years. title: Jhansi teen builds AC for Rs 1,800 that cools room by 5°C
text:
Kalyani Srivastava (Instagram)

India is a country where scorching summers are often a problem which make staying indoors difficult. Air conditioning is also beyond the reach of many low-income households. For families living in heat-prone rural regions, summers are a challenge to survive along with electricity bills. In 2017, a 16-year-old student from Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh, attempted to find a solution to this problem. Meet Kalyani Shrivastava, a Class 12 student at Lokamanya Tilak Inter College then, who built a low-cost cooling device. She also named it the 'Desi AC'. The reported cost of making it was just ₹1,800. Designed with affordability in mind, her innovation attracted attention for its simple construction and solar-powered operation.Who is Kalyani Srivastava Kalyani’s story caught people’s attention because she had looked beyond a school project and considered a problem affecting ordinary households. Rather than trying to replicate an expensive commercial appliance, she explored how readily available materials and basic components could be put together to create a more accessible cooling solution.How Kalyani's ₹1,800 Desi AC worked

Kalyani with her Desi AC

According to published reports, Kalyani's device used a thermocol icebox and a 12-volt DC fan. The arrangement allowed air to pass through the cooling chamber before being directed outside through an elbow-shaped outlet. Reports mentioned that the device could lower the room temperature by around 4-5°C after an hour of operation. It was also described as solar-powered, meaning it could operate without drawing electricity from the household supply when powered by an appropriate solar setup. The combination made the project particularly interesting. Conventional air conditioners required a significantly larger financial investment and consumed electricity during operation. Kalyani's design, by contrast, attempted to make cooling accessible through a much simpler arrangement. It is important to understand that the device was not equivalent to a conventional air conditioner capable of maintaining a set temperature through a refrigeration cycle. It was better understood as a low-cost cooling system that used ice and moving air to provide localised relief.An idea inspired by the heat For Kalyani, the innovation addressed a familiar challenge in the Bundelkhand region. The summers were intense here making everyday life uncomfortable. More for people who couldn’t afford an expensive AC. “For the people of Bundelkhand, it is not possible that everyone can afford an AC, and the heat is unbearable, so I got this idea and transformed it into a reality which is being appreciated a lot,” she had said in an interview. And it was the noble thought behind the project that mattered. Kalyani's experiment offered a reminder that innovation did not always begin in a sophisticated laboratory. title: Kuwait-flagged tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers hit by projectile in Hormuz
text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: A Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker carrying 21 Indian seafarers was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, with all crew members reported safe, Union minister of ports, shipping and waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said. The vessel, M/T Al Dasma, was hit on October 21, amid the ongoing Middle East tensions. The minister said in a post on X that the authorities were monitoring the situation and were in contact with the ship management company to ensure the safety of the crew. "On Oct 21, Kuwait-flagged oil product tanker M/T AL DASMA, carrying 21 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. All 21 of our Indian crew members, along with the rest of the crew are completely safe," Sonowal said. "We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security and wellbeing of our seafarers," he added. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) tracked the incident at a location 11 nautical miles west of Bukha, Oman. According to Times Kuwait, the strike triggered a fire aboard the tanker, which was subsequently extinguished. The vessel remained stationary following the incident, and all crew members were reported safe.

Another tanker incident in Strait of Hormuz

The latest incident comes amid a series of attacks and security incidents involving commercial shipping in the Gulf region. Earlier, on October 16, crude oil tanker MT ST 3, carrying 15 Indian seafarers, was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. Sonowal had said that all Indian nationals aboard the vessel were safe and no casualties had been reported. In a separate incident on October 14, chemical tanker YARA J, carrying nine Indian seafarers, was hit by a drone at Sulina Anchorage off Romania. Sonowal had said that all 24 Indian nationals aboard the two vessels involved in the incidents were safe, with no casualties or injuries. Other incidents have also raised concerns about the safety of Indian seafarers operating in the region. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) had earlier condemned attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on October 11. The ministry had referred to tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, which was reportedly struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage. Nine crew members were rescued, while two remained missing. Another vessel, the Marshall Islands-flagged MT VALTHERA, was struck by an unidentified projectile, causing a fire on board.

title: ‘I will come for them’: Elon Musk threatens Democrats over plans to probe his empire
text:
Elon Musk warns Democrats

Elon Musk has warned Democratic lawmakers against using congressional oversight powers to investigate him and his businesses. On Wednesday, he said he would pursue those he believes are behind such efforts if Democrats gain control of either or both chambers of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. “Live by the sword, die by the sword,” Musk wrote on X, the social media platform he owns, responding to a Politico report detailing Democrats’ plans to investigate him and his businesses, including Tesla and SpaceX. “Those who pick fights with me should understand that I will find out who is really pulling the strings and come for them, not just their puppets,” he added. The remarks come as Democratic lawmakers reportedly prepare to scrutinise Musk’s government role, business dealings and decisions affecting national security, should they secure a congressional majority. Musk worked with US president Donald Trump’s administration through the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which sought to reduce government spending and streamline federal operations. He left his role in late May after his 130-day tenure as a special government employee expired, returning his focus to Tesla and SpaceX. According to the US Government Accountability Office (GAO), the federal workforce contracted by about 250,000 employees during 2025. DOGE has also faced calls for investigations over its access to sensitive government data, the withholding of funds and its role in dismantling the US Agency for International Development (USAID). Democrats have additionally raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest involving Musk’s companies and their multibillion-dollar federal contracts and subsidies. “The sheer number of conflicts of interest are astounding,” representative Zoe Lofgren, the top Democrat on the House Science, Space and Technology Committee, said, according to Politico. The proposed scrutiny also extends to reports that Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink services used by Ukraine’s military. Senator Adam Schiff called for an investigation, in a social media post he wrote, “Either the President was lying or Musk was lying, but the decision to slow down satellite speed and access has life or death consequences for Ukraine.” “This deserves a full investigation by the Senate. Elon Musk should be compelled to testify before Congress and under oath,” Schiff added. Musk has maintained that decisions on Starlink’s use ultimately rest with the US president. Meanwhile, Trump has said he did not know who was responsible for the reported slowdown, while Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was told by secretary of state Marco Rubio that the restriction would be lifted.

End of Article

title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen's $640K charity donations spark scrutiny
text:
Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen (Instagram and Getty Images)

In November 2022, questions emerged about how Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen used their wealth to support charitable causes. A report by the New York Post examined the couple's Luz Foundation, revealing that its donations between 2007 and 2019 were modest compared with their estimated fortune. The findings drew attention to the difference between celebrity wealth and charitable giving, particularly as the former couple had built public profiles around philanthropy, wellness and environmental causes. The report also examined the foundation's spending, its beneficiaries and Brady's separate charitable organisation.

Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen's Luz Foundation faced questions over donations

The Luz Foundation was established in 2007, with Bündchen saying its purpose was to support young girls through grants and other assistance. However, the New York Post reported that the nonprofit distributed $640,402 to various organisations between 2007 and 2019, based on available records. Some of its donations went to environmental groups and organisations supporting meditation, yoga and physical fitness. In 2018, the foundation reportedly gave $300 to Waterkeeper Nicoya Peninsula, $900 to the World Wildlife Fund and $1,000 to the Challenged Athletes Foundation. Its larger contributions included $25,000 to the David Lynch Foundation and another $25,000 to You Go Girl Yoga in 2017. The following year, the Pointing Out the Great Way Foundation received $80,000 from the organisation's $350,000 budget, according to the report. Bündchen had previously spoken about her commitment to charitable work. In a 2015 interview with the Sydney Morning Herald, she explained why her professional career mattered to her philanthropic goals. “My life is devoted to this,” said Bündchen in a 2015 interview. She also described how her work helped fund causes she cared about, challenging the assumption that modelling was her only focus. “My life is devoted to this,” said Bündchen in a 2015 interview with the Sydney Morning Herald. “I know from the outside that people think, ‘This girl just poses for pictures.’ But in my head, I’m thinking the whole time, ‘Okay, if I take this job, then I can have more money to put into this [project].’ So that’s what I’m doing, because that’s [why] God gave me to do what I can do, right?”

Tom Brady's TB12 Foundation also attracted scrutiny

Brady operated a separate charitable organisation, the TB12 Foundation, which aimed to help athletes access health and wellness resources. However, a report by The Daily Beast raised questions about its financial relationship with his for-profit company, TB12 LLC. According to the outlet, the charitable foundation had paid more than $1.6 million to TB12 LLC since its launch in 2015, making the company its largest contractor. title: Patrick Mahomes faces tough Chiefs reality as Brittany Mahomes draws attention
text:
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes (Instagram)

Patrick Mahomes has given the Kansas City Chiefs plenty of reasons to celebrate this season, and that success has brought a welcome change after a difficult 2025 campaign. The quarterback has returned from a serious knee injury and helped his team start the 2026 season unbeaten through five games. However, the celebrations could soon face a test. With tougher opponents approaching, Mahomes must prepare for a demanding stretch that could challenge his patience on the field. If the Chiefs begin to struggle, Brittany Mahomes could also notice a shift in the mood at home.

Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs face a tougher NFL schedule

Kansas City has made an impressive comeback after finishing the 2025 season with a disappointing 6-11 record. Entering Week 7, the Chiefs sit at 5-0 and lead the AFC. title: Historic win! India's Anahat stuns 8-time World Champion Nour ElSherbini
text:
India's Anahat Singh (ANI Photo)

NEW DELHI: Eighteen-year-old Anahat Singh of India produced one of the standout results of the 2026 PSA Squash Tour when she defeated eight-time world champion Nour ElSherbini 11-8, 11-8, 11-7 in just 30 minutes at the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City on Wednesday. The straight-games victory over the top-seeded Egyptian, a World No. 3 and equal of Nicol David’s record for most world titles, propelled the Indian into the quarter-finals of the USD143,500 PSA Gold event and marked the biggest win of her professional career. Singh, born in New Delhi on 13 March 2008 and currently ranked around the world top 15-17, has risen rapidly. She became India’s first World Junior champion earlier in 2026, the first non-Egyptian winner since 2010, and claimed a historic women’s singles silver at the 2026 Asian Games in Japan. Coached by former world No. 1 Grégory Gaultier alongside Saurav Ghosal and Stéphane Galifi, she turned professional in 2023 and has already collected multiple PSA titles while becoming the youngest Asian player to crack the top 20. ElSherbini, a dominant force who has held the world No. 1 ranking for extended periods and won four British Opens, arrived in California as the clear favourite.

Anahat Singh enters quarterfinals

Singh, who has now qualified for the quarter-finals, had earlier eased past Nour Aboulmakarim in the opening round. After the upset she reflected that she had “grown up watching every single match” of the Egyptian, underscoring the personal weight of the result against a player she has long admired. The win arrives as squash prepares for its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028. For Singh, it confirms her ability to trouble the game’s established elite on the senior tour and strengthens her case for further ranking progress. The Silicon Valley Open, staged from 20-24 October, continues to showcase a new generation capable of challenging the long-standing hierarchy led by Egyptian players.

title: French riots and Indian protests linked in same ecosystem: Report
text:
Senior editor Asra Nomani’s investigation says it has identified 101 organisations across nine countries.

A Fox News digital investigation has claimed to have uncovered links between the riots in France and the youth protests in India demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Senior editor Asra Nomani’s investigation says it has identified 101 organisations across nine countries in a “red-green protest ecosystem” (referring to Islamist and communist groups) that are coordinating, organising or amplifying protests in Europe in an expanding protest ecosystem. Her report, “Global Chaos Inc Grows to 101 Groups”, flags Indian Alliance Paris (IAP), a France-based organisation, as “connecting French and Indian protest messaging”, saying it is “partnered with the People’s Forum in Manhattan”. Her story also flags how transnational anti-capitalist organisation Progressive International (PI) explicitly grouped the current protests in France, Spain, India and Albania in an Oct 16 briefing on its website, asking whether the “new rebellions can acquire the organised power to change the conditions that produced them?”. “These are the forces that Progressive International is working to support and connect,” it wrote. “The European unrest is also receiving sympathetic amplification from a network of pro-communist organisations, including BreakThrough News, CODEPINK and Party for Socialism and Liberation, funded and supported by Neville Roy Singham, an American-born tech tycoon who lives in Shanghai,” Nosmani’s report claims. In an interview with BreakThrough News published Oct 14, the wife of Singham, Jodie Evans, co-founder of CODEPINK, said: “I want people to look at France, Spain, and India and just say, ‘Where are we? Why are we not in the streets?’” Another X handle, DisnfoLab, tweeted that Paris-based Indian-origin scribe IAP secretary Joy Banerjee is a former CGT union delegate and has associations with French CommunistParty.

title: Who is Suvarna Raj? Asian Para Games gold medallist who is also an advocate
text:
Suvarna Raj (Image credit: PCI)

Suvarna Raj, a 44-year-old para-athlete from Greater Noida, won gold for India in the women's F54 discus throw at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. She finished first with a best throw of 15.66m, adding another medal to her international career. A wheelchair user, Suvarna has been competing in para-athletics since 2017. She has represented India at three Asian Para Games and several international events. Away from sports, she works to improve accessibility for people with disabilities.

Suvarna Raj wins gold with 15.66m throw

Suvarna produced a steady performance in the final, with four of her six throws going beyond 15m. Her best effort came in the fifth attempt, when she threw 15.66m to take the gold medal. Iran's Shahla Hadidi won silver with 15.45m, while Vietnam's Thi Ngoc Thuy Nguyen finished third with 14.65m. Suvarna's six attempts were 13.68m, 15.09m, 15.05m, 14.57m, 15.66m and 15.19m.

Who is Suvarna Raj?

Suvarna is an international para-athlete who competes in the F54 discus throw category. She is coached by Pintu Nagar and has built her career through regular training and hard work since taking up the sport in 2017. She is ranked second in Asia in the F54 discus throw, according to previously reported rankings. Her latest gold at the Asian Para Games adds to a growing list of achievements.

Suvarna Raj's medals and achievements

Suvarna has won medals at several international competitions.

Asian Para Games: Gold in the women's F54 discus throw in 2026.

Dubai World Para Athletics Grand Prix 2026: Bronze in the women's F54/55 discus throw at the 17th Fazza International Para Athletics Championship.

Canberra Track Meet, Australia, January 2026: Gold in discus throw and silver in shot put.

National Youth Award, 2015: Received the award from the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

Her career reflects years of work in both training and international competition.

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suvarna Raj's work beyond sports

Suvarna is also an accessibility specialist and disability rights advocate. She has carried out more than 1,000 accessibility audits across India to help identify barriers faced by people with disabilities. She has also served as the Election Commission of India's Brand Ambassador for Accessible Elections, supporting efforts to make voting easier for people with disabilities. Her training and competition expenses are supported under the government's Annual Calendar for Training and Competition (ACTC). She has received financial assistance of Rs 7,70,607 under the programme.

What is the F54 discus throw category?

F54 is a classification for seated field athletes whose impairments affect trunk and lower-body function. Athletes compete from a throwing chair and use their arms and upper-body strength to throw the discus. Limited trunk control can affect how they balance and generate power during a throw.

Indonesia would need OEM support (India) to operate, maintain and later for life extension of these (BrahMos and Astra) missiles.

NEW DELHI: Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia Wednesday signed ‘Badr Memorandum of Understanding’ in Doha to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities.
