title: ‘Almost looks fake’: two Sydney beaches closed after whale carcass washes up
text:
A whale carcass has forced the closure of two busy swimming and surfing spots after washing up between Coogee and Maroubra beaches in Sydney – but there are no plans to remove it.

The whale’s heavily decomposed body was found on Thursday morning at Lurline Bay, a rocky cove surrounded by cliffs in Sydney’s eastern suburbs.

It’s believed to be a juvenile humpback.

Local council said nearby Coogee and Maroubra beaches would be be closed until further notice to protect oceangoers as whale carcasses have been known to attract sharks.

“We have cordoned off the area to leave this creature in peace and safe from the attention of people,” Randwick Council mayor, Dr Clare Willington, told reporters.

The council has also contacted Surf Life Saving about introducing extra drone patrols, but Willington said it was a precaution as there had not yet been reports of an increase in shark activity.

Willington said there were no plans to remove the whale and that staff were working with Gamay Rangers about a culturally and environmentally sensitive approach to take.

“This is a natural occurrence and in time nature will deal with the carcass.”

The whale is an important totem animal to the local Bidjigal people, and Gamay Rangers manager Robert Cooley said previous instances where beached animal carcasses were taken to landfill had distressed his community.

However, Cooley said he was not “super confident” the rising tide would return the carcass to the sea.

“We’re got a reasonably strong north-east wind here and a bit of a swell pushing it back up – so that’s going to be a challenge,” he said.

“We’ll just have to wait and see what happens but the animal is in a pretty advanced stage of decomposition, so if it did go out into the ocean, I don’t think it would take long for nature to break it down.”

If intervention is necessary, the rangers would be discussing plans with cultural advisors, he said.

The whale is believed to be a young humpback, but it is difficult to confirm due to its state of decomposition, Cooley said.

The carcass was first spotted on Wednesday in Sydney’s northern beaches near Manly, where attempts were made to tow it out to sea, which is why there are pieces of rope found with the whale.

The council is encouraging residents and visitors to avoid the area and follow directions from lifeguards and authorities.

It comes as authorities are working to free a large whale found stuck in shallow waters off off Turners Beach on Tasmania’s north-west coast.

“Members of the public are asked to avoid the area and not enter the water on the incoming tide due to the anticipated danger,” Tasmanian police said.

‘Almost looks fake’

Curious locals have stopped by Lurline Bay throughout the morning to try catch a glimpse of the whale.

Meeri Pajala, an au pair from Finland who is living in Sydney, said she had never seen anything like this before.

“It almost looks fake to me,” she told Guardian Australia. “That skin looks so weird.”

title: Man fined after 700 frozen and taxidermied animals found on Victorian property
text:
The white-walled room packed with magpies, galahs and sulphur-crested cockatoos, foxes and possums is eerily quiet. As a video pans across shelves filled with these and many other species, there is no flapping or squawking or hissing; the animals are frozen and silent.

They are among the more than 700 native animals that were found illegally taxidermied and frozen that were seized from the property of a Victorian antiques store owner last year.

On Tuesday, 74-year-old Glenn Richard Rollo was fined $10,000 by a court after he pleaded guilty to 13 charges, including selling and possessing protected and threatened wildlife and failing to provide treatment to a sick animal.

The regulator searched his property as part of a broader crackdown on the illegal wildlife trade, executing search warrants for the man’s store and home in April last year. Restrictions on selling and possessing threatened and protected species apply to both living and dead animals.

During their search they found 14 freezers containing animals. Across the property they found hundreds of dead reptiles, native birds and mammals, including 78 emus, 42 brushtail possums and 26 echidnas. They also found the remains of threatened species, including the barking owl, diamond python and Murray River short-necked turtle.

In addition to the dead animals, 15 live reptiles were found in enclosures, including North American red-eared slider turtles and corn snakes. Six of the reptiles, the regulator said, were not being kept under the required animal welfare standards.

The regulator said the man did not have the licence of authorisation under Victoria’s wildlife laws to obtain or possess the animals.

Wildlife in Victoria is protected under the Wildlife Act 1975, which outlaws taking native animals without approval. A commercial wildlife licence or private wildlife licence is required to trade dead animals.

Victorians who wish to taxidermy animals are also required obtain a licence under the conservation regulator.

During an appearance before Kynton local court on Tuesday, magistrate Patrick Southey reportedly told the man: “It is bewildering that a man of your intelligence and knowledge and love of wildlife would arrogantly flout the law so comprehensively.”

The conservation regulator director of regulatory operations, Cal Heppell, said: “The scale of offending in this case highlights why Victoria has strong protections in place for wildlife and animal welfare.

“Our laws and permit systems help protect wildlife from unlawful exploitation, ensure animals are appropriately cared for and safeguard Victoria’s environment and biodiversity from potential threats.

“These requirements are not optional. Anyone who keeps, trades or possesses wildlife must comply with the law.”

title: Man arrested for allegedly making threats at Hannah Beazley’s electorate office while armed with nunchucks
text:
A man has been charged after allegedly threatening staff and wielding nunchucks at the electoral office of the Western Australian local government minister, Hannah Beazley.

The Perth incident came days after the federal independent MP Helen Haines was hospitalised with severe injuries following an alleged attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta in Victoria on Monday.

Electoral staff at Beazley’s Victoria Park office called police after a man caused a disturbance on Wednesday afternoon.

Police said they received reports the man was making verbal threats while in possession of an “improvised martial arts weapon” described as “nunchucks”.

They arrested the 56-year-old man nearby and took him into custody. On Thursday he was charged with being armed in a way that may cause fear, making unlawful threats and cannabis possession. Nobody was injured in the incident.

The man was refused bail to appear at Perth magistrates court on Thursday.

Beazley was not in the office at the time but told reporters on Wednesday evening her staff were “rattled” by the “confronting situation”.

“He was [allegedly] being very threatening. He did want access to me, I believe, but we don’t know his motivations at all,” the minister said.

Beazley said there had been two staff members in the office at the time. The man allegedly attempted to lean through the security screen but her staff were a safe distance away, she said.

“It’s not the first time I’ve had threats made against me.

“My primary concern is the welfare of my staff, obviously. That was very rattling for them. They called the police.”

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said Hannah Beazley was a friend “because I’m a good friend of her dad”, the former Labor defence minister Kim Beazley.

“This is far too prevalent,” Albanese told Perth radio on Thursday. “It’s not who we are as Australians. We can have our discussions and debates and settle those issues at the ballot box.”

‘A unique and pernicious form of attack’

The governor general, Sam Mostyn, speaking generally on Thursday, discussed the gendered dynamics of threats and abuse directed at women in high-profile positions.

“Like any woman who has stepped up into any position across any part of our society, there is a unique and pernicious form of attack that comes our way,” Mostyn told ABC TV.

“I still receive that online. In fact, I was just saddened this morning to see some of the comments on my own Instagram page, in capitals with expletives, once again questioning the very nature of what it is that I do.

“Women across the country know that there are certain things that are reserved for women … that go to our gender and they are often vicious and just despicable.”

A community vigil was held for Haines in Wodonga on Wednesday evening after it was revealed the MP had lost both her legs following Monday’s alleged attack.

title: Sam Wood makes bid for bail to supreme court over domestic violence charges
text:
Former reality television star Sam Wood will go to the Queensland supreme court seeking release from custody, more than two weeks after he was denied bail over allegations he choked and assaulted his wife.

Wood, a 46-year-old wellness influencer from Melbourne, was arrested at Noosa on 4 October on domestic violence allegations.

He was refused bail by a Queensland court after police detailed evidence about a similar incident from Victoria about three years ago and argued that his behaviour was “escalating”.

Wood is now seeking for the bail decision to be reviewed by the supreme court.

Under Queensland’s domestic violence laws, serious charges including “strangulation in a domestic setting” carry a presumption against bail.

Wood appeared in a Sunshine Coast court earlier this month charged with two domestic violence offences: assault occasioning bodily harm and strangulation in a domestic setting.

The court heard that his wife, Snezana, was supportive of the charges and that “there was a cessation of breath” as she was allegedly choked.

“She articulates the banging of her head on the floor. She couldn’t breathe,” police prosecutor Jeanette Grigoris said. “She thought she was going to die.”

In Wood’s first application for bail, lawyer Matthew Cuskelly said his client denied the allegations. He cited a psychologist’s report that said Sam Wood was suffering from “severe depression”.

“He ought to be given the opportunity to engage with mental health professionals,” Cuskelly said.

“And also try to salvage something of his professional reputation and career, which is taking a hell of a beating at the moment.

“Ultimately, as all families have, there was problems. And my client had been enduring the hardship of attempting to quarantine those problems from his family for some period of time. It was agonising.”

Cuskelly cited a psychologist’s report that describes “the difficulty that my client has been enduring in respect of the deterioration of his psychological state”.

“His depression is regarded as extremely severe.”

Wood spent four days in the Maroochydore police watch house after his arrest. He was subsequently held in the high-security Wolston correctional centre near Brisbane.

It is understood the supreme court bail hearing won’t take place until next month, meaning Wood will spend at least a month in custody.

title: Business rights can't disregard sanctity of pilgrimage site: Gujarat government to HC on non-veg ban
text:
The right to business cannot override the religious, historical and cultural character of a pilgrimage destination, the Gujarat Government has told the High Court while defending the ban on non-vegetarian food around the famous Somnath Temple.

The Gujarat HC was on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) hearing a plea challenging a state notification banning sale and storage of non-vegetarian food within a 500-metre radius of the Somnath Temple, a shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva located in Gir Somnath district.

Defending the ban, the government told a bench of Justice Nisha M. Thakor that Somnath cannot be viewed merely as a commercial town, ignoring its extraordinary religious, historical and spiritual significance to millions of Hindus across the country.

"The right to carry on business cannot be stretched into a right to disregard the religious, historical and cultural character of a pilgrimage destination," it said.

Government pleader G.H. Virk argued that no one can claim an absolute fundamental right to sell non-vegetarian food at the temple doorstep or along the sacred routes traversed by millions of Hindu devotees.

Six restaurant owners have challenged the blanket ban imposed by the Gujarat Government two months ago on the sale of non-vegetarian food within a 500-metre periphery of the temple.

The notification identified several routes along the pilgrimage sites within a 500-metre radius where the ban has been enforced.

In its submission, the government pointed out that over 1.16 crore devotees visited the temple in the past nine months alone and underlined that Rishikesh, Haridwar, Amritsar, and Mathura-Vrindavan, among other pilgrimage towns, have similar restrictions on the sale of non-vegetarian food items.

The government further maintained that restaurants remained free to serve vegetarian food at their existing premises or carry on non-vegetarian trade outside the specifically notified areas, subject to applicable laws.

The restaurant owners challenging the ban have argued that they have been lawfully operating for several decades, holding valid licences, and their food establishments are located well beyond the Somnath Temple periphery.

The district magistrate had exceeded the powers by imposing a permanent prohibition upon an otherwise lawful trade, they insisted.

The restaurants are located in one of the half a dozen prohibited zones specified in the government's notification issued in August this year that permanently bans sale and storage of non-vegetarian food items.

The petitioners said the authorities forced them to shut their eateries.

They have challenged the notification, claiming that it violates their rights enshrined in Article 19(1)g of the Constitution and that the authorities cannot restrain a person from conducting any trade or livelihood without assigning a reason.

title: Will get support of 275 MLAs in 294 member Assembly, says West Bengal CM
text:
Asserting that 64 legislators elected on Trinamool Congress tickets would back him in case of a trust vote, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) claimed that the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) would secure the support of 275 MLAs in the 294-member West Bengal Legislative Assembly if a floor test were to be conducted.

“If you have a floor test in the Assembly tomorrow, we will get the support of 275 MLAs. Among them [the MLAs of Trinamool Congress] 64 are ready to raise their hands in our support,” the Chief Minister said, speaking to media persons.

The BJP has 209 MLAs in the State Assembly, after the West Bengal Assembly elections held earlier this year. Of the 80 MLAs of Trinamool Congress who had won, about 65 MLAs supported Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of Opposition and parted ways with Mamata Banerjee.

The remarks by the Chief Minister, that rebel Trinamool MLAs who now are called Democratic Trinamool Congress, will support him evoked strong reaction from the Opposition parties including Mamata Banerjee loyalists. Ms. Banerjee and her loyalists have alleged that the BJP was behind engineering defections in her party.

Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress said that the remarks by the Chief Minister prove that the Ritabrata Banerjee loyalists are “nothing but agents of the BJP”. CPI(M) leader Shatarup Ghosh said that Mr. Adhikari’s remarks should be brought to the notice of courts to remove Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition. Akhruzzaman, the Opposition Chief Whip and member of the rebel faction said that the policy of the party was to keep equal distance from all the parties including the BJP.

While the rebellion in the State Assembly has resulted in Mamata Banerjee losing control over her party name and symbol, 20 Lok Sabha MPs of her party have merged with Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). The The NCPI has requested a two-week extension until November 3, 2026, from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to respond to disqualification petition filed by Mamata Banerjee led faction.

title: SIR Enumeration Form may have violated electoral rules prescribing Form-4 for collecting voter details
text:
Enumeration Forms, which are integral to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, may lack a legal basis under the Registration of Electors Rules (RER), 1960, raising questions about the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) authority to use the format to include or exclude voters from the draft rolls.

Rule 8 of the RER, 1960, prescribes Form-4 issued by the Electoral Registration Officers to collect details of the electors in all kinds of revisions of the electoral rolls, be it Special Summary Revision or Special Intensive Revision.

The rule states that the Electoral Registration Officers may “for the purpose of preparing the roll, send letters of request in Form 4 to the occupants of dwelling-houses in the constituency or any part thereof; and every person receiving any such letter shall furnish the information called for therein to the best of his ability.”

The model Form-4 does not contain pre-printed electoral details or seek information about a voter’s parents/relatives from previous electoral rolls. It has columns for the voter’s name, age, father’s, mother’s, or husband’s name, signature, and date.

On the contrary, the Enumeration Forms distributed by the ECI came with pre-printed details of the electors as per the 2025 electoral rolls. They also include columns seeking voters’ details from the 2002 SIR and, and if the voter was a minor at the time, information about their parents/relatives.

This format, therefore, differs from the one prescribed under the RER, 1960, which also lays down the procedures to be followed during different types of electoral roll revisions.

Rule 25, dealing with the revision of rolls, says that the electoral roll should be prepared afresh during intensive revision, with Rules 4 to 23 applying as they do for the first preparation of a roll.

“Where the roll or any part thereof is to be revised intensively in any year, it shall be prepared afresh and rules 4 to 23 shall apply in relation to such revision as they apply in relation to the first preparation of a roll,” it says.

Since Rule 8, which prescribes Form-4 for collecting voters’ details based on the household survey, falls within the ambit of the rules mentioned above, the ECI’s decision to use a different format has raised questions about its compliance with the rules.

Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C. Sudharsan Reddy called the SIR a “de novo” preparation of electoral rolls. Critics argue that the exercise relies on the 2025 electoral rolls, prepared after a Special Summary Revision, rather than starting afresh through a household-based exercise as envisaged under Rule 8.

Activist Lubna Sarwath has raised serious objections to the CEO’s characterisation of the exercise as “de novo”.

“A de novo process is preparation of voter roll afresh without reference to any previous roll. Whereas the SIR 2026 undertaken by CEO Telangana has references to 2025 and 2002 electoral roll. Pre-printed Enumeration Forms and 2002 Mapping details

title: Mumbai Police issue notices to 24 ''X'' accounts over Sabeer Bhatia's documentary
text:
Mumbai Police have issued legal notices to 24 'X' (formerly Twitter) account holders, days after they shared a controversial documentary posted by tech entrepreneur Sabeer Bhatia.

The notices were issued on October 18, 2026, days after the documentary, allegedly containing false and disparaging claims about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, sparked a controversy.

The notices stated that cyber police had received a formal complaint alleging that multiple X handles had published highly objectionable content targeting a prominent business conglomerate.

The links mentioned in the notices directed to Mr. Bhatia's X account.

The content allegedly had false, misleading, and disparaging statements and allegations against the company, which were circulated without any factual or lawful basis, causing continuous harm to its reputation, goodwill and public image, the notices said.

The publication of such content violated platform guidelines and constituted offenses punishable under Sections 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace) and 356 (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), they said.

The notices asked the platform and account holders to urgently review the objectionable posts and remove or disable access to the content.

While several account holders complied by deleting the video clips, others publicly shared copies of the police notice on their handles, alleging overreach and terming the action as unjust.

“Mumbai Police asked me to take down certain highly objectionable tweets. I have complied and removed them,” Mr. Bhatia, the Indian-American entrepreneur who co-founded the first free web-based email service Hotmail.com in 1996, said on X.

“The “highly objectionable” tweet merely pointed out alleged corruption at the highest levels of power," he said.

The law enforcement agency apparently found the corruption less objectionable than the act of exposing it, he added.

“When pointing out wrongdoing becomes a greater offense than the wrongdoing itself, who is the law really protecting?”

“I regret to inform the good people of India that their fundamental right to free speech is being curtailed by the government. This government is no longer of the people, by the people, or for the people,” he said.

“I am deeply disappointed. In a nation of 1.45 billion people, citizens are afraid to open their mouths and speak about what they see. How can anyone hope to fix India when fear has silenced its people?” he said on X.

A nation cannot progress when speaking the truth requires courage, Mr. Bhatia said.

title: CMRL-Exalogic case: In an update from oral pronouncement, Supreme Court specifies freeze period as 10 days in published order
text:
In an update from its oral pronouncement, the Supreme Court has directed the investigation into the First Information Reports (FIRs) against former Keralam Chief Minister and current Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T. Veena and son-in-law and former Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case to be extended to 10 days.

The oral pronouncement in open court on October 21 had specifically dictated the time of stay as a week or seven days. However, the subsequent published order mentions the period of the stay as 10 days.

“We direct that the investigation in the impugned FIRs shall remain stayed for a period of ten days from today, which, however, shall not be treated as a conclusive opinion expressed on interim relief, and the Division Bench [of the Kerala High Court] shall be entitled to fashion independently such relief in accordance with law,” the order read.

Allowing Mr. Vijayan and his co-petitioners in the Supreme Court to pursue their appeal against a Single Judge Bench order of October 9, 2026, directing the registration of FIRs under the Prevention of Corruption Act, the apex court noted that its observations were limited to the “locus of the appellants to prefer the appeal, and not an expression of opinion on merits”.

On Wednesday, a Special Bench of the apex court comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana convened in the middle of Dussehra vacations to hear 82-year-old Mr. Vijayan, who voiced fears of imminent arrest, and his two family members.

Mr. Vijayan and the other two co-petitioners, represented variously by senior advocates Siddharth Luthra, N. Hariharan and Krishna Dev Jagarlamudi, had submitted they were neither made parties nor heard by the Single Judge Bench before the registration of the FIR was ordered on October 9.

Setting aside the October 15 order of the Kerala High Court Division Bench refusing them leave to appeal the October 9 order, the apex court had directed the Division Bench to hear the appeals filed by Mr. Vijayan and the other two petitioners against the registration of the corruption FIR. Justice Bagchi reminded the State that no matter how low or high a person was, he was subject to the rule of law and principles of natural justice.

“We will not disturb the FIR, but we will stall the investigation… Further, we are sending this case back to the High Court for adjudication,” Justice Bagchi observed.

title: Schools closed in five Tamil Nadu districts after overnight rain
text:
Schools in Tirunelveli, Tenkasi, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari and Tirupattur districts of Tamil Nadu will remain closed on Thursday (October 22 2026) following overnight rain, district officials declared.

Tirunelveli District Collector Anand Mohan and Tenkasi District Collector Ranjeet Singh declared holidays for schools in their respective districts following overnight rain. Thoothukudi District Collector Vishu Mahajan and Kanniyakumari District Collector M. Prathap also announced holidays in view of widespread rainfall. A holiday was declared for schools in Tirupattur district as well.

According to data from the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), several districts received moderate to heavy rainfall till 6 a.m. on Thursday. Mamallapuram recorded the highest rainfall at 9 cm, followed by Tenkasi and Sattankulam in Thoothukudi district, which received 6 cm each. Tirunelveli, Mayiladuthurai and Tiruvarur recorded 5 cm each.

Several other districts, including Coimbatore, Nagapattinam, Salem, Ranipet and Kanniyakumari, also received rainfall.

The RMC forecast light to moderate rainfall in Cuddalore, Dharmapuri, Kanniyakumari, Tirunelveli, Tirupattur, Tiruvannamalai and Viluppuram districts till 10 a.m. on Thursday (October 22).

title: Parvinder Singh Jhota: Who was the anti-drug activist, why was he killed
text:
Parvinder Singh Jhota, a prominent anti-drug activist, was shot dead in the Mansa district of Punjab on Tuesday (October 13, 2026), sending shock waves and sparking outrage across the State.

Known for raising his voice against the illegal sale of addictive substances at chemist shops, Jhota was shot in broad daylight inside a medical store at a busy marketplace in Mansa last week.

Who was Parvinder Singh Jhota?

Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, had been running a campaign against drug abuse in Mansa and neighbouring areas in Punjab through ‘Nasha Roko, Rozgaar Do’ (stop addiction, give employment) campaign for the past few years.

A star athlete during his school and college years, he got the name ‘Jhota’, meaning bull, as a State-level boxer. As per The Hindu report, he once said he started using chitta, a heroin-based opioid, the first time he went to jail for a street fight. He quit in 2015 after a friend died from an overdose in front of him.

Jhota started the ‘Nasha roko, rozgaar do’ campaign, with the help of Punjab Kisan Union leader Sukhdarshan Singh. Along with his supporters, he raided chemist shops and homes suspected of selling illicit drugs and counselled people against selling or consuming them. His popularity grew, and civilian “Nasha Roko Committees” sprang up in villages across Mansa and Bathinda, carrying out similar searches and raids on suspected drug outlets.

Why was Jhota killed

Jhota, who was known for exposing the illegal sale of addictive drugs at chemist shops, died after being shot at by a medical store owner in Mansa district.

The activist was questioning the medical store owner over the sale of certain drugs to a man, and also recording the argument on his mobile phone, when he was shot at.

Ashwani Kumar, the store owner who allegedly opened fire at Jhota, was taken into custody from Rajasthan’s Salasar.

The Police asserted that preliminary investigation into the murder of Jhota has pointed towards personal enmity as the motive behind the crime. Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Harjeet Singh then said, “Preliminary investigation indicates that the murder stemmed from personal enmity. An incident involving the two individuals had also taken place in 2023, and this previous dispute is being examined as part of the investigation.”

The feud between Jhota and the accused goes back to July 2023, when the activist allegedly garlanded the chemist with shoes, accusing him of selling illicit drugs.

What is the latest update in Jhota case

The incident, which took place while Jhota was hosting a Facebook Live, triggered a political slugfest in Punjab, which goes to polls early next year.

The CBI has registered a case into the murder of the anti-drug activist and taken over the investigation. Notably, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab announced the CBI probe on October 20, hours before Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s visit to Punjab where he also met with Jhota’s family.

title: Controversy erupts after ‘protest’ photographs by Priyanka Gandhi’s son allegedly get removed from Bikaner House exhibition
text:
Controversy erupted after visual artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, took to social media on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) and alleged that the management of Bikaner House has removed many of his photographs documenting recent protests and youth movements in India.

Titled “No Idea Is Final”, the exhibition featured wildlife photography, abstract art and pictures documenting recent youth movements in India.

In a post on Instagram, Mr. Vadra wrote, “Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show 'No Idea Is Final”, which opens this evening at 7 p.m.. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently the content is objectionable.”

He further alleged that the authorities also directed him to remove two photos of the Tiranga.

“I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag,” he said, adding that the show will go on in part for now, and he will find another venue and display the entire collection of protest photos.

According to reports, Mr. Vadra was told by the organisers, that it was not the appropriate time to display “such images”.

He argued that a detailed proposal and outline of the exhibition was shared well in advance with the management.

Responding to the development, Congress MP and chairman media and publicity department Pawan Khera questioned the “offence” in clicking protest.

“When even the Tricolour isn’t safe from the censor’s scissors, perhaps the problem isn’t the art. It’s the regime,” he wrote on X.

He added that the photographs merely documented protests, and not one was derogatory or inflammatory.

“Imagine a government so threatened by ideas that not just protests, but even photographs of protests — and the Tricolour itself — have become intolerable. The end must be close,” he said.

title: Namma Metro Phase 3: Karnataka issues third land acquisition notification for Orange Line package
text:
The Karnataka government has issued a preliminary notification for the additional acquisition of land required for Package 1 of Namma Metro Phase 3, also known as the Orange Line, between J.P. Nagar 4th Phase and the Mysuru Road side of the corridor. This is the third land acquisition notification issued for the package.

Dated October 16, 2026, and published in the Karnataka State Gazette, the notification identifies properties measuring a total of 13,409.05 sq. m. across 11 entries. It provides details of the properties proposed for acquisition, including identification numbers, survey numbers, land extent and information on existing structures.

The properties are located in Kaggalipura, Jaraganahalli and other localities along the proposed metro alignment.

“This is the third land acquisition notification issued for Package 1 of Corridor 1 of Namma Metro Phase 3. The notification is part of the land acquisition process for the 44.65-km Phase 3 project, which will expand Bengaluru’s metro network with 31 stations across two corridors,” a Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) official said.

Meanwhile, more than two years after the project received approval, BMRCL recently invited expressions of interest from Indian and international consultancy firms to serve as the General Consultant for Phase 3. The consultant will provide technical and project management support for the development of both corridors.

Corridor 1 will run 32.15 km from J.P. Nagar 4th Phase to Kempapura and have 22 stations, while Corridor 2 will cover 12.50 km between Hosahalli and Kadabagere, with nine stations.

JICA assistance sought

BMRCL has applied for a Japanese Official Development Assistance loan of ¥102.48 billion from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to part-finance the two corridors.

“The proposed JICA loan will meet only a portion of the overall project cost, while BMRCL will arrange the balance funding. Consultancy appointments and procurement for components financed through the loan will be carried out in accordance with JICA guidelines,” the official said.

The General Consultant will review engineering designs, prepare and finalise tender documents, assess bids, and assist with contract negotiations. Once construction begins, the consultant will also monitor quality standards, workplace safety and environmental compliance, coordinate contractors’ work, and support testing and commissioning before the lines become operational.

Phase 3 is expected to improve connectivity across Bengaluru and ease congestion on busy stretches, particularly along the western Outer Ring Road, Magadi Road and other major arterial roads.

The project also envisages integration with existing and under-construction metro stations, BMTC bus terminals, Indian Railways stations and proposed suburban rail stations being developed by K-RIDE.

title: U.P. CM Yogi issues directions for strict legal action in cases of land encroachment
text:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Mr. Adityanath issued directions during a Janata Darshan held at Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur.

“The Chief Minister instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Strict legal action must be taken against them. If a dispute concerning land or property is familial in nature, the concerned parties should be brought together and the matter resolved through mutual dialogue,” reads an official statement.

The Chief Minister added that no one should suffer injustice. Every victim must be assisted with sensitivity. “Those who, for any reason, have been deprived of the benefits of government schemes should be provided with those benefits,” added Mr. Adityanath.

During the Janata Darshan, some people approached the Chief Minister seeking financial assistance for medical treatment. The CM assured them that the government would provide all possible assistance for their treatment. “While forwarding their applications to the officials, the Chief Minister directed that the process of preparing treatment estimates be completed as soon as possible and that the estimates be submitted to the government,” added the official statement.

During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister told officials, “Resolving everyone’s problems and bringing public welfare and happiness into citizens’ lives is the government’s commitment. In accordance with this commitment, the resolution of grievances must be ensured by treating every victim with sensitivity,”.

During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister met around 200 people. He personally approached the people seated in front of the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan in the temple premises and heard their problems one by one. While forwarding everyone’s applications to the concerned officials and directing them to ensure prompt and satisfactory resolution, he assured the people that the government is committed to resolving the problems of every victim.

title: 'Much, much bigger leaders than me': Dipke hails Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka after release
text:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) welcomed the Special Executive Magistrate's order releasing its leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, with founder Abhijeet Dipke calling them "much, much bigger leaders" than him.

CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said the decision should have come earlier.

Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were released after the expiry of judicial custody in connection with the October 14 protest at Jantar Mantar.

In a social media post, Mr. Dipke expressed his willingness to follow orders of Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka.

"Saurav and Ashu are not just better but much, much bigger leaders than me. Happy to follow your orders, my leaders. Jaan hazir hai!" Mr. Dipke said.

He added a playful remark in Hindi, saying, "Lekin iske baad mere bina garden mein koi akela nahi ghumega!!! (But after this, don't go alone in the garden without me)".

In another post, Mr. Dipke shared a photograph of Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka and captioned it "My leaders".

Earlier, Ms. Singh said, "We welcome the decision. I think this decision should have been taken long ago, but it is not too late".

She said the police had sought a five-day extension of their custody citing an imminent threat, but the defence argued that there was no imminent threat and no call for a protest.

"You cannot take that as an assumption and extend the judicial custody. The SEM has taken that on record," she said.

Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were initially remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after being detained for allegedly entering the denotified protest site of Jantar Mantar and violating peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on October 19.

Asked about the Delhi High Court's observations earlier in the day, Ms. Singh said the judge was entitled to express an opinion, but the CJP did not necessarily agree with it.

"They have given their opinion. It is an observation, an oral observation.”

“There was no discussion on the merits in the Court. We were here today for the release of Saurav and Ashutosh, for which we had been trying for the past week. Finally, that has happened," she said.

Ms. Singh said the team was emotional and eager to meet the two leaders.

"The team is also very emotional right now. They also want to meet them because everyone has not met them for a long time," she said.

She expressed hope that nobody's liberty would be curtailed in the future over issues related to sureties or technical reasons, adding that the release order had been sent and the team hoped to see Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka soon.

Earlier, the High Court declined to interfere with Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka's judicial custody, asking them to await the SEM court's decision and approach the appellate court if their grievance persisted.

title: BJD slams BJP for personal attack on Naveen over his demand for CJP leaders’ release
text:
Former Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik’s support for Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka of the Cockroach Janata Party has triggered a major political controversy, with the Odisha unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party accusing him of attempting to create a Bangladesh-like situation in the country. The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), on the contrary, has strongly condemned alleged personal attacks against the veteran leader on Wednesday (October 21, 2026).

“The detention of CJP leaders Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka has raised serious questions about democratic rights and freedom of expression. An impartial investigation is essential to establish the truth in this matter. In a democracy, the rule of law and the protection of citizens’ rights must remain paramount,” Sanjay Kumar Dasburma, BJD vice president, said, addressing a press conference on Wednesday (October 21).

Soon after Mr. Patnaik demanded review of judicial custody and release of two CJP leaders on Tuesday (October 20), the Odisha unit of BJP came up with a reaction on ‘X’ saying “Naveen wants to create a situation like Bangladesh in the country to shine his own politics!”

Besides, BJP State President Manmohan Samal said the BJD leadership had become directionless and was clueless about their positioning in politics.

“Hoisting the national flag, even in a prohibited area, should not warrant such prolonged detention. The judiciary and the executive must rise to the occasion to ensure that the youth of this country do not lose faith in the rule of law and constitutional rights,” BJD supremo had written on ‘X’.

“The manner in which BJP State President Samal has criticised Mr. Patnaik over his position on the Special Intensive Revision issue raises serious questions about political decorum and democratic values. The ruling party has every right to disagree with the views expressed by a Leader of the Opposition. However, resorting to personal attacks instead of responding with reason and facts is entirely unacceptable,” said BJD vice president.

“Before calling Naveen Patnaik directionless, the State government must provide clear answers to the people about its own direction and policies. The interests of the nation and the dignity of the Constitution are equally important to everyone. However, no political party has an exclusive right to issue certificates of patriotism,” he maintained.

Mr. Dasburma remarked, “If there is disagreement with a leader’s views, the response should be based on reason and facts. Targeting the Opposition under the guise of nationalism merely for political gain must stop.”

Posing a flurry of questions to the BJP, the BJD vice president said, “Do you want the Opposition to agree with everything the government says? If not, why resort to such language whenever the Opposition expresses a different opinion? In a democracy, asking questions is not a crime; it is a responsibility.”

title: Haryana Congress flays BJP government over its failure to keep poll promises
text:
Congress party on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) flayed the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), describing the functioning of the Haryana government as a complete failure and alleging a clear gap between their tall pre-poll promises and the people’s present hardships.

Senior Congress leaders in a series of press conferences across the State, criticised the government over

Deteriorating law and order, farmers’ grievances, unemployment, corruption, poor healthcare services and drug abuse are among other issues. The Congress leaders cornered the BJP on the government’s completion of two years of its third term in Haryana.

Haryana Congress In-charge Sanjay Dutt said the government has to be held accountable on issues of employment, inflation, farmers’ problems and public welfare. “What happened to the promises? Where is the development, and when will the youth, farmers, women and ordinary citizens get relief?” he said.

Mr. Dutt added that the Congress Party will not allow the people’s voice to be silenced. “We will intensify our struggle for Haryana’s rights, the protection of democracy and accountability from the BJP government. In the second year of the BJP’s third term, Haryana is in total distress. BJP must give an account of their two years to the People of Haryana,” he said.

In Sirsa, Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee president Rao Narender Singh said that instead of merely making claims about its achievements, the government must present a factual account of its election promises before the people.

“The BJP government had completed two years of its third term, but people across the State continued to struggle with crime, unemployment, farmers’ problems, corruption and the poor State of public services. During the Assembly elections, the BJP had made major promises to every section of society. The government must now explain how many promises have been fulfilled.”

In Chandigarh, Kumari Selja said the BJP had promised to provide women ₹2,100 every month. The government should clarify how many women were currently receiving the amount, how many were eligible in total and when the remaining eligible women would start receiving the benefit. Similarly, the government had announced free medical treatment of up to ₹10 lakh for every family. It should disclose how many families had actually received treatment coverage and how many patients had benefited.

Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda said in Rohtak that young people in Haryana deserved employment, farmers deserved fair prices for their crops, and ordinary citizens deserved a safe environment.

title: Surrendered Maoist found dead in rehabilitation facility: Police
text:
A former Maoist — who had surrendered earlier this year — allegedly hanged himself in a government rehabilitation facility in Chhattisgarh’s Bijapur on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), said a senior police officer.

The reason behind the alleged step is not yet known.

The 26-year-old deceased Narsu Boddu took the alleged step exactly a week before he was due to complete his vocational training in agriculture as part of the government’s initiative to assist such surrendered Maoists in reintegration and achieving financial self dependence.

Before his surrender in February 2024, Boddu was a section deputy commander rank Maoist before his surrender along with other Maoists this February, said Superintendent of Police (Bijapur) Umesh Prasad Gupta.

“Around 7 a.m., fellow surrendered Maoists in the facility informed the police that Baddu was found dead in one of the bathrooms. We sent the body for post-mortem and are investigating further. Forensic teams also visited the spot,” said Mr. Gupta.

No note was found from the step. Asked if there was any history of confrontation with fellow inmates or any other history of illness, the SP replied that neither was the case. “Further probe is on,” he added.

Boddu had been lodged in the rehabilitation facility, one of the multiple such centres in different districts of the Bastar region where several waves of surrenders have happened since early 2025, since July 23 this year.

“Boddu is survived by his father, wife and two children. His mother and brother died by suicide in the past,” according to the police.

The Centre had set a deadline of March 31 this year for the elimination of Maoism from the country, following which Union Home Minister Amit Shah had declared the country free from Maoism.

title: West Bengal government sets up SIT headed by retired justice to probe Durga Puja pandal stampede
text:
The West Bengal government on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) issued an order setting up a special Investigation Team (SIT) to undertake a comprehensive, impartial and thorough inquiry into the stampede at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Pandal which claimed 19 lives on October 17.

The six-member SIT will be headed by Justice (Retired) Anindita Roy Saraswati, with several other officials of the state government and a representative of the National Disaster Response Force.

After the incident, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the SIT will be headed by a sitting judge of Calcutta High Court. However, on October 20 a Division Bench presided by Chief Justice Ravindra V. Ghuge said a sitting judge of the High Court could not be appointed to head an inquiry, in accordance with a Supreme Court directive.

The SIT shall submit its report, together with its findings and recommendations, to the State Government within three months from the date of issue of this order, the notification by the West Bengal government said.

The order signed by State’s Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal said that the SIT will ascertain the time, location and manner in which the initial crowd surge occurred and developed into a stampede and examine the prevailing weather conditions, including relevant meteorological reports and rainfall or thunderstorm bulletins, and their possible impact on crowd movement.

The SIT will also inspect and assess the condition and adequacy of passages, barricades, stairways, gates, emergency exits and other structural and access arrangements at the pandal and examine whether permissions were granted in accordance with applicable rules and whether adequate crowd-management plans and disaster-management plans.

Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja Pandal, inaugurated by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari himself, drew large crowds this season until the tragedy occurred on the evening of October 17. Most of the deceased were women and children. Seven persons, including the organizers of the Durga Puja Pandal, have been arrested.

Questions have been raised over the role of Kolkata Police which was responsible for crowd management at the pandal. The SIT does not have a member of Kolkata police.

Meanwhile, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, for the second consecutive day, met the families of the deceased. Mr. Adhikari visited the New Barrackpore and New Town areas and handed over a cheque for ₹25 lakh to the kin of the deceased. The state government has promised compensation of ₹25 lakh to the next of kin of the deceased.

Kunal Ghosh, spokesperson of Mamata All India Trinamool Congress said that unless the BJP leaders who were in-charge of the Durga Puja pandal are arrested the SIT has no real purpose. Mr. Ghosh said that poor home guards and members of private security agency are being made a scapegoat in the stampede incident.

title: Kochi pharma firm loses ₹99 lakh in alleged impersonation fraud
text:
A pharmaceutical company based in Kochi has allegedly been duped of ₹99 lakh by an unidentified fraudster who impersonated the chief executive officer of the firm on WhatsApp.

The Kochi City Cyber police have registered a case in connection with the incident based on a complaint. The alleged incident took place on October 16.

According to the FIR, the accused hacked a mobile phone used by the company’s accounts department and managed to save a phone number as that of the CEO, using the WhatsApp display picture used by him.

The fraudster then allegedly communicated with the accounts department staff, posing as the CEO, and convinced a female staffer to transfer the amount to another account. The case has been registered under relevant sections of the IT Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

title: Steep steps, wide gaps make train travel a challenge for elderly, differently abled
text:
Despite the State’s ongoing efforts to create barrier-free surroundings for persons with disabilities, some long-distance and local trains continue to pose serious accessibility challenges, with steep and unsafe steps making boarding and alighting difficult, particularly for elderly and differently abled passengers. Complaints from senior citizens’ forums and various railway passengers’ associations have so far failed to bring about a change.

Many passengers have to seek the support of fellow passengers to board or alight from trains. During peak hours, their slow entry and exit interrupt the smooth movement of other passengers waiting to board. Those travelling with heavy luggage also find it difficult to negotiate the steps.

“The senior railway officers are yet to conduct a thorough inspection of the situation, though they frequently audit other safety measures. We feel that the new coaches are also being built without considering the needs of elderly people,” says K. Mohandas, a member of the All-Kerala Railway Passengers Association. He adds that the risk of slipping and falling increases during the rainy season and rush hours.

Passengers have also flagged the wider gaps between footboards and platforms, which make them difficult to navigate. They say a team of engineers will have to re-inspect the footboard designs for any flaws in execution. The gaps are dangerously wide at some stations due to changes in platform construction.

“As most of the trains have old coaches, it may not be practical to change all the footboards at once. What we seek is the possibility of gradual replacement in such a way as to make the railways elderly- and differently abled-friendly,” says Abhilash Thekkel, a differently abled passenger from Feroke. He points out that at least three or four coaches on a train can be considered for the redesign of footboards.

Women passengers have also complained about the “risky footboards” on some trains, saying they increase the risk of slipping and falling. Semeena Mujaeeb, a frequent traveller from Kozhikode city, says mothers travelling with young children face considerable difficulties negotiating the “inaccessible” steps.

Meanwhile, railway officials say they are unable to take an immediate decision, as train footboards are designed to be narrow to maintain structural clearance and prevent trains from hitting station platforms. They add that several passengers have raised the same issue and that it will be brought to the attention of higher authorities for possible action.

title: Student killed after being hit by train in Kozhikode
text:
A college student was killed after being hit by the Vande Bharat Express near the Iringal railway gate between Vadakara and Payyoli in Kozhikode district on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) evening.

The deceased was identified as Nandana, a native of Iringal. She was studying at a college in Angamaly and had returned home for the holidays.

According to police sources, the accident occurred while she was attempting to cross the railway tracks. The Vande Bharat Express, which was travelling towards Thiruvananthapuram, struck her, killing her on the spot, they said.

Police and railway officials reached the spot and completed the inquest procedures. Her body was handed over to her relatives after the post-mortem examination at Kozhikode District Hospital.

title: Greens oppose move to revive Cheekkalloor airstrip project in Wayanad
text:
Greens have opposed an alleged move to revive the proposed Cheekkalloor airstrip project in the ecologically sensitive Wayanad, warning that it could displace hundreds of families, destroy paddy fields, and threaten water security in parts of the district and adjoining areas of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

The Wayanad Prakruthi Samrakshana Samiti (WPSS) has urged the Keralam government to abandon the project.

WPSS president N. Badusha said the airstrip in Kaniyambetta grama panchayat would require the displacement of more than 1,000 families, including around 50 Adivasi families displaced by the Banasurasagar and Karapuzha project. It would also entail the reclamation of around 500 acres of cultivable paddy fields.

The samiti alleged a conspiracy involving land mafias, real estate agents, the Chamber of Commerce and those in power to push through a project that “would bring no tangible benefits to Wayanad.” It warned that any attempt to impose the project without public consent would be resisted in association with farmers.

An earlier move by the then Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government to construct the airstrip had triggered widespread protests more than a decade ago. The project was subsequently halted after then Leader of the Opposition V.S. Achuthanandan visited the site.

The proposal regained momentum in 2022 when a meeting of political parties chaired by Kalpetta MLA T. Siddique, now Agriculture Minister, decided to expedite steps to establish the airstrip. Earlier this year, KIIFCON-RITES, a joint venture firm, was entrusted with conducting a feasibility study of potential sites after it won the bid last June. Following the UDF’s return to power in May this year, demands to implement the project gathered pace, with Cheekkalloor remaining a priority site. Last week Kaniyambetta grama panchayat passed a resolution urging the government to establish the airstrip at Cheekkalloor.

The renewed push has prompted opponents, including farmers, to plan protests and conventions.

Mr. Badusha alleged that the proposed project would violate the Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act.

“Over the past 25 years, Wayanad’s paddy cultivation area has shrunk to one-tenth of its former extent. The Cheekkalloor fields are among the district’s largest and most fertile remaining paddy tracts. Most of the land required for the proposed airstrip comprises paddy fields that would have to be filled and raised by 6.5 metres. These fields are vital to Wayanad’s water security,” he said.

Filling up the Cherupuzha river, which flows through the tract, could also cause flooding in neighbouring areas and seriously affect the flow of the Kabani river, with unpredictable consequences for Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, Mr. Badusha added.

The Cheekkalloor region is also a major dairy farming centre. Farmers fear that the loss of paddy fields would deal a severe blow to cattle rearing.

title: Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace
text:
After two days of diplomacy – in Norway's capital and Russia's St Petersburg – is the war in Ukraine any closer to ending?

"Good and constructive" is how Norway's prime minister described Tuesday's talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, US President Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and European representatives.

In Oslo, the idea of a trilateral meeting at leaders' level was floated. The hope was that Steve Witkoff's trip to Russia would pave the way for President Vladimir Putin, Zelensky and Trump to meet and agree an end to the fighting.

But Putin has shown little desire to share a table with Zelensky - unless that table is in Moscow.

The Kremlin says it may be willing to resume trilateral talks next month in Abu Dhabi, but only at the technical level.

In a post on X, Steve Witkoff himself conceded that "there is still important work to do", though he claimed "President Trump remains committed to seeing this war end..."

For me, the most telling statement of the day was from Vladimir Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov. He took part in the St Petersburg talks.

Ushakov said that Steve Witkoff had told President Putin about the discussions in Oslo and (as Witkoff viewed them) "new approaches from the Europeans and Kyiv".

The Kremlin adviser was clearly unimpressed by what he heard.

"In terms of resolving the Ukraine crisis, there wasn't much there that was useful," commented Ushakov.

Later Russian state TV asked him about the prospects for peace.

"I don't know how close we are getting," Yuri Ushakov said, "but things are moving in that direction."

All rather vague.

It seems that President Putin doesn't feel under pressure right now to end the war.

He knows that Ukraine's air defences are under severe strain.

He knows that winter is coming and may well view the cold weather as an opportunity to pound Ukraine into submission.

He knows, too, that there is a US president in the White House who clearly wants a bigger, better, more profitable relationship with Moscow.

title: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery
text:
Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said.

Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican.

"A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added.

The 71-year-old was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital over the weekend four days after his operation - stopping to speak to well-wishers as he left the grounds.

It comes as he held his first weekly general audience since leaving hospital at St Peter's Square on Wednesday.

The surgery, which took place on 13 October and lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung.

The pontiff himself had announced during his weekly Sunday prayers that he would be having the procedure - telling those gathered in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung.

He said at the time that it had been caught "at an early stage".

Images shared days after his operation, on Friday, showed the Pope celebrating Mass from the hospital wearing green vestments and standing behind a makeshift altar.

On the same day, the Vatican said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone to urge a ceasefire in the blockaded Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow the delivery of food aid, and to call for "dialogue and peace".

The pontiff had a similar phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday.

Those close to the Pope have also previously said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America which is planned for early November.

title: 'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken
text:
Wangaratta has been thrust into an unwelcome spotlight this week. Residents in this rural Victorian town are used to catering to tourists passing through on their way to regional wineries, or music lovers visiting its annual jazz and blues festival.

Instead, locals are fielding endless questions about their MP - and having to explain to strangers what it all means for the town's nearly 30,000 people.

They are clearly in shock about what police say was a targeted and deliberate attack on Helen Haines on Monday afternoon, when she was struck by a car just outside her office.

"People are simply dumbfounded and finding it very hard to fathom the scale of this tragedy," Australia's Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who represents King Charles, said at a press conference on Wednesday.

The independent federal MP had to have both legs amputated after she was airlifted to Melbourne. But the "two most important parts of Helen", her heart and her mind, were in "good shape", her husband Phil Haines said.

The MP isn't a divisive figure, locals tell the BBC, and no one can understand why she was allegedly targeted.

"Everyone knows Helen," says Jane Hill, who owns a giftware shop a few hundred metres down the town's main street from where Haines was hit.

"She is a such a good person in our community. She'd go to everything - celebrations, funerals, she's one of those genuinely kind people - and so are her family."

Local man Brendan Nugent, whose father has been good friends with Haines for decades, faces at least three charges over the alleged attack including intentionally causing harm and appeared in court on Wednesday. Police say they are considering further charges, including attempted murder.

First elected to parliament in 2019, Haines is best known for her years-long efforts to establish a national anti-corruption commission.

She was spurred on by a series of major political scandals which, in her words, saw "public money spent for political gain", disproportionate spending on "shiny infrastructure projects" in marginal seats and decisions benefitting big donors over ordinary people.

The commission finally opened in 2023 under Anthony Albanese's Labor government.

Haines has also helped to secure funds for housebuilding, railway improvements and health infrastructure in her region, which she argues has long been sidelined by policies favouring cities.

On a spring afternoon in Wangaratta, nobody seemed to have a bad word to say about the former nurse and midwife turned politician.

Local Mayor Irene Grant described her as "warm", "cheerful" and "committed", and pointed to her record on climate action and Indigenous rights.

In a police update on Wednesday, Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush said she'd given "wonderful support" to local police when two officers were shot dead in the nearby town of Porepunkah last year.

Bystanders who came to Haines' aid recalled how she thanked them even as she lay severely injured.

title: Ex-prosecutor charged with treason in Mexico over US drug raid
text:
Federal prosecutors in Mexico have charged a former state prosecutor with treason for allowing US agents to join a raid on a suspected drugs lab in April without proper authorisation.

César Jáuregui Moreno served as attorney general of the northern border state of Chihuahua from 2023 to this year.

The involvement of Americans came to light after two US agents said to have worked for the CIA died in a car crash in Chihuahua along with two Mexican law enforcement officers.

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy Ramos said Jáuregui had allowed foreign agents to carry out activities reserved for Mexican authorities and had failed to share information. Jáuregui has denied the allegations.

The former prosecutor, who is a member of the conservative opposition PAN party, was arrested at the weekend. A court hearing is scheduled for Saturday.

A judge must still determine whether there is enough evidence to proceed with the case, Reuters news agency reports.

Jáuregui also faces state-level charges in Chihuahua, including of abuse of public office. In a court hearing for those charges on Sunday, he denied that he instructed or consented to the involvement of US agents in the operation.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has come under pressure from US President Donald Trump to crack down on drug trafficking but has repeatedly declined offers of US-led counter-narcotics operations in the country.

She has been adamant that foreign officials can only operate on Mexican soil if given prior clearance by the federal government, and has insisted the Latin American nation's sovereignty should not be breached.

The crash occurred on 19 April, when a convoy returning from an operation targeting suspected methamphetamine labs in a remote, mountainous area veered off the road and plunged into a ravine.

Two members of the Chihuahua State Investigation Agency were killed along with the Americans, officials said.

At the time, in his capacity as state attorney general, Jáuregui told a news conference that the Americans had been "instructor officers" from the US embassy engaged in "training work as part of the general and normal exchange we have with the US authorities".

US media have reported that the two individuals worked for the CIA as part of an expanded effort to combat narcotics trafficking in the region.

title: Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' about controversial Ohio attack ad
text:
US Vice-President JD Vance has urged fellow Republicans to stop "whining" about a controversial attack ad that featured a Democratic candidate's estranged mother calling her a liar.

While campaigning in Ohio for Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for governor, Vance said he was "a little bit disgusted" by criticism from members of his own party.

In the ad, Donna Arthur, the mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton, said her daughter "lied her entire life". It does not mention that Arthur's husband was charged with raping Acton when she was a child.

The Ramaswamy campaign have claimed credit for the ad, and have paid millions to have it advertised around the state.

Acton's brother is among those who have condemned the ad, saying turning alleged sexual assault into "a political talking point" was a "despicable low".

Acton and her brother were removed from their mother's custody when her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested and charged in 1978.

That is when she last spoke to her mother, Acton said in an interview with The Vindicator, an Ohio news outlet. The Arthurs fled Ohio and Cledith Arthur was never prosecuted on the rape charge. He died in 2004.

When the ad featuring Donna Arthur was initially released to social media on Monday evening, it did not say who the video was paid for or authorised by. Ramaswamy confirmed on Tuesday that it came from his campaign, and he later pledged to spend $4m (£2.9m) to further air it.

The move has drawn a bipartisan backlash.

Former South Carolina Governor Nikki Haley, who ran against Ramaswamy for the Republican nomination for president in 2024, said "he's a bad guy. It's a shame he continues to get away with it".

Vance, when asked by BBC News if he thought the ad was appropriate, answered: "It's not really my concern."

"What is my concern is who's going to govern the next generation of American government."

He also said he was "a little bit disgusted" by members of his own party who "are whining more about that advertisement than they are about what the congressional Democrats and other Democrats want to do to the United States of America".

Vance, a former Ohio senator, later defended the ad at a rally for Ramaswamy, saying: "Now the media and the Democrats in the state of Ohio are obsessed because guess what? Vivek Ramaswamy had the audacity to run a TV commercial which calls it out like it is, and calls Amy Acton a liar."

When asked about Ramaswamy's ad on Wednesday, Trump said: "I know nothing about it. I heard the mother went very rogue on the daughter."

He added: "It's a very unusual situation to have a mother hate a daughter that much. But I dont think that has anything to do with Vivek."

Acton's team released its own campaign ad on Tuesday, a video featuring her brother, Philip Stearns, recounting childhood abuse and saying "Amy always got the worst of it".

"Shame on Vivek," he says in the 30-second clip. "It's the contempt he has for Amy. It's the contempt he has for Ohio."

title: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
text:
Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with the largest ever fine against it for its business practices.

A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

"The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices".

Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico". The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful.

The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.

New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That firm utilised data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.

New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced. The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too.

Meta disputed those accusations. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added.

Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.

They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.

"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said on Wednesday.

"Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable."

The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta. Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.

Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.

He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years", stretching from 2010 to 2021.

title: Nigeria's first Ebola patient holidayed in Uganda, officials say
text:
Nigeria's first confirmed case of Ebola since the outbreak in East Africa began in May is the wife of a diplomat who travelled to Uganda's capital for a holiday, the head of Africa's health agency has told the BBC.

The woman is originally from Uganda but based in Abuja, where she fell ill three days after arriving home in the Nigerian capital on 3 October, according to Dr Jean Kaseya from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

Nigeria's health minister has confirmed to the BBC the 42-year-old patient spent two and a half weeks in Kampala, adding that she also made a two-hour stopover in Ethiopia's capital on her return.

"She's stable, she's improving," Muhammad Ali Pate said.

The authorities were working to prevent the virus from spreading and had identified 44 people who had been in contact with the woman, who tested positive for Ebola on Tuesday, the minister said.

"Not all of them have been in close proximity. We cast the net wide so that we contain it as broadly as possible," Pate told the BBC.

None of the contacts, who are now in isolation, are known to have developed symptoms, including the person the patient travelled with, the health minister said, adding that the woman had not travelled outside Abuja since landing.

Kaseya explained that the woman had first developed symptoms on 6 October when she had sought medical help.

"She went to the first hospital, a private hospital, thinking that she had malaria, and then she went to the second private hospital. She was admitted on the 11th," he told the BBC's Newshour programme.

Malaria is endemic in Nigeria and its symptoms - a high temperature, headaches, muscle aches, vomiting and or diarrhoea - are similar to those of Ebola.

After her condition failed to improve, public health authorities were alerted on Monday 19 October, Pate said.

Her diagnosis was confirmed the next day following three laboratory tests, he said.

The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks.

Ebola is a rare but deadly disease, external caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo, which began in May, has claimed at least 4,600 lives, with more than 9,500 cases recorded, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reports, external.

Shortly after the outbreak was announced, it was also reported in Uganda, where at least two people died. Uganda declared itself free of the disease in August after its last patient was discharged.

There have been conflicting accounts about the patient in Nigeria and her movements.

title: India 'cockroach' leaders who called on election chief to quit are freed from jail
text:
Two leaders of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) have been freed from jail a week after they were arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka walked out of Tihar jail hours after a magistrate ordered their release. They had been detained by police and jailed after they crossed barricades and climbed over the locked gate at Jantar Mantar.

The historic venue was recently removed from a list of designated protest sites.

The men, who denied wrongdoing, have been calling on India's chief election commissioner to resign. Critics accuse the commission of manipulating voter rolls to benefit India's governing party, charges the commission rejects.

A special executive magistrate court in Delhi, passed their release order, legal news website Bar and Bench reported.

After bail was granted, Das told reporters from a police van: "Truth alone triumphs. Long live the revolution."

title: Trump administration seeks Supreme Court approval to build Big Bend wall
text:
The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to allow it to resume plans to build a border wall through the Big Bend region of West Texas, as part of its anti-immigration policy to strengthen security on the border with Mexico.

The Justice Department filed an emergency request on Wednesday asking the court to lift a federal judge’s injunction in a lower court that has halted construction while a lawsuit against the project, brought by an environmental group and other challengers, plays out.

list 3 of 3ICE tactics spark debate before pivotal US midterm elections
