The Department of Homeland Security plans include vehicle barriers, patrol roads, lighting and detection technology in and around Big Bend National Park.

Big Bend has about 805km (500 miles) of border, and, according to opponents of the project who have sued the administration, accounts for about 1 percent of migrant arrests.

Landscape, historic church

The lawsuit, filed by plaintiffs including the Center for Biological Diversity and a Big Bend-area river guide, seeks to preserve the landscape, protect a historic church, and challenge the federal government’s waivers of environmental and historical laws to fast-track the $1.7bn project.

Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and current Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who issued the waivers between February and July, found the region to be an “area of high illegal entry”, requiring additional barriers to control the border.

US District Judge Kathleen Cardone issued an injunction in El Paso on October 2 halting work “until and unless Defendants comply with all applicable laws,” she wrote in her order.

In a later opinion, the judge found that the waivers exceeded the authority of Noem and Mullin.

The Justice Department in its request urged the Supreme Court to pause or overturn Cardone’s injunction.

The Supreme Court has not yet responded to this appeal.

“Even assuming that the secretary’s waiver authority implicates a question of ‘vast economic and political significance,’ Congress did clearly authorize the secretary both to build border barriers and to waive legal requirements in order to facilitate their expeditious construction,” the Justice Department wrote.

In August, the administration paused construction in Big Bend after the project drew bipartisan criticism over its potential impact on the park’s landscape and wildlife.

title: Can Trump deport Congresswoman Ilhan Omar?
text: US President Donald Trump says Congresswoman Ilhan Omar could face jail or deportation as federal authorities investigate allegations surrounding her US citizenship. Omar denies wrongdoing and accuses the administration of political intimidation. With the midterm elections approaching, what could happen next? Al Jazeera’s Noor Wazwaz explains.

title: Russia frees American Stephen Hubbard after 4 years behind bars
text: US citizen Stephen Hubbard has been freed from a Russian prison, four years after being convicted of being a mercenary for Ukraine, a claim he denies. The 74-year-old’s release coincided with US envoy Steve Witkoff’s visit to Russia to try and get Moscow to rejoin peace talks.

title: Tigray resumes daily life amid fears of wider war
text:
Mekelle, Ethiopia- In Mekelle, shops are reopening, and banks are resuming services, but residents remain anxious about what comes next. Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters retook the Tigray regional capital on October 4, as renewed fighting raised fears that the region’s fragile recovery could be derailed once again.

Tigray, in northern Ethiopia, is still recovering from the 2020–2022 war between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the region’s dominant political movement. For residents, the return of fighting has brought new uncertainty over jobs, education, security and the future.

Daily life resumes, but hardship remains.

Businesses and financial services are gradually reopening in Mekelle, but many households are struggling to afford necessities. Delayed salaries have left public employees struggling to cover food, rent and school costs, while years of conflict have depleted family savings.

“Things may be reopening, but that does not mean our problems are over. We still have expenses every day, and without our salaries, it is difficult to know how we will manage,” said Gebregziabher, a public servant in Mekelle.

The funding crisis has affected the wider public sector. In March, Tigray’s interim administration said it could no longer cover monthly salaries for about 137,000 civil servants because expected federal budget transfers had not arrived. In April, the regional finance bureau reported an 8.5-billion-birr (about $52,000) funding shortfall affecting salary payments and development projects.

For many residents, the reopening of businesses offers only a partial return to normality. Without reliable incomes and greater security, everyday expenses remain difficult to manage.

Students fear losing more time

For students in Tigray, renewed fighting has revived fears of another interruption to their education. Many already lost valuable study time during the previous war and worry about falling further behind.

In Adigrat, Shewit, a grade 10 student, said uncertainty about classes and security had left him worried about his future.

“I have already lost so much time because of the war. I am afraid that if our education is disrupted again, I will lose another year and fall further behind,” he said.

Some university students have left Tigray for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia’s capital, to seek transfers to other public universities. The Ministry of Education announced temporary placements at universities elsewhere in the country for students enrolled at institutions in Tigray. More than 5,000 returning students had applied by September 17–18, according to reporting on the ministry’s programme.

Abel, a third-year student at Axum University, travelled to Addis Ababa to request a transfer.

“I didn’t want to leave, but I also can’t keep putting my education on hold. I came to Addis to see if I can transfer to another university and continue my studies. I just want to finish what I started,” he said.

title: What is the FDLR, and why does its anti-Tutsi ideology endure?
text:
Musanze, Rwanda – The Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) was built on an ideology that cast the Tutsi as enemies, according to four of its former senior officers, who say they were taught to hate them long before the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi ethnic group.

“In our history and ideology, Tutsis are referred to as ‘snakes’,” said Anastase Munyaneza, a former FDLR major general.

“The analogy is that if a snake bites you, it injects poison and you die. Therefore, it is better to kill the snake before it bites you.”

The former officers say such ideas were reinforced through Rwanda’s political and military institutions before the 1994 genocide and persisted among those who fled into neighbouring Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), after the Rwandan Patriotic Front (RPF) took control of Rwanda in July 1994.

More than three decades later, the FDLR remains a source of regional security concerns, with its presence in eastern DRC a major point of contention between Kigali and Kinshasa.

Al Jazeera met the four former officers, who defected from the FDLR, returned to Rwanda and underwent rehabilitation at the Mutobo demobilisation centre. Their accounts offer an insight into the origins of the group’s ideology, its development in exile, and the networks that have helped it survive.

Where did the ideology come from?

The roots of the anti-Tutsi ideology described by the former officers stretch back decades, to a period when ethnic identities became increasingly politicised and institutionalised in Rwanda.

In November 1959, a Hutu uprising helped bring about the overthrow of Rwanda’s monarchy. The period was also marked by violent attacks on Tutsis, the killing of hundreds and the forced exile of thousands to neighbouring countries.

Before colonial rule, Hutu and Tutsi identities were shaped by social, political and economic relationships. Under Belgian rule, these distinctions were increasingly formalised. In the early 1930s, the colonial administration introduced compulsory identity cards classifying Rwandans as Hutu, Tutsi or Twa, reinforcing distinctions that became increasingly rigid.

By independence in 1962, about 120,000 people, mostly Tutsi, had fled the country. Exiles in Tanzania and Zaire who sought to return staged attacks between 1962 and 1967. According to the United Nations, each incident was followed by retaliatory killings of large numbers of Tutsi civilians in Rwanda, prompting further waves of refugees.

By the end of the 1980s, about 480,000 Rwandans were refugees. President Juvenal Habyarimana argued that population pressures and limited economic opportunities made it difficult to accommodate large numbers of returning Tutsi refugees.

In 1988, exiles in Uganda founded the RPF to secure their repatriation, according to the UN.

Lieutenant Colonel Idrissa Bizimana said the exiles who launched attacks against Rwanda were branded “Inyenzi”, meaning cockroaches.

title: Qatar, France call for opening of Hormuz and Gaza ceasefire implementation
text:
Qatar and France have called for freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and the implementation of the so-called ceasefire in Gaza, after the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, met French President Emmanuel Macron in Doha.

A joint statement on Wednesday said the two leaders stressed the importance of restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz “without constraints or fees”.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Macron lines up more Gulf diesel as France battles soaring fuel prices

list 2 of 3As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future?

list 3 of 3Iran’s enriched uranium re-emerges as point of contention in US talks

end of list

Qatari mediator Ibrahim bin Sultan Al Hashmi had said on Tuesday that diplomatic efforts are ongoing to de-escalate regional tensions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Wednesday that “Iran is prepared to give diplomacy another chance.”

“The two leaders condemned Iranian military attacks against countries in the region which constitute a serious breach of international law,” according to the Qatari-French statement.

Heeding ‘agreed arrangements’

The two leaders also called for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza “in accordance with the agreed arrangements”, as well as the urgent, safe and unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid “without conditions or restrictions”.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said on Monday that about 1.4 million people in Gaza, roughly two-thirds of the population, face acute food insecurity at crisis levels or worse.

“France and Qatar reiterated their opposition to any annexation of the West Bank and called for an end to Israeli settlement policies and settler violence,” the statement added.

On Lebanon, the two countries backed full implementation of the Trilateral Framework Agreement to restore Lebanese sovereignty, disarm Hezbollah and secure a complete Israeli withdrawal.

They also warned against a security vacuum following the end of the UN peacekeeping mission’s mandate, calling for continued international support for Lebanese authorities and armed forces.

On Syria, both countries said they were ready to jointly support stabilisation and economic recovery projects in coordination with Syrian authorities.

Beyond regional issues, Qatar and France agreed to expand defence, security and economic cooperation.

Macron’s regional tour, which also included Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, aimed to strengthen strategic and economic partnerships and support efforts to restore regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Colombian president purges National Museum of works promoting ‘communism’
text:
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has announced he is spearheading a cultural “counterrevolution” that includes removing dozens of exhibits from the National Museum, drawing protests and comparisons to United States President Donald Trump.

De la Espriella, a conservative Trump ally, said last week that he wants to prevent cultural institutions from being taken over by what he calls “atheist social communism”.

list 1 of 3Colombia inaugurates embassy to Israel in Jerusalem

Since then, exhibits have been taken down that once addressed the history of social movements, including feminist and LGBTQ activism, and Colombia’s political violence.

The changes have sparked protests by civil rights groups, artists and students who have accused the government of censorship and warned that it could erase important parts of the country’s history.

Dozens of demonstrators gathered on Wednesday outside the National Museum in downtown Bogota as riot police guarded its entrance.

“I find it outrageous that they want to erase part of our history,” said Azul Riascos, a history student.

He said the government was promoting a vision of Colombia as exclusively white, Catholic and Spanish-speaking. That image, he explained, excluded Black, Indigenous and LGBTQ communities.

Gimena Sanchez-Garzoli, director for the Andes at the Washington Office on Latin America, a research and advocacy organisation, said the Colombian government’s approach reflects a broader trend among Trump allies who are copying US political narratives and strategies.

Trump has been fiercely critical of Washington museums, particularly those tied to the Smithsonian Institution.

The White House released a report in July branding leaders of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History as radical activists and ordered signs installed outside the museum telling visitors that some exhibits are inaccurate.

Nearly three months later, those signs still haven’t been installed. The museum’s director, Anthea Hartig, told Congress that the White House report “does not fairly or accurately characterise the full body of work at the museum”.

Sanchez-Garzoli said Trump’s cooperation with allied Latin American governments on security and counternarcotics efforts also has an ideological dimension.

“These are imported narratives about terrorism and about being ‘woke’,” anthropologist Arturo Sanabria said during Wednesday’s protest, describing the Colombian government’s approach as a form of neocolonial intervention.

Colombia’s Culture Minister Paola Holguin said the government was reviewing and redesigning exhibitions and curatorial practices at other museums overseen by her ministry.

title: George W Bush’s brother backs Democrat James Talarico in Texas Senate race
text:
Neil Bush, brother of former Republican President George W Bush, has said that he voted for the Democratic candidate James Talarico in a crucial race for the United States Senate.

In a social media post on Tuesday, Bush said he voted for Talarico due to concerns about the Republican candidate, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Trump launches midterms campaign blitz amid record low approval ratings

list 2 of 3‘Bordering on angry’: The state of play as US midterms enter final month

list 3 of 3Democrats gain momentum in pivotal US Senate and governor’s races in Texas

end of list

Talarico and Paxton are in a tight race for Texas’s open Senate seat. Democrats are hoping to seize control of the 100-member Senate in the November 3 midterm elections, when 35 seats will be on the ballot.

Bush’s endorsement of Talarico is the latest sign of division among Texas Republicans.

Bush comes from a prominent Republican family: not only was his brother a president, but his father, the late George HW Bush, was too.

“My concerns about his judgment and conduct are hardly mine alone,” Bush wrote. “He was impeached by the Republican-controlled Texas House, although subsequently acquitted by the Texas Senate.”

To explain his decision, Bush pointed to Paxton’s divisive track record, including efforts to support President Donald Trump’s false claims about the 2020 presidential election.

“I have been deeply troubled by Paxton’s conduct as Texas Attorney General, particularly his decision to challenge the results of the 2020 presidential election in other states in an effort to help Donald Trump remain in power,” Bush said.

“I believe that effort was an affront to our democratic institutions and the peaceful transfer of power.”

His brother, the former president, has largely receded from political life and has declined to endorse candidates in recent elections. Before serving in the White House from 2001 to 2009, George W Bush was governor of Texas.

But George W Bush’s daughter Barbara Bush has also shown her support for Talarico by donating to a political action committee backing his campaign.

Texas has long been considered a Republican stronghold, and Democrats have not won a Senate race in the state since 1988.

But polls show Talarico locked in a close race with Paxton, who defeated incumbent Senator John Cornyn in the Republican Party’s primary run-off on May 26.

Paxton had secured an endorsement from Trump on May 19, days before the run-off.

In a statement, Trump criticised Cornyn as “not supportive of [him] when times were tough”, while praising Paxton as a “MAGA Warrior”.

Some Republicans have expressed frustration over Trump’s intervention on Paxton’s behalf, given the vulnerabilities posed by his state impeachment and other scandals.

A Marist poll released on October 14 found Talarico winning 47 percent of the vote compared to 45 percent for Paxton.

text:

All of the wounded, whose injuries range from minor to critical, were transported to hospitals to receive medical attention, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said in a statement on Wednesday.

title: World leaders warn of security flaws found in PHP programming language
text:
Authorities in Europe, Asia and other continents have temporarily taken some government websites offline to protect against newly discovered security vulnerabilities in a programming language used to power the vast majority of sites on the internet.

On Wednesday, vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language prompted a rare public warning from the United States National Security Agency (NSA), which advised taking websites offline if they could not be updated immediately.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Scientists urge tighter AI controls to prevent global cyber risks

list 2 of 3Israeli ad-tech firm helped place spyware on Al Jazeera devices

list 3 of 3How Israeli firm’s ‘zero-click’ malware attack poses global security risk

end of list

“Effective Immediately, all organizations using PHP for their systems are advised to be prepared for an update addressing two critical vulnerabilities,” the NSA said in a social media post.

In Germany, the Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernisation said it took some websites offline as a preventative measure. France’s Ministry of the Interior deactivated the official websites for local administrative offices.

Authorities in Belgium, the Netherlands, Finland and the Czech Republic also said they had shut down websites to apply a security patch to close the PHP loophole. Even Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi posted on social media to warn about the PHP risk.

Cybersecurity experts discovered the pair of vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, with the help of artificial intelligence (AI) models.

Researchers at security firm Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first flaw on August 11. Wiz, a security firm owned by tech giant Alphabet, reported the second vulnerability on August 24.

Wiz said the findings “rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history”.

The underlying flaws had been present for decades, the firm said, but proving they were exploitable required a chain of steps “at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve”.

AI tools let researchers find vulnerabilities in software by testing more attacks than human programmers can alone.

Volunteers maintain the PHP programming language, and the nonprofit PHP Foundation said on Wednesday that the flaws were among the most severe it had encountered.

The group urged anyone administering a website to update their code immediately.

Both flaws rely on accessing parts of memory without proper authorisation and exploiting that access to run malicious code. The two loopholes mean an attacker can remotely run commands on a server running old PHP code over the internet, without needing a password or legitimate account access.

The PHP Foundation also warned that AI would make such security weaknesses easier to find. It called on tech companies to mount a coordinated response to avoid major disruptions to online services.

title: US accuses Canada of election interference ahead of midterms
text:

But the US embassy identified public statements about the tariffs as being attempts to sway the November 3 midterm election.

Among the politicians singled out in the fact sheet was Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly. The fact sheet pointed to comments Joly made in August about responding to Trump’s tariffs.

“We’re also targeting products that will target states in the US. And so we’re being wise and strategic to put political pressure,” Joly said at the time.

The embassy also took issue with Joly’s meetings with Democratic officials in Boston and Chicago in September. When asked by a reporter what she thought might happen with regard to tariffs if Democrats won the midterms, she said, “That’s exactly why I’m meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates.”

Joly has rejected the suggestion that her actions could amount to interference, saying Canada would never meddle in US elections. She said her meetings with US politicians, both Democratic and Republican, were about building Canada’s economy.

“Fundamentally, what I’ve done in the US is to attract investments,” she told reporters on October 14.

The embassy also pointed to Ontario Premier Doug Ford’s calls for retaliatory measures on US products, as well as his government’s advertising campaign against Trump’s tariffs, launched last year.

The campaign, which featured clips of former US President Ronald Reagan criticising tariffs in a 1987 radio address, prompted Trump to call off trade talks with Canada in October 2025.

While the embassy laid out several examples of Canadian officials trying to influence US trade policy, it didn’t explain how those efforts amounted to interference.

Other instances of alleged election interference included Liberal MP Anthony Housefather saying he had campaigned in Florida on behalf of Democratic Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz, ahead of her primary election in August.

title: What happened during Witkoff and Kushner’s latest meeting with Putin
text:
United States special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have wrapped up their latest meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin with the release of a retired American teacher from Russian custody.

On Wednesday, Witkoff visited with Putin at the Constantine Palace in Saint Petersburg, while Kushner attended virtually.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Putin and Zelenskyy back three-way US peace talks on Ukraine

list 2 of 3US envoy Witkoff calls Russia’s Putin a ‘humanitarian’

list 3 of 3Russia to send first diesel tanker to the US amid Trump deal

The two special envoys have taken a leading role in conflict negotiations under US President Donald Trump. Their last meeting with Putin came during a trip to Moscow in September.

The latest talks come as the Trump administration intensifies its efforts to secure a peace deal to end Russia’s nearly five-year-long war against Ukraine. The war began when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of the Eastern European country in February 2022.

But there are growing concerns in Kyiv that the Trump administration is backing away from its support of Ukraine.

Trump has fostered warm relations with Putin, and critics fear that he may be willing to yield to Russian demands to reach an agreement that would end Europe’s bloodiest conflict since World War II.

Here’s what took place during the meeting:

Putin agrees to resume peace talks with Ukraine and US

The Russian president agreed on Wednesday to resume US-mediated peace negotiations with Ukraine for the first time in months.

A US official told Al Jazeera that Witkoff and Kushner proposed a “trilateral meeting at the technical level” that would focus on guaranteeing the security of Ukraine and Russia once the war had ended. The Ukrainians accepted the meeting when they met with the Americans on Tuesday in Oslo, Norway.

The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, just days before the US and Israel launched their war against Iran.

The Kremlin, according to the Reuters news agency, said the new talks with Ukraine and the US may take place in Abu Dhabi and could start as soon as next month.

Russia frees retired US teacher

Wednesday’s meeting began with a goodwill gesture from Russia: the release of Stephen Hubbard, a retired American teacher who has been held in Russia for more than four years.

Hubbard, 74, was arrested in 2022 and sentenced to more than six years in a Russian prison after he was accused of being a Ukrainian mercenary. The US has argued the former teacher was wrongfully detained.

Trump, who made a direct appeal to Putin for Hubbard’s release, posted on social media Wednesday that Russia did not ask for a prisoner swap “out of respect for” him.

A US official said Trump spoke with Hubbard by phone and reiterated his “unwavering commitment” to bringing home all Americans who are wrongfully detained abroad.

Hubbard is headed back to the US where he will be reunited with his family.

title: Pope Leo needs no further treatment after cancer surgery, doctors say
text:
Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment for lung cancer after confirming the disease had not spread following recent surgery, the Vatican announced in a statement from doctors.

“A subsequent oncological evaluation has confirmed that no further therapy is required,” the pope’s lead surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Luigi Carbone, said Wednesday.

Recommended Stories

list of 3 items

list 1 of 3Pope Leo recovering well after cancer surgery, Vatican says

list 2 of 3Pope Leo resumes work in hospital while recovering from surgery

list 3 of 3Pope Leo to make public appearance Sunday, first since cancer surgery

end of list

The 71-year-old pontiff had the lower lobe of his right lung surgically removed on October 13 and was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer. Leo was discharged from Rome’s Gemelli Polyclinic on Saturday, four days after his operation, and the Vatican said he would gradually resume his activities. On Wednesday, he returned to St Peter’s Square for his weekly audience with pilgrims.

Found by chance

Additional treatment is generally offered in cases where follow-up testing finds signs that the cancer has spread, such as through the lymph nodes, or if other signs indicate that it might be particularly aggressive. Surgery often can be enough when tumours are caught very early, as the Catholic leader appears to have had, when the nodule was initially found during another unrelated exam.

In an interview with Vatican News on Saturday, Margaritora, the chief thoracic surgeon at Rome’s Gemelli hospital, confirmed that the nodule was found by chance during routine abdominal examinations, and that the pope had not been experiencing any symptoms.

The pope carried on his official business while in the hospital, including a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. He has appeared strong in two public appearances at the Vatican since his surgery: the traditional Sunday blessing from a window overlooking St Peter’s Square and Wednesday’s longer audience in the square, greeting the faithful from around the world.

“Thank you! Thank you for the support of your prayers,” Leo exclaimed to the audience.

It appears that the Catholic leader remains committed to his November 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

Leo’s lead surgeon told Vatican News that there was “no clinical reason” to prevent the trip, which includes a dozen flights, two helicopter rides and high-altitude stops.

title: Nigeria’s first Ebola case matches DR Congo strain, health officials say
text:
Nigerian health officials say test results have confirmed the country’s first case of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which is behind a major outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), marking the disease’s first spread to West Africa in the current outbreak.

The case involves a woman who travelled from Uganda to the capital, Abuja, on October 3, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said.

She was tested for Ebola on October 19 after health officials learned she had recently travelled to Uganda, one of the countries affected by the current outbreak. Officials confirmed the positive result on Tuesday.

“We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, director of the public health laboratory service at the NCDC, said on Wednesday.

The World Health Organization (WHO) also confirmed the strain, for which there is neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.

‘Multi-organ failure’

An unnamed official told the AFP news agency that the woman is a diplomat whose condition has deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”.

Ayoade Alakija, a Nigerian physician who co-chairs a G7 committee for investment in global health, said that it had taken 12 days since the woman fell sick for her to be tested for Ebola, potentially exposing many other people to the infection.

Nigerian authorities have identified 44 contacts, most of them healthcare workers. They include the patient’s husband, a Swiss national, who lives with her in Abuja.

Officials are also tracing passengers who travelled with her from Uganda to Nigeria but do not believe she was symptomatic during the flight.

Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate told public broadcaster NTA that the woman was in isolation and receiving treatment.

Earlier cases

In 2014, the first Nigerian case, detected in Lagos, raised fears the virus would spread rapidly, but it was brought under control within three months, resulting in 20 infections and eight deaths.

That epidemic killed more than 11,000 people across West Africa between late 2013 and 2016.

The WHO says Nigeria is the fifth country to detect the virus in the outbreak, which this past week widened across the continent, with Kenya in the east reporting nine cases since October 6.

Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Director-General Jean Kaseya said on X on Wednesday that the outbreak was “no longer one country’s fight”, and that he would hold a meeting of Africa’s health ministers next week to strengthen the cross-border response and review hospital capacity.

The DRC is the epicentre of the outbreak, its deadliest on record.

title: Canadian publisher drops writer Thelyson Orelien over AI use in novel
text:
The publisher of best-selling Haitian-Canadian writer Thelyson Orelien says it has severed its professional relationship with the author after confirming he used artificial intelligence to help write his novel, “It Was Either That or Die”.

Boreal said on Wednesday that it conducted a further investigation after allegations surfaced in September to determine whether AI was used to write the novel.

Recommended Stories

“New information, confirmed over the past few days, indicates that artificial intelligence was used in the writing process” of the novel, a Boreal statement said.

Orelien had previously denied allegations surrounding his breakthrough novel, and last week, the Canadian publisher said it was standing by the 38-year-old writer.

Boreal said it did not know the extent of AI’s use in the writing process “and we will likely never have a definitive answer”.

It said it gathered all the working versions of the novel and hired an outside party to analyse the various drafts.

“The results obtained this week revealed traces of AI tags in the metadata of certain documents,” Boreal said.

The publisher said it had tried to work with Orelien to gather the evidence necessary to prove his innocence.

That effort was inconclusive, and Orelien “subsequently announced that he would not provide any further information,” the publisher said.

‘Slander and heresy’

Orelien’s novel about migration, known by its original French title “C’etait ca ou mourir”, had been scheduled for translation in more than 20 countries.

France’s top book prize, the Goncourt, removed “C’etait ca ou mourir” from its shortlist after tests with the AI detector Pangram indicated a 100 percent probability that it contained computer-generated text.

But Orelien called the allegations “slander and heresy” in a statement sent to AFP earlier this month.

“Here and there I did use tools for research, particularly for foreign idioms,” he said.

“But not a single sentence in this book was created by a machine, nor the meaning or the structure of a story that comes from my gut,” Orelien said.

On Wednesday, he stood firm, telling the French newspaper Liberation that he had used AI “in the creative process” for “historical research”.

The author said he began writing the book in late 2017, before AI services such as ChatGPT were widely available.

When the allegations first surfaced in September, Orelien said he suspected racism was behind the attacks on him.

NEW DELHI: India slammed Pakistan at the United Nations, questioning Islamabad's record on religious freedom and the protection of minorities while pointing out its failure to safeguard vulnerable communities at home despite criticising New Delhi. Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief on funeral rights in exceptional circumstances on Thursday, India's first secretary to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said, "In Pakistan, the number of minorities is shrinking, and their rights are regularly abused. A state that cannot ensure the safety of its own minorities has no standing to lecture India. " She also said human suffering should not be used to serve political interests and called for a more impartial approach to reporting violations of religious freedom. The remarks come against the backdrop of concerns over alleged forced conversions, abductions and marriages involving minority girls in Pakistan, particularly in Sindh. Separately, experts cited by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights warned that coercion and weak legal safeguards were enabling forced conversions through marriage, particularly among Hindu and Christian communities. The experts emphasised that conversion must be voluntary and that child marriage undermines consent under international law.

‘Rights of terrorists’ and their victims

The Indian representative also questioned the report's emphasis on the funeral rights of terrorists, arguing that the suffering of victims and their families should not be overlooked. She then invoked the 1999 Kargil conflict to challenge Pakistan's position on burials and religious rights, saying Islamabad had refused to accept the bodies of some of its soldiers killed in combat. “It is deeply ironic that a state that did not even accept the bodies of its own soldiers who were killed in combat in 1999 in Kargil, unabashedly speaks with fervour on faith, religious freedom and burials,” Mangalanandan said. She added that the Indian Army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic customs.

title: 'Lifting sanctions will make Putin stronger': Zelenskyy differs with Trump on Russia
text:
Zelenskyy says Ukraine needs better missiles as US pushes for peace deal with Russia

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said his differences with US President Donald Trump are “not about personalities”, warning that lifting sanctions against Russia would strengthen President Vladimir Putin and undermine efforts to end the war. In an interview with CNN in Kyiv on Thursday, Zelenskyy said he was opposed to easing sanctions on Moscow, arguing that Putin had no intention of ending the conflict. “My attitude to Putin is very clear. title: Only ‘sanatanis’ will touch Durga idols during immersion: Bengal CM Suvendu
text:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that only those who believe in Sanatan Dharma can touch Durga idols during immersion

KOLKATA: Only those who believe in ‘sanatan dharma’ will be allowed to touch Durga idols during immersion, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Wednesday while inspecting security arrangements at Baje Kadamtala Ghat. Dismissing suggestions that the directive had a communal intent, Adhikari said the measure was aimed at upholding the sanctity of immersion rituals. Adhikari said Kolkata Police commissioner Ajay Nand has been instructed to maintain a record of those involved in immersion. “Only those who believe in Sanatan Dharma should touch the idols. I have told the CP to record the names of those who come here. They must also be identified,” the CM said. “To preserve sanctity, we must follow traditions, scriptures and norms followed for thousands of years,” he added. The CM’s remarks drew strong reactions, with opposition netas accusing him of promoting religious exclusion and violating constitutional principles. “Does he (Adhikari) have a list of who is a ‘sanatani’ and who is not? Can he explain how someone becomes a ‘sanatani’? He has no answers,” former CPM MP Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya said. He also alleged that the CM was acting in accordance with the RSS agenda. Bengal Congress senior Suman Roy Chaudhuri condemned Adhikari’s remarks, arguing that they ran contrary to India’s constitutional commitment to pluralism. Trinamool’s Baiswanor Chatterjee criticised the CM, saying, “One cannot understand Hinduism with such a narrow mindset.” Earlier, citing traditions, Adhikari had said trolleys, and not cranes, would be used in immersions and DJ music would be banned. On Wednesday, cranes were out and rail-mounted trolleys took their place at immersions in Hooghly. Special mechanical ramps, trolleys and conveyor systems have been installed at major immersion ghats like Baje Kadamtala, Nimtala and Gwalior ghat. Blaring loudspeakers, unlike in previous years, were absent. In some pockets, however, fireworks shattered the relative quiet. Environment activist Naba Dutta of Sabuj Mancha said, “We have been protesting the use of DJ music, but for the first time, our wishes have been fulfilled.” Sources at KMC confirmed that around 2,800 idols were immersed on Wednesday. While Doighat recorded immersion of around 700 idols, Baje Kadamtala recorded 560 immersions. Nimtala and Judges Ghat saw a surge in immersions. A majority of puja organisers stayed away from immersions. On Thursday afternoon, however, a TOI team saw heaps of idol structures at Baje Kadamtala Ghat. Holding low tide responsible for this, a KMC official said, “We are waiting for high tide to clear the accumulated structures.”

End of Article

title: Why US banks are blocking AI agents from accessing customer accounts
text:
Representative image

Major US banks have been blocking third-party artificial intelligence (AI) agents from accessing customer accounts and carrying out transactions, as concerns grow over the risks posed by autonomous AI tools, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters. Banks are increasingly wary of AI agents that can perform tasks on behalf of users, particularly when the technology interacts with financial accounts and could take actions beyond a customer's instructions. An Axios report on Thursday said major lenders had detected unauthorised third-party AI agents operating within customer accounts, with some attempting to take actions that appeared to be independent of user instructions. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The banks taking steps to contain the risks include Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo, according to the Axios report. In some cases, customers have shared their login IDs and passwords with AI agents, prompting banks to flag and block transactions, a person in the banking industry said. However, such transactions cannot be considered unauthorised if customers have voluntarily shared their credentials, the person added. Morgan Stanley has blocked third-party agents from accessing its platforms but has not seen instances of unauthorised or rogue AI agents, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Banking executives warn of AI agent risks

The issue has drawn attention from senior banking executives, who have raised concerns about AI agents acting independently while carrying out tasks on behalf of customers. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said earlier this month that the bank was developing tools to manage the risks associated with AI agents performing tasks autonomously. "We're not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that's just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan," he said. Charles Schwab CEO Richard Wurster also said earlier this month that the brokerage was blocking unauthorised agents to retain control over authentication and the customer experience. "I get a report every day tracking how many times we've had to block one of the different agents, and it's not many because I think people aren't using it in that way in their financial life. We are blocking it because we want to have control over authentication and the experience," Wurster said. The developments underscore growing concerns across the financial sector about the security implications of AI agents that can interact with online services, access sensitive information and initiate transactions on users' behalf.

End of Article

title: 7-magnitude earthquake strikes Tibet, at least 16 killed - watch
text:
People run outside of buildings as earthquake strike China

At least 16 people were killed and 46 others injured after a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, in China’s Xizang region, at 10:33 pm on Thursday. According to the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the earthquake occured with its epicentre about 191 kilometres east-north-east of Nagqu. The area is sparsely populated and lies at a high altitude in northern Tibet. The USGS estimated the quake's depth at 18 kilometres below the Earth's surface.Nagqu lies more than 300 kilometres north of Lhasa, the capital of Tibet. Authorities have begun relief operations in the affected area, with emergency supplies reaching the quake-hit zone early Friday. China Xinhua News released a series of images on X showing the devastation caused by the earthquake. In X post, it wrote, "Relief materials allocated by authorities at various levels include 1,000 sets of prefabricated houses, more than 3,200 tents and over 2,800 folding beds. Essential supplies such as quilts, stoves and clothing are also being sent to support people affected by the earthquake."

End of Article

title: Elon Musk responds to statement that he may be in jail soon
text:
Elon Musk

Elon Musk has responded to a ‘warning’ by technology journalist and podcaster Kara Swisher, who recently said that the tech billionaire might be in jail right now if Kamala Harris was in office and “he knows what’s coming” if Democrats take back power”. “Message received,” the world’s richest person replied to a clip of the journalist arguing that probes into Elon Musk's businesses were paused under Trump but would resume if Democrats flip Congress in the 2026 midterms. . “If Donald Trump loses the House and the Senate, I would worry. I'd be worried if I were him,” Swisher said, adding that Musk may face scrutiny of the Congress soon. “Elon Musk is right up there for that. And so they're going to look at what he's done” she said, further stating that “He has a very big sense of fate and I think it's coming for him and real hard”.

Elon Musk responds to post saying he might be in jail soon

“Under Kamala Harris, he might be in jail right now, right?" Swisher said on The Bulwark. She argued that Musk "stopped like a half a dozen investigations of his various companies” and that "they're going to start investigating again." “He's under investigation by the Democrats and if Trump wins, he's out. He gets a get-out-of-jail-free card,” Swisher said. She also pointed at Musk's access to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) saying: “He got DOGE. He got all this access. Sounds like Swisher really wants to go to prison,” he said in another post.

Elon Musk’s political spending criticised by Bernie Sanders

In another X post, US Senator Bernie Sanders criticised Elon Musk for his political spending ahead of the 2026 mid term elections. “Musk's super PACs have now spent over $400 million to buy the midterm elections. This campaign is not just about Democrats vs. Republicans. It’s about whether the world’s first trillionaire can buy our government. Say NO to Musk. Say NO to oligarchy. Say yes to democracy,” Sanders wrote in the post.

title: Texas farmer went from 27 sheep to overseeing 10,000 across 40,000 acres
text:
When JR Howard considered selling his small flock of 27 sheep, he was struggling to make a living from farming in Texas. Today, he manages 10,000 sheep that graze across 40,000 acres of large solar farms throughout the state. The change began when a developer built a solar project near his property. Instead of seeing the energy project as a threat to farming, Howard secured a contract to let his sheep graze on the site and control plant growth. As reported by the San Antonio Express-News, that first deal gave him the income and opportunity he needed to grow his business into one of the largest solar grazing operations in North America. This approach, known as agrivoltaics or solar grazing, has become a practical business option for renewable energy companies and livestock farmers facing rising land costs and ongoing drought.

Scaling up vegetation control

Large solar farms need short grass and low plant cover to stop weeds and bushes from shading solar panels or creating fire risks. Traditional mowing can be expensive. It uses heavy machinery that burns diesel and can throw up rocks that damage costly equipment. According to reporting by the San Antonio Express-News, solar developers found that using sheep was a cheaper, lower-risk option than sending in crews with tractors and mowers. The animals can eat grass around narrow support structures and beneath low panel edges that ordinary mowing machines cannot easily reach. "We were struggling with cotton and dug ourselves a hole with it. We were digging out of it with sheep, but at a much slower rate than we are now thanks to solar grazing," Howard told Sheep Industry News. Through his company, Texas Solar Sheep, Howard provides flocks to control plant growth at several commercial solar sites. The business earns money in two ways. Energy companies pay for vegetation control, while livestock sales provide another source of income.

Commercial benefits for energy developers

For energy companies, using livestock at solar sites can lower long-term maintenance costs while also offering environmental benefits. According to a report by Canary Media on large solar projects in Texas, energy company Enel North America hired Howard to supply 6,000 sheep to graze across 10,000 acres of solar fields. Jesse Puckett, director of sustainability projects and community affairs at Enel North America, told Canary Media that the approach helps improve project profits while supporting the company's sustainability goals. "Ultimately, we're a business. This is one way that we can enhance the bottom line and build sustainability into our project," Puckett explained to Canary Media. He added that sheep can move around the complex layouts beneath solar panels without damaging the equipment. Along with cutting mowing costs, grazing can improve soil quality. Data collected by Enel from earlier solar grazing projects showed that soil organic matter increased by 200 per cent over time. This was due to natural fertilization fro

title: Red Corner Notice against Russian ‘who fled with child’
text:
The Delhi Police have issued a Red Corner Notice for Russian citizen Viktoriia Basu

NEW DELHI: Nearly a year after Russian national Viktoriia Basu allegedly left India with her minor son despite a Supreme Court-mandated shared custody arrangement, Delhi Police have secured an Interpol Red Corner Notice against her and initiated extradition proceedings through Russian authorities, according to a status report filed before a Delhi court. The Action Taken Report (ATR), submitted by Defence Colony police station before Judicial Magistrate Deepakshi Rana at Saket Courts, states that an extradition request has been forwarded to ministry of home affairs (MHA) for processing through ministry of external affairs (MEA) and Indian Embassy in Moscow. The Red Corner Notice has been issued to facilitate international tracking of Basu. The report also details the investigation into an alleged associate. According to T Jaiswal, counsel for complainant Saikat Basu, police have approached Yash Raj Films seeking details about co-accused Natasha, who is suspected of helping Viktoriia flee India. Her examination will be conducted after the company responds. Meanwhile, the investigating officer has sought additional time to file the final report, stating that documents submitted by the complainant are still under scrutiny. The case arises out of a custody dispute between Saikat Basu and Viktoriia, who moved to India in 2019 after their marriage. Following the breakdown of the marriage, Viktoriia approached Supreme Court in 2023 seeking full custody of their son, born on Oct 29, 2020. In May 2025, Supreme Court ordered a shared custody arrangement, extended Viktoriia’s visa and directed police to maintain vigilance at her residence. However, in July that year, Saikat informed the court that she had gone missing with the child, prompting a search operation and intervention by ministry of external affairs. An earlier status report had flagged discrepancies in travel records received from Nepal. According to those records, Viktoriia and the child entered Nepal through Birgunj on July 11, 2025, with Russia shown as their place of origin. Investigators, however, suspect they entered Nepal through a jungle route with the assistance of co-accused Samir Ansari. Russian authorities had earlier informed Delhi Police that the mother and child were “not traceable”. The latest ATR also records a separate complaint alleging that Viktoriia and her mother, Olga Zhigalina, left their home on March 13, 2023, leaving the child behind and exposing him to health risks through negligence. Police have sought additional time to complete the investigation.

End of Article

title: Will decide on any notice to remove CEC according to rules: LS Speaker Om Birla
text:
Om Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge.

NEW DELHI: Amid speculation that the opposition may make a fresh move for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Thursday said he would take a decision according to rules and procedures when he receives such a notice. Both the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha chairman had rejected previous notices from the opposition, saying their allegations “do not prima facie meet the high constitutional bar for removal proceedings”. Birla noted the process for removal of the chief election commissioner was the same as for removing a Supreme Court judge. Amid protests from the opposition and activist groups, Birla also emphasised India’s democratic strength, saying democracy was ingrained in the country’s fabric. “Whatever happens in the world has an impact in India. It will be our effort that the world benefits from our system of dialogue and free speech,” he said ahead of India hosting the 12th Brics parliamentary forum on Oct 26-27. PM Modi will interact with the delegates at the event.

The Speaker had no role in this, he added. title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags vulnerabilities
text:
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a criticalseverity warning. (Reuters photo)

BENGALURU: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems. In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.

CERT-In Flags Vulnerabilities

Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them. Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations. The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems. Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security.

End of Article

title: California family spent $4,000 turning its front yard into Jurassic Park
text:
A family in Granada Hills, California, has spent about $4,000 (£3,080) and more than 200 hours building a huge Jurassic Park display in their front yard. The attraction features 13-foot entrance gates and a timed dinosaur escape show that is free for the public to watch. Rob and Kel Warner turned their suburban property into a detailed tribute to the 1993 Steven Spielberg film. According to an exclusive report by People magazine, the couple built tall wooden entrance gates that stand higher than their single-storey home. The gates serve as the main entrance for neighbourhood trick-or-treaters and visiting fans of the film. The display includes custom-made moving dinosaur models, themed lighting, artificial fog, music from the film, and several life-sized dinosaur figures spread across the lawn.

Custom gates and mechanics

The project took months of hard work, planning, and testing. According to details the family shared with People magazine, they spent around $4,000 in total. This covered raw timber, the internal frames, special electronic controllers, and strong weatherproofing materials to protect the display from the elements. To recreate the film's famous entrance, Rob Warner designed and built wooden pillars and hanging gates that stand 13 feet tall. The structure needed reinforced ground anchors to support its weight and keep the gates steady during strong winds. Behind the gates, the front lawn features fake electric fencing, emergency warning lights, and tropical plants. These details are designed to recreate Isla Nublar, the fictional island resort and research centre in the film.

Automated dinosaur escape show

The main attraction is a regular automated show that recreates a dinosaur escape. Visitors gather along the pavement to watch a planned light and sound performance. Warning sirens flash and beep, red emergency lights brighten the lawn, and life-sized dinosaurs appear to break free from their enclosures. The show uses audio and visual equipment hidden in the garden. Custom timers and relays control the sequence. They switch floodlights on and off, play recorded dialogue from the film, and trigger mechanical movements in the dinosaur models. This allows the show to run without the owners having to operate everything by hand. Kel Warner shares themed design projects and family outings on social media under the name @themeparkmomlife. She told People magazine that the family wanted to give local residents an immersive theme park experience without charging an entrance fee.

Community reception and family tradition

The family began planning the project early in the year, with construction picking up over several months. Together, they spent more than 200 hours designing, building, and testing the mechanical features. Most of the work took place in the evenings and at weekends around their regular schedules. For the Warner family, creating large seasonal displays has become an annual community tradition. Neighbours and local visitor

title: Jason Momoa buys Sam Neill's former 4.92-hectare NZ estate for NZ$15m
text:
Hollywood actor Jason Momoa has expanded his presence in New Zealand by buying a 4.92-hectare lifestyle property in Queenstown for NZ$15 million (£7.1 million). The property is in the rural area of Dalefield. It once belonged to the late actor Sir Sam Neill before being passed on to his former wife. According to property records reported by real estate website OneRoof, the sale price was NZ$3.5 million above the property's official rating valuation. It was also the second-highest residential sale recorded in the Queenstown-Lakes district this year. Momoa officially took ownership of the large estate after spending several months looking for a permanent home in Central Otago. He has visited the region many times for both work and leisure.

Premium price in a tight market

The multi-million-dollar sale highlights the strength of the high-end property market in Queenstown-Lakes. While property values have slowed in other parts of New Zealand, local data analyzed by OneRoof shows that average property values in the district have risen by more than NZ$300,000 over the past three years. The regional average is now close to NZ$2.2 million. Market experts say prices remain high because the region has limited space for new development, with mountains restricting the amount of available land. Steady interest from overseas buyers has also helped keep prices strong. Mark Harris, managing director of New Zealand Sotheby's International Realty, told OneRoof that wealthy buyers from overseas, especially from the United States and Australia, continue to show strong interest in the region. "Celebrities are in that category as well. There's a wealth tax proposed for California, and that's playing on people's minds, but I think it's largely the privacy, the space and the raw beauty of New Zealand that attracts them," Harris explained to OneRoof. Recent changes to New Zealand's Active Investor Plus visa rules have also made it easier for foreign nationals to buy high-end residential properties. This has renewed interest among international buyers looking for private retreats.

Deep ties to New Zealand

Momoa is best known for playing Aquaman in the DC Extended Universe and appearing in the Game of Thrones series. He has spoken publicly about his strong personal connection to New Zealand. "I came here when I was about 20 years old, and when I landed there, Hawaii is home, but there's never been anywhere in the world where I've ever felt more connected," Momoa told the New Zealand Herald during a recent interview. "I can't really explain it. If it was my destiny, my ancestors ... don't know what it was, but the moment I stepped off that plane I felt it, and I've always been drawn to it." Along with buying property, the actor has expanded his business investments in New Zealand. title: After renaming Lake Ontario, Google CEO rejects US request to rename Atlantic Ocean
text:
Trump said he called Google to rename 'Atlantic Ocean' to 'Trump Ocean'

President Trump, who floated the idea of renaming ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’ earlier this month, has once again raised the possibility of renaming the ocean. Speaking at an event recently, Trump revealed that he called Google Maps and asked to rename the Atlantic Ocean. He said that Google CEO Sundar Pichai replied to his proposal saying: “No, no, no. This time I'm not doing it.” According to Trump, Pichai said, “Oceans are different, sir. They cover a lot of countries. Please don't ask us to do that.” This comes months after Google renamed 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' in the US following an executive order signed by Trump.

Trump wants to rename ‘Atlantic Ocean’ to ‘Trump Ocean’

As mentioned above, Trump first discussed renaming the Atlantic Ocean this month. “We’ve got the gulf. We’ve got a beautiful lake,” Trump said during a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee. “Now, somebody said, you need a river. We need a river. We need an ocean.” He jokingly said that the new name could be in honor of him. “We call it ‘Trump Ocean’ or ‘Ocean of the Americas,’ something like that,” Trump said further adding “Before I get out, I think we should have an ocean. And we need a great river.”

US previously renamed Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario

Earlier this month, the US administration renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America, sparking diplomatic tensions between the US and Mexico. In August, Trump also renamed Lake Ontario, between New York and Canada, as “Lake America”. After an executive order, Google posted a brief update on its Google Maps blog, noting that it follows the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for its maps. This primarily means that the company has to rename Lake Ontario in Google Maps. Google's update on the name change also made it clear that the change will be only for Google Map users in the US. According to Google, those in the US will only see the new name, which is 'Lake of America'. Meanwhile, Canadians will continue to see the 'Lake Ontario' label. In the rest of the world, Lake Ontario will take precedence, but Lake America will also be there in parentheses. Apple followed the suit renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America on Maps for US users.

title: Virginia teen's model improves simulated earthquake sensor coverage by 16.7%
text:
Isabel enjoys working through equations and mathematical proofs in her spare time (Photo: Society for science)

A 14-year-old student from Williamsburg, Virginia, has earned her a place among 30 finalists in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge for finding a new way to position earthquake sensors. Earthquake sensors can help detect seismic activity and provide early warnings, but deciding where to install them is not easy. Scientists must consider how accurately the devices can detect earthquakes, how much ground they can cover and whether their locations are accessible. According to The Virginian Pilot, Isabel Rossi, who carried out the research as an eighth-grader, developed a computer-based model that showed a possible 16.7% improvement in earthquake detection coverage using just five additional sensors. The finding emerged from a six-month project in which Isabel examined whether mathematical methods commonly used to make decisions could help identify better locations for earthquake sensors. For this, she worked with existing earthquake records and computer-generated sensor arrangements. Nearly 10,000 students applied to the national competition, which recognises research projects completed by middle school students across the United States. Isabel developed her project independently while attending James Blair Middle School. She is currently a freshman at Jamestown High School. According to Society for Science, which organises the challenge, Isabel's project, titled Listening in the Right Places: Game Theory and Optimisation for Earthquake Sensor Placement, was based on simulations.

Importance of choosing sensor locations

Earthquake monitoring depends on instruments that record seismic waves travelling through the ground. Some of these waves can be detected before stronger shaking reaches an area, allowing early warning systems to issue alerts. However, the usefulness of a sensor network also depends on where its instruments are located. For her study, Isabel concentrated on the Los Angeles region of California. She accessed a data library containing information about previous earthquakes and the locations of existing sensors. This allowed her to examine different arrangements without physically moving or installing any equipment. She wrote a computer program that generated random sets of possible sensor locations. Each arrangement was then assessed using two mathematical methods: a weighted sum model and Nash bargaining. The weighted sum model evaluates several objectives by assigning different levels of importance to them. Nash bargaining, a concept associated with game theory, looks for solutions that balance competing interests. Isabel used these approaches to examine the relationship between earthquake detection accuracy and sensor accessibility. title: Hospitals ‘overcharging’ is a malpractice: Govt to Supreme Court
text:
Hosps charge up to 700% premium on cancer drugs (Generative image)

NEW DELHI: Govt has admitted before Supreme Court the “malpractice” of hospitals charging patients high MRPs for medicines and consumables, and said it was conscious of the problem, examining it and devising appropriate interventions in consultation with all stakeholders. In an affidavit filed in SC on the issue of capping prices of all medicines and medical consumables, chemicals and fertilisers ministry said that patients have a very low bargaining position with respect to hospitals, resulting in various malpractices. The affidavit noted the irony of India being home to companies making cheap drugs but patients here having to pay way above the manufacturing price, as well as patients being subjected to overcharging by hospitals. “The Indian drug market is fairly competitive, with a large number of pharmaceutical companies in every drug segment, resulting in one of the lowest prices in the world. Ordinarily, where there is substantial competition, there is no need to regulate prices. However, by their very nature, health treatment and pharmaceutical products involve information and bargaining asymmetries between patients on the one hand, and retail pharmacies, hospital pharmacies, hospitals providing treatment and doctors on the other,” the affidavit said.

Hospitals charge up to 700% premium on cancer drugs

The govt affidavit said a patient has a “very low bargaining position vis-a-vis the hospital, and the patient’s knowledge of drugs, their substitutes and their prices is also very limited”. These bargaining and information asymmetries result in various malpractices in the system despite strong competition among manufacturers, leading to the need for regulation, it said. Enumerating the steps taken by it to control the pricing of drugs, govt said ceiling prices for 935 scheduled formulations and retail prices of 3,881 new drugs have been fixed. Govt filed the affidavit on a plea filed by Dr Sanjay Kulshrestha, who referred to a Niti Aayog report and a 2020 statement of the then health minister Harsh Vardhan that expenditure on health pushed an estimated six crore families below the poverty line each year.

title: Amid attacks, sales surge at Kolkata Left bookstalls
text:
Book stalls set up by Left parties saw significant sales increases during Durga Puja amid incidents of vandalism.

KOLKATA: Book sales at stalls set up near Durga Puja pandals by various Left parties—including the CPM, CPI(ML) Liberation, and SUCI—spiked manifold this year, coinciding with reports of vandalism, arson, and books being thrown onto the streets across the city and the state. At the Jadavpur 8B bus stand, where a bulldozer attempted to demolish book stalls on Saturday before facing resistance from locals, the CPM stall recorded sales worth Rs 16 lakh—a nearly fourfold increase from last year’s Rs 4.5 lakh. Meanwhile, the stall set up by the All India Students’ Association (AISA) at the same location recorded sales of Rs 80,000, up from Rs 50,000 last year, according to AISA state president Ritam Maji. The only total casualty was the SUCI (Communist) stall, which was pulled down around midnight. However, its sales still surged after volunteers resumed operations using makeshift tables and chairs. The Jadavpur SUCI stall sold books worth Rs 75,000, compared to Rs 55,000 in 2025. The APDR moved the Calcutta High Court on Thursday against the demolition of a book stall near Jadavpur Super Market, demanding accountability and compensation; the matter will be heard on October 29. CPI(ML) Liberation was not allowed to set up its stall at Dhakuria. However, party sources said books worth Rs 25,000 were sold from its Moulali stall—almost double last year’s figures. CPM state committee member Sudip Sengupta said: “Despite the attacks on bookstalls, we have noticed a surge in sales. Apart from the Jadavpur 8B bus stand stall, our stall at Bagbazar Sarbajonin also received a great response, generating Rs 4.5 lakh this year compared to around Rs 1.5 lakh last year. At Bijoygarh, books worth Rs 1.3 lakh were sold, while our Netaji Nagar stall generated Rs 2.2 lakh.” Kallol Majumdar, CPM Kolkata district secretary, said that out of 119 bookstalls set up by the CPM in Kolkata this Puja, over 30 faced disruptions or were vandalised. Stalls were attacked in Rashbehari, Lake Market, Behala, Haridevpur, Nagerbazar, Boral, Howrah, and Siliguri, among other places, he added. A video from Nagerbazar went viral on social media showing right-wing supporters vandalising a CPM stall and throwing books—including Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay’s Pather Dabi—onto the ground. Seventy-three-year-old Bipul Dasgupta, a CPM whole-timer, was seen urging the youths to flip through the pages before discarding them, but his pleas fell on deaf ears. SUCI (Communist) state secretary Chandidas Bhattacharya said: “Despite attacks on hundreds of stalls across districts, overall sales have increased by 40% to 50% compared to last year.” Senior BJP and RSS leaders have also spoken out against damaging books. BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said no genuine party worker could carry out such an act, emphasizing that the vandalism of Left bookstalls cannot be supported under any

title: Anahat scripts history, storms into maiden PSA Gold semi-final
text:
India's Anahat Singh (ANI Photo)

Indian squash sensation Anahat Singh continued her giant-killing run at the Silicon Valley Open 2026, producing a remarkable comeback to defeat Egypt's Salma Hany in a five-game thriller and book her maiden semi-final berth at a PSA Gold-level event. The 18-year-old World No. 15 recovered from a 1-2 deficit to register a 4-11, 11-8, 4-11, 11-2, 11-5 victory over the sixth-seeded Egyptian in 42 minutes in Redwood City, California. Anahat showed tremendous resilience after twice falling behind in the contest, raising her level in the final two games to complete an impressive turnaround. Having conceded the opening and third games, the Indian dominated the closing stages, dropping just seven points across the last two games to seal a landmark win. The victory marks another significant milestone in Anahat's burgeoning career and comes on the back of her stunning second-round upset of eight-time world champion and World No. 3 Nour ElSherbini.

Anahat rallies from behind to seal historic victory

Hany made a strong start, capitalising on Anahat's errors to take the opening game 11-4. The Indian responded with an improved performance in the second, winning it 11-8 to restore parity. However, the Egyptian regained control in the third game, cruising to another 11-4 win to move within a game of victory. With her quarter-final hopes hanging in the balance, Anahat produced a superb response, stepping up her intensity to dismantle Hany 11-2 in the fourth game. The teenager carried that momentum into the decider, maintaining her composure and dictating the rallies to close out the contest 11-5. Her emphatic finish underlined her ability to respond under pressure against an experienced opponent. The win ensures Anahat reaches the last four of a PSA Gold event for the first time in her career, further strengthening her growing reputation on the international squash circuit.

Asian Games final rematch awaits Anahat in semi-finals

Anahat's reward for the hard-fought quarter-final victory is a semi-final showdown against Malaysia's World No. 4 Sivasangari Subramaniam, who booked her place in the last four with a straight-games win over compatriot Rachel Arnold.

title: Centre betrayed us, now want full statehood for Ladakh: Sonam Wangchuk
text:
Sonam Wangchuk alleged that decisions were being taken unilaterally by the Ladakh administration (LG)

NEW DELHI/SRINAGAR: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk accused Centre of backtracking on an understanding reached with Ladakh groups in May 2026, including on a UT-level elected body, calling the failure to hold talks in Delhi on Thursday “yet another betrayal of trust”. “The govt had said Ladakh lacked resources for full statehood. We asked for a UT with a legislature and safeguards under Article 371. Govt agreed at the May 22 meeting, but now says there will be neither statehood nor a legislature. Instead, it is talking about a small council, which is shameful and undignified for Ladakh,” he said.

title: Will back all meaningful efforts for Ukraine peace, PM Modi assures Poland's Tusk
text:
PM Modi with Polish counterpart Donald Tusk at Hyderabad House Thursday.

NEW DELHI: Looking to further expand their strategic partnership, India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030 and announced dialogue mechanisms for defence industrial collaboration and counterterrorism cooperation as PM Narendra Modi hosted his counterpart Donald Tusk for talks Thursday. Modi and Tusk expressed deepest concern in a joint statement over the war in Ukraine, including its tragic humanitarian consequences and the impact on Global South. In his media statement, Modi assured Tusk that whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India will continue to support every meaningful effort for peace. Poland views the war in Ukraine as a direct threat to its national security and sovereignty due to its shared border, influx of refugees and the threat of future Russian aggression in eastern Europe. “They reiterated the need for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in line with international law, consistent with the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity,” said the joint statement. The leaders also noted the negative impacts of the war on global food and energy security, especially for the Global South. Modi and Tusk, the first Polish PM to visit India in 16 years, also backed an MoU under negotiation for cooperation in critical minerals. Modi said the friendship between India and Poland was based not only on diplomatic ties but also on a shared heritage of humanity and empathy. He recalled how, during the Second World War, the royal families of Jamnagar and Kolhapur had provided shelter in India to thousands of Polish children and families. He also thanked Poland for helping India evacuate Indian students from Ukraine shortly after the Russia-Ukraine war began in 2022. Modi said the world was passing through a period of uncertainty and change, and even in such times, both India and Poland were emerging as important hubs of growth, technology and innovation. “Today we have agreed to deepen ties in defence, space and nuclear energy. In all these strategic sectors, we invite Polish companies to engage in co-development and co-production with India,” he said. He also announced a startup bridge to facilitate cooperation in IT, Artificial Intelligence and critical technologies. “Both India and Poland believe in democratic values and the rule of law,” Modi said, underlining that both sides considered reforms essential to make global governance institutions more empowered. The two countries agreed that the UN needed structural reforms, including expansion of UNSC in both permanent and non-permanent categories, to remain relevant, credible and effective. In the joint statement, Poland expressed support for India’s membership of a more inclusive, reformed and expanded UNSC, as well as its candidature for a non-permanent seat on the council for 2028-29.
